```ts
// ctx.body is the RAW input: before-hooks run before better-auth validates the body (§11.3) [R1:BA-r1-08]
type AfterAuthMethod<P extends string> = (
  ctx: AuthAfterHookContext<P>,
) => unknown | Promise<unknown>;
// after:  undefined (keep) | value (replaces ctx.context.returned) | throw APIError (replaces the response)
type DatabaseHookMethod<
  E extends DatabaseHookTarget,
  Ph extends "before" | "after",
> = (
  data: DatabaseHookData<E, Ph>,
  ctx: GenericEndpointContext | null,
) => DatabaseHookResult<E, Ph> | Promise<DatabaseHookResult<E, Ph>>;
// create.before: void | false | { data } (merged; the next hook sees the merge)
// update.before: void | false | { data } (merged into the update; every hook sees the ORIGINAL payload)
// delete.before: void | false (returned data is ignored by better-auth, so it is not allowed by the type)
// *.after:       void
```

Registration is discovery (§10.3). A package only has to be imported. Hooks from independent packages are additive; where order matters, `order` settles it.

#### 4.5.2 Third-party sketch: an audit-log package

```ts
@Injectable()
export class AuditHooks {
  constructor(@Inject(AuditSink) private readonly sink: AuditSink) {}

  @AfterAuth(["/sign-in/email", "/sign-in/social", "/callback/:id"], {
    calls: "http",
  })
  async signedIn(
    ctx: AuthAfterHookContext<
      "/sign-in/email" | "/sign-in/social" | "/callback/:id"
    >,
  ) {
    if (ctx.context.newSession)
      await this.sink.write("sign-in", ctx.context.newSession.user.id);
  }

  @BeforeDatabase("user.delete")
  async beforeUserDelete(user: DatabaseHookData<"user.delete", "before">) {
    await this.sink.write("user-delete-requested", user.id); // return false here would abort the delete
  }
}
@Module({ providers: [AuditHooks, AuditSink], exports: [AuditSink] })
export class AuditModule {} // importing it is the whole integration
```

### 4.6 Auxiliary extension: `http.around` `[A][B][C]`

Raw auth routes bypass Nest interceptors by design. The reference library grew a `middleware` option for ORM request contexts and tracing (`REF/src/auth-module-definition.ts:35-41`). `http.around` is the typed, platform-neutral replacement: a runtime option whose functions receive the Web `Request` and may replace it or short-circuit with a `Response`:

```ts
BetterAuthModule.forRootAsync({
  platforms: [expressPlatform()],
  inject: [MikroORM],
  useFactory: (orm: MikroORM) => ({
    auth,
    http: {
      around: [(call, next) => RequestContext.create(orm.em, () => next())],
    },
  }),
});
```

Interceptors must not log `Cookie` or `Set-Cookie` values. A conformance case checks that the kit's probe cookies never appear in captured logs `[B]`.

## 5. Module configuration

### 5.1 Registration API

`BetterAuthModule` is hand-written; it does not use `ConfigurableModuleBuilder` `[A][B][C]`. Builder extras reach only the transform callback and never a provider. They leak into the options value when their defaults object is empty. An explicit `undefined` overrides a default. Those traps caused reference issues #59, #88 and #159 (R:nest-di §1.2–1.3). The name `BetterAuthModule` avoids colliding with the `AuthModule` most applications already have, and `BetterAuthGuard` avoids `@nestjs/passport`'s `AuthGuard` `[A][B]` (ADR-24).

Three supported shapes, simplest first:

```ts
// (1) Static instance (recommended: the better-auth CLI can load auth.ts; R:ref-issues §3.19)
BetterAuthModule.forRoot({
  auth, // runtime
  platforms: [expressPlatform()], // app-level static (default instance only)
  transports: [apolloTransport(), socketIoTransport()], // app-level static (default instance only)
  principals: [apiKeyPrincipal()], // instance static (tried before the session where a route accepts 'api-key')
});

// (2) Static instance, runtime knobs from configuration
BetterAuthModule.forRootAsync({
  platforms: [fastifyPlatform()],
  transports: [mercuriusTransport()],
  imports: [ConfigModule],
  inject: [ConfigService],
  useFactory: (config: ConfigService) => ({
    auth,
    http: { bodyLimit: config.get("AUTH_BODY_LIMIT") ?? "1mb" },
    defaultAccess: config.get("AUTH_DEFAULT_ACCESS") ?? "authenticated",
  }),
});

// (3) Instance built from DI (e.g. a Prisma client); types via the factory's return type (no shadow instance, #62/#112)
// auth.ts
export const createAuth = (prisma: PrismaClient) =>
  betterAuth({
    database: prismaAdapter(prisma, { provider: "postgresql" }),
    plugins: [admin(), nestjs()],
  });
declare module "nestjs-slightly-better-auth" {
  interface Register {
    auth: ReturnType<typeof createAuth>;
  }
}
// auth.cli.ts (for the better-auth CLI only): export const auth = createAuth(new PrismaClient());
// app.module.ts
BetterAuthModule.forRootAsync({
  platforms: [expressPlatform()],
  imports: [PrismaModule],
  inject: [PrismaService],
  useFactory: (prisma: PrismaService) => ({ auth: createAuth(prisma) }),
});
```

Shape (3) with an asynchronously initialized dependency is safe under both bootstraps: platform preparation waits for whichever of "adapter known" and "platforms registered" happens last (§5.7, LEAD-EXP-3) `[R1:NEST-r1-03]`.

### 5.2 Static vs runtime options

| Kind                                                                 | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Why                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **App-level static** (`BetterAuthAppOptions`, default instance only) | `platforms`, `transports`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | One HTTP adapter and one transport registry per app. Declaring them once removes merge ambiguity; the named-instance overloads reject them at compile time and B25 at runtime `[R1:NEST-r1-09]`. |
| **Instance static** (`BetterAuthStaticOptions`)                      | `name`, `isGlobal`, `globalGuard`, `principals`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Each decides which providers, enhancers or exports exist. Nest fixes that when the dynamic module is created. Extensions may be DI classes, which must become providers.                         |
| **Runtime** (`BetterAuthRuntimeOptions`)                             | `auth`, `defaultAccess`, `defaultRequirements`, `session`, `http.{mount, bodyLimit, around, allowRootMount, allowRequestDerivedBaseURL, diagnostics}`, `cookies.forwardDirectCalls`, `originCheck.{mode, missingOrigin}`, `errors.{map, exposeRawCause}`, `limits.maxAuthorizationCallsPerRequest` `[R3:SEC-r3-08]`, `logSummary` | Read by providers after DI resolution, so they may come from `useFactory`.                                                                                                                       |

The split is enforced twice `[C]`:

1. **At compile time.** `useFactory` must return `BetterAuthFactoryResult<A>`, which maps every static and app-level key to `StaticOptionMustBePassedToForRootAsync<K>`. Returning `{ auth, globalGuard: false }` fails with `Type 'boolean' is not assignable to type 'StaticOptionMustBePassedToForRootAsync<"globalGuard">'` (EXP-C9).
2. **At runtime.** The options provider rejects static keys found in a factory result with `BetterAuthConfigurationError: 'globalGuard' was returned from useFactory; pass it to BetterAuthModule.forRootAsync({ globalGuard, useFactory })`. This covers JavaScript users and `any`.

Toggles users commonly want to drive from configuration are runtime options, so they never hit this wall. Making a whole app public is `defaultAccess: 'public'`, not "remove the guard". Behavior that depends on runtime options is decided at runtime by always-registered providers, following the nestjs-cls pattern (R:nest-di §1.4). For example, the built-in session source is always registered, and `session: false` removes it from the chain when the options resolve.

### 5.3 How the typed instance flows `[A][C]`

```
auth.ts ──typeof auth──► Register augmentation ──► RegisteredAuth / AuthOf<N>
                                                     ├─► AuthSession<N> / AuthUser<N> / AuthPrincipal
                                                     ├─► BetterAuthService (default generic)         [DI: class / BETTER_AUTH_SERVICE]
                                                     ├─► AdminPermissions / OrgPermissions           [decorator arguments]
                                                     ├─► EndpointPath / AuthHookContext<P>           [hook decorators]
                                                     ├─► DatabaseHookData<E, Ph>                     [from BetterAuthOptions['databaseHooks']]
                                                     └─► forRoot<A> check: A must be RegisteredAuth for the default instance
forRoot({ auth }) ──infers A──► SessionOption<A> (customSession ⇒ session.userId mapper required)
```

1. `forRoot<A>` infers `A` from `auth`. It gives completion for `session.userId(s: SessionOf<A>)`. When the program has registered an instance, the default-instance overload also requires `A extends RegisteredAuth` (EXP-C2 case 9).
2. For non-generic injection sites and decorators, the user registers the type once with `interface Register { auth: typeof auth }`. Named instances go under `instances: { admin: typeof adminAuth }`.
3. At runtime, `InjectAuth()` resolves `getAuthToken('instance')` to the exact object the user passed, with no wrapper and no proxy. No runtime code reads `$Infer`.
4. Our declarations contain only conditional types over `Register`, evaluated in the user's program. Nothing deeply inferred from better-auth is emitted (§11.7).

### 5.4 Bootstrap validation (fail fast)

All checks run in `onModuleInit` of the internal core module. Nest orders lifecycle hooks by module distance, and every global module has the same distance, so they run in insertion order (LEAD-V27). The core module therefore runs before non-global user modules' hooks. It does **not** necessarily run before another global module imported ahead of `BetterAuthModule`. Code that seeds data through `auth.api` belongs in `onApplicationBootstrap`, and B26 reports better-auth calls that ran before Nest hooks were bound `[R1:NEST-r1-11]`. The core module's lifecycle work runs once per application: `NestMicroservice.init()` calls `onModuleInit` and `onApplicationBootstrap` twice (REV2-NEST:`exp4b-double-init.mjs`), and a repeated call returns at once, while a second application on the same container, after the first shut down, starts clean or fails with `APP_ADAPTER_CHANGED` (§5.7) `[R2:NEST-r2-05]` `[R3:NEST-r3-03]`. Errors are **aggregated** `[C]`: one boot reports every problem found, each as a `BetterAuthConfigurationError` with a stable `code` and a copy-paste `hint`. Rows marked _warn_ or _info_ log instead of throwing. The numbers are identifiers, not an execution order: several checks validate the result of a boot step (hook discovery, binding, mount resolution) and run right after it, as §5.7 step 2 lists.

**"In production"** in the rows below, in `BootAdviceContext.production` and in every runtime default keyed on it (404 diagnostics, `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED`) means: `NODE_ENV` is **not** `development`, `dev` or `test`. An unset `NODE_ENV` counts as production, and so does `staging`. v3 keyed these checks on `NODE_ENV === 'production'`, so a container that never set `NODE_ENV` silenced B23 exactly in the misconfiguration it exists for, together with every production warning (REV3-SEC, SEC-r3-07). Development needs one variable (`NODE_ENV=development`), which better-auth's own docs already ask for. `TEST` does not make a process non-production here, so a stray `TEST=true` in a deployed image cannot silence these checks; its effect on better-auth's origin checks is reported by B19. The boot summary prints the assumed mode and why (`environment: production (NODE_ENV unset)`) `[R3:SEC-r3-07]`. This definition is the library's, not better-auth's: better-auth keys its own production defaults on `NODE_ENV === 'production'`, the default secret check and **the rate limiter** among them (LEAD-V48, LEAD-V52). In a deployment this library treats as production without `NODE_ENV=production`, better-auth's rate limiter is off unless `rateLimit.enabled` is set, which B30 reports and which the IP-related rows (B18, B27, `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED`) take into account `[R4:BA-r4-02]`.

| B16 | **Coverage**, one core rule over the claims every transport's `validate()` makes (§4.2.1) `[R1:NEST-r1-05, NEST-r1-06, NEST-r1-13]` `[R2:NEST-r2-02, NEST-r2-11, NEST-r2-12, SEC-r2-08]` `[R3:NEST-r3-02, NEST-r3-05, NEST-r3-07, NEST-r3-08]` `[R4:NEST-r4-02, NEST-r4-01]`:<br>• a handler **declares something** (the one definition; §9.1, ADR-40, §15.1 step 7 and `T-coverage-claims` refer to it) when `plan.declares` is true: its method-level metadata, or its class-chain metadata unless a transport nests the handler (§7.6 step 3), carries `@RequireAuth()`, `@OptionalAuth()`, `@AcceptPrincipals`, a requirement, or a principal or invocation param decorator, or its plan forwards direct calls (`@ForwardAuthCookies()` or `cookies.forwardDirectCalls`). Other instance-wide defaults do not count: `defaultAccess`, the default kinds and `defaultRequirements` say what the guard does where it runs, not where it must run, so under `globalGuard: false` an undecorated route stays the app's choice even with `defaultRequirements` set. Forwarding counts from either source, because it sets auth cookies, and only the guard runs the form-CSRF check that protects that (§7.10);<br>• a claimed handler is covered when its effective access is `inherit`, or `public` with an origin check other than `'form'`; or its reach is `'global'` and the application's global enhancers include **both** `BetterAuthGuard` and `BetterAuthScopeInterceptor`, whoever registered them; or `@UseBetterAuth()` (or both `@UseGuards(BetterAuthGuard)` and `@UseInterceptors(BetterAuthScopeInterceptor)`) applies at class or method level. Global enhancers are read at `onModuleInit` from `ApplicationConfig.getGlobalGuards()` and `getGlobalInterceptors()` (the request-scoped lists included). An entry is `BetterAuthGuard` when it is **identical** to `moduleRef.get(BetterAuthGuard, { strict: false })`, the instance the class token currently resolves to, so `overrideProvider(BetterAuthGuard).useValue(…)`/`.useClass(…)` and `overrideAuthGuard()` stand-ins count; the interceptor likewise. The `Symbol.for` brand is only the fallback for an enhancer registered from the other package copy, whose class token differs. v4 recognized the brand alone, so the standard Nest guard override put an unbranded object into the global list and failed boot with `ROUTE_UNGUARDED` although `globalGuard` was true (NEST-r4-02, which broke NEST-r1-08's fix again). v3 counted only a `forRoot` with `globalGuard: true`, so an app that registered `{ provide: APP_GUARD, useExisting: BetterAuthGuard }` itself, to order its own guards, failed boot (NEST-r3-02). A user guard that merely delegates to `BetterAuthGuard` is neither identical nor branded and does not count. A `public` plan in `'form'` mode (a `@ForwardAuthCookies()` login proxy) is not covered by its access, because its check runs in the guard (§7.1). Reach `'none'` is never covered otherwise;<br>• an uncovered claim is reported with the transport's code and hint, at its `coverage` severity, when the claim says `everyHandler` or the handler declares something;<br>• library metadata that no transport claims fails with `UNGUARDED_AUTH_METADATA`, naming the registered transport ids (a transport is missing, e.g. `socketIoTransport()` on Nest 11 or `rpcTransport()` in a hybrid app). It fires for a scanned method that no transport claims, or a scanned class none of whose methods any transport claims, whose own metadata includes one of: `@RequireAuth()`, `@OptionalAuth()`, `@AcceptPrincipals`, a requirement, a principal or invocation param decorator, `@ForwardAuthCookies()`, `@UseAuthInstance()`, `@UseBetterAuth()`. It never fires for `@Public()`, `@SkipOriginCheck()`, `@SkipDefaultRequirements()` or the hook and database-hook decorators, which mark hook providers, not handlers; v3's wording ("library metadata other than `@Public()` and `@SkipOriginCheck()`") caught every hook provider (NEST-r3-07). Helper methods of a claimed controller are not reported;<br>• **canaries**: before a transport, or this rule, relies on a Nest-owned metadata literal (§12.4), it applies the real Nest decorator to a private probe class and reads the literal back. A mismatch fails boot with `NEST_METADATA_KEY_CHANGED`, naming the unit and the literal, so a renamed key can neither hide handlers nor pass a claim vacuously on the installed Nest (NEST-r3-08) | [C] [R1] [R2] [R3] [R4]       | transport-supplied (`ROUTE_UNGUARDED`, `GATEWAY_UNGUARDED`, `RPC_HANDLER_UNGUARDED`, `FIELD_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`, `REFERENCE_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`, and the GraphQL units' prerequisites `GRAPHQL_DRIVER_MISMATCH`, `GRAPHQL_STATIC_CONTEXT`, `FEDERATION_FIELD_GUARDS_REQUIRED`, §9.2); core `UNGUARDED_AUTH_METADATA`, `NEST_METADATA_KEY_CHANGED` |

```
[BetterAuth] 'default': mounted at /api/auth (all methods, body limit 1 MiB) on fastify (trust proxy: partial "1"),
             outside global prefix '/v1'; transports: apollo, http; principals: better-auth:api-key (explicit) → better-auth:session (default);
             hooks: 3 before, 1 after, 2 database; default access: authenticated; handlers: 42 (3 public, 1 optional, 5 inherit, 2 skip defaults);
             origin check: cookie/reject; direct-call cookies: opt-in; client IP: platform (random header per plugin instance);
             environment: production (NODE_ENV unset); rate limit: on (rateLimit.enabled: true); global guards: ThrottlerGuard → BetterAuthGuard
```

Plans for B14–B16 are compiled by scanning every controller and every provider's methods with `DiscoveryService` and `MetadataScanner`, one plan per (class, method), so two subclasses that inherit one handler function get two plans (§7.6). Policy references are resolved first (B14), because plans read `requires` from the resolved instances `[R3:NEST-r3-04]`. The scan is full, skips alias wrappers, and reads only our own `Symbol.for` metadata keys; transports read the Nest-owned keys they document when they claim handlers (§9), after a canary has confirmed each key on the installed Nest (B16). Handlers in lazily loaded modules are compiled on first use with the same checks. A failure there surfaces as a 500 `AUTH_MISCONFIGURED` response (generic on GraphQL) plus an error log, never as a silent allow `[C]`.

### 5.5 Multiple instances `[A][C]`

The stance is one default instance per app, plus any number of **named** instances with explicit routing. Dynamically swappable instances are not supported (§17 Q10).

```ts
// auth.ts: distinct cookie prefixes, or the two instances overwrite and clear each other's cookies (B24)
export const auth = betterAuth({ /* … */ plugins: [organization(), nestjs()] });
export const adminAuth = betterAuth({
  /* … */ advanced: { cookiePrefix: "admin-auth" },
  basePath: "/api/admin-auth",
  plugins: [admin(), nestjs()],
});

@Module({
  imports: [
    BetterAuthModule.forRoot({ auth, platforms: [expressPlatform()] }), // 'default': app-level platforms/transports, global guard
    BetterAuthModule.forRoot({ name: "admin", auth: adminAuth }), // globalGuard: false by default; no platforms here
  ],
})
export class AppModule {}

@UseAuthInstance("admin") // the (single) guard evaluates this controller against 'admin'
@Controller("admin")
export class AdminController {
  constructor(
    @InjectBetterAuthService("admin")
    private readonly admin: BetterAuthService<AuthOf<"admin">>,
  ) {}
  @Get("me") me(@CurrentSession() s: AuthSession<"admin">) {
    return s.user;
  } // the plan's instance: 'admin'
}
// types: declare module '…' { interface Register { auth: typeof auth; instances: { admin: typeof adminAuth } } }
```

- Each instance has its own tokens (`getAuthToken(kind, name)`), its own `nestjs()` plugin binding, and its own mount path from its own `$context`. Mounts must not overlap (B10), and cookie names must not collide (B24) `[R1:SEC-r1-11]`. Each `betterAuth()` call creates its own plugin object with `nestjs()`, as the example does: a `plugins` array shared by two instances shares one binding, which fails boot with `PLUGIN_SHARED_BETWEEN_INSTANCES` (B03) `[R4:BA-r4-05]`.
- **Platforms and transports are app-wide and declared once**, on the default instance `[R1:NEST-r1-09]`. One platform serves every instance's mount. **Principal sources and runtime options are per instance.**
- There is one `BetterAuthGuard` and one scope interceptor, both in the static core module. The guard resolves the instance per route from `@UseAuthInstance` metadata (method over class, default `'default'`).
- Metadata keys carry no instance name, so every decorator works for every instance.
- Hooks bind to one instance through `HookOptions.instance` (default `'default'`).
- Memo keys include the instance name, so one request can be authenticated against two instances without confusion.

### 5.6 Double-import safety

`forRoot()` returns a new dynamic module on every call, and Nest identifies modules by reference, so importing it twice creates two modules (R:nest-di §1.3). The documented pattern is one import in the root module; the module is global, and decorators need no import. Three independent defences turn a mistake into a boot error instead of a silently doubled guard:

1. **Name uniqueness** in the app-scoped `InstanceRegistry` (B07) `[A][C]`.
2. **Exclusive plugin binding** (B06) `[B][C]`. The same better-auth instance cannot be bound twice, even from two copies of this library, because the handle lives on the plugin object.
3. **A per-server mount stamp** (B10) `[B]`. `Symbol.for(…:mounted)` on `httpAdapter.getInstance()` catches two mounts of the same path, again even across library copies.

The guard lives in the static core module, which Nest deduplicates by class, so a second `forRoot` can never register it twice. `APP_GUARD` is contributed only by the `forRoot` whose `globalGuard` is true (B07), and platforms and transports only by the default instance (B25).

### 5.7 Providers and lifecycle `[B][C]`

| Provider                                                                                                                         | Token                                                                        | Scope     | Module                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `BetterAuthGuard`, `BetterAuthScopeInterceptor`                                                                                  | class                                                                        | singleton | core (static, global)                  |
| `InstanceRegistry`, `RequestScope`, `TransportRegistry`, `MountCoordinator`, `PolicyResolver` `[R3:NEST-r3-04]`                  | internal `Symbol.for`                                                        | singleton | core                                   |
| `PRINCIPAL_RESOLVER` (`ChainPrincipalResolver`)                                                                                  | `Symbol.for(…:principal-resolver)`                                           | singleton | core                                   |
| `POLICY_INVOKER` (default invoker: `policy.evaluate(params, context)`; `overrideDecisions` replaces it, §14.8) `[R2:NEST-r2-15]` | `Symbol.for(…:policy-invoker)`                                               | singleton | core                                   |
| options, instance, handle                                                                                                        | `getAuthToken('options' \| 'instance' \| 'handle', name)`                    | singleton | per `forRoot`                          |
| `BetterAuthService`                                                                                                              | class (default instance) + `getAuthToken('service', name)` via `useExisting` | singleton | per `forRoot`                          |
| principal-source providers + registry                                                                                            | `Symbol.for(…:ext:principals:<name>:<i>)`, `…:principal-sources:<name>`      | singleton | per `forRoot`                          |
| platform and transport providers + registries                                                                                    | `Symbol.for(…:ext:<point>:default:<i>)`, `…:platforms`, `…:transports`       | singleton | default `forRoot`                      |
| extension `exports` (e.g. `WS_CONNECTION_AUTH`)                                                                                  | the extension's token                                                        | singleton | re-exported by the `forRoot` module    |
| `APP_GUARD` / `APP_INTERCEPTOR`                                                                                                  | `useExisting: BetterAuthGuard` / `BetterAuthScopeInterceptor`                | —         | the `forRoot` with `globalGuard: true` |

All library constructors put an explicit `@Inject(token)` on every parameter, including `Reflector`, `ModuleRef`, `DiscoveryService`, `MetadataScanner`, `HttpAdapterHost` and `ApplicationConfig` (S5; §12.6). No library provider is request-scoped, because a request-scoped `APP_GUARD` makes every controller request-scoped (R:nest-di §3.3).

**Lifecycle** `[R1:NEST-r1-02, NEST-r1-03]` `[R3:NEST-r3-03]`:

1. **Platform preparation: last arrival wins.** Two events must both have happened:
   - _adapter known_: `MountCoordinator` subscribes to `HttpAdapterHost.init$` (a `ReplaySubject`) in its constructor and records `host.httpAdapter ?? null`;
   - _platforms known_: the default instance's platform registry factory calls `coordinator.registerPlatforms(list)`.

   Whichever event comes second triggers `select` and `prepare()`, once per application, and the coordinator records the adapter it prepared. Neither side depends on the order in which Nest constructs modules. That order is concurrent, and under `NestFactory` `init$` fires before any provider exists (LEAD-V27). LEAD-EXP-3 showed the result on 11.1.17 and 12.0.1:
   - `NestFactory.create`: `init$ → platforms registered → prepare`, all **before `create()` resolves**, so before `main.ts` code and before `init()` registers Nest's body parsers. This holds even when the platform registry waits on an async factory dependency.
   - `@nestjs/testing`: `platforms registered → compile() resolved → init$ → prepare`, all **before `createNestApplication()` returns**.
   - `createApplicationContext` and `createMicroservice`: `init$` fires with `httpAdapter === null`. The coordinator records "no HTTP": no `supports`, no `prepare`, no mount, `TransportKit.http = null`, B08 skipped.
   - `Test…compile()` + `moduleRef.init()`, and `Test…createNestMicroservice()`: `init$` never fires and `httpAdapter` is `undefined` (REV2-NEST:`exp4-testing-no-init.mjs`). If "adapter known" has not happened when the core module's `onModuleInit` runs, the coordinator records `host.httpAdapter ?? null` there, synchronously, which is "no HTTP" for these bootstraps. If `init$` later emits a non-null adapter while that application is still alive (a `createNestApplication()` from the same testing module after `moduleRef.init()`, without `moduleRef.close()`), the coordinator logs `LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER` at ERROR and the application's next lifecycle call of the core module (its `init()`) throws `BetterAuthConfigurationError('LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER')`: auth routes would otherwise silently stay unmounted `[R2:NEST-r2-09]`.
   - **A second application on the same container** `[R3:NEST-r3-03]`: several `createNestApplication()` calls on one compiled `TestingModule`, each closed before the next, a common speed-up of e2e suites. `init$` is a `ReplaySubject` that `HttpAdapterHost` **completes** after its first emission (LEAD-V49), so it never announces the second adapter. The core module notices at `onModuleInit` instead (step 2).

   These bootstrap asymmetries are covered by matrix jobs for every bootstrap (§14.2).

2. **`onModuleInit`** of the global core module, **once per application** `[R2:NEST-r2-05]` `[R3:NEST-r3-03]`. `InstanceRegistry` holds the lifecycle state of the application that currently owns the container: `{ state: new → initialized → bootstrapped, adapter }`, where `adapter` is `host.httpAdapter ?? null` as seen when the state left `new`. `onApplicationShutdown` resets the state to `new` (step 4). At `onModuleInit`, with `current = host.httpAdapter ?? null`:
   - **state not `new`, same adapter**: a repeated lifecycle call of the same application, which returns at once. `NestMicroservice.init()` runs `onModuleInit` and `onApplicationBootstrap` twice (`super.init()`, then `registerModules()`; REV2-NEST:`exp4b-double-init.mjs`, `exp4c-microservice-init-twice.mjs`, on 11.1.17 and 12.0.1), and a hybrid microservice connected with `deferInitialization: true` runs them from `listen()` (LEAD-V49). Nothing below runs twice and `bind()` is never called again for the same application;
   - **state not `new`, different adapter**: a second application started while the first is still alive: `LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER` (step 1);
   - **state `new`, and `current` is the adapter `prepare()` ran for, or `null`**: a fresh application; everything below runs;
   - **state `new`, and `current` is another adapter** (the second application of a reused `TestingModule`): when the selected platform declares `capabilities.prepareAtInit` (Fastify: its `prepare()` only adds a root `onRequest` hook, which Fastify accepts until `ready()`), the coordinator runs `select` and `prepare()` for `current` now and everything below runs. Otherwise (Express: raw capture must precede the body parsers `init()` has already registered) the core module throws `BetterAuthConfigurationError('APP_ADAPTER_CHANGED')`, hint: "compile a new TestingModule for each application (or use NestFactory)". v3 kept one lifecycle state per container, so the second application skipped binding and mounting silently: its auth routes answered 404, Nest hooks were unbound, and every authoritative route answered 401, because the endpoint-result observer records nothing while unbound (REV3-NEST:`exp3-reused-testing-module.mjs`).

   The boot checks are interleaved with the steps they validate, in this order:
   - instance and plugin checks: B01–B05, then the app-structure checks B07 and B25;
   - hook discovery, with B11 (singletons) and B12 (hook patterns and instance names);
   - exclusive binding, with B06 (live owner, or takeover of a closed or never-bootstrapped one) and B26 (the plugin's pre-bind dispatch counter, read at bind). The binding's owner is a fresh object per application, and the binding names its instance. Binding is skipped for an instance whose B01–B04 failed, because it has no usable handle, and for instances that share a plugin object (B03) `[R4:BA-r4-05]`;
   - mount path resolution, with B10;
   - the remaining platform, plan, transport and advice checks: B08, B09, B14 (policy references resolve before any plan compiles), B13, B15, then every transport's `validate()` with its canaries and the coverage rule over its claims and the app's global enhancers (B16), then B17–B21, B23, B24 and B27–B30 (B21 collects every `advise()`);
   - aggregate: if any check failed, throw once with every error (a binding made above never bootstraps, so the next app takes it over, B06). Otherwise print the boot summary (B22);
   - `platform.mount()` per instance.

   This all happens before Nest registers its 404 and error handlers (EXP-C5). On Fastify the auth scope's child error handler reads Nest's handler at request time, so the handler Nest installs later is the one used (§6.4.2, LEAD-EXP-2). **Hybrid apps with `deferInitialization: true`** must initialize the HTTP application (`app.init()` or `app.listen()`) before `app.startAllMicroservices()`: otherwise the microservice's `listen()` runs the core module's `onModuleInit` before Nest's `init()` registered consumer middleware and controller routes, and on Express the auth dispatcher lands ahead of them (LEAD-V49). The docs state the order; RK30 records that the library cannot observe it.

3. **`onApplicationBootstrap`**, once per application. Marks each binding `bootstrapped`. A binding that never reaches this point (a failed `init()`) can be taken over by the next app (B06).
4. **`onApplicationShutdown`.** Mark each plugin binding **closed** (idempotent), then reset the lifecycle state to `new`, keeping the record of the adapter `prepare()` ran for, so the next application on the same container starts clean (step 2) `[R3:NEST-r3-03]`. A closed binding keeps dispatching the application's Nest hooks until another application binds the instance (§10.6) `[R4:SEC-r4-01]`. v4 unbound the handles here, and an unbound plugin skipped every Nest hook. Nest runs `onApplicationShutdown` over the modules in reverse order, and among global modules the one inserted last shuts down first (LEAD-V54), so a global module imported ahead of `BetterAuthModule` that drains work in its own shutdown hook, such as `@nestjs/bullmq`'s worker explorer waiting for active jobs, ran that work after the unbind: a job's `signUpEmail` for a domain a `@BeforeDatabase('user.create')` rule rejects created the account (REV4-SEC:`probe-shutdown-unbind.mjs`). A hook whose own dependencies are already shut down then throws, which fails that better-auth call closed. Nothing is done in `onModuleDestroy` or `beforeApplicationShutdown`, which run before `dispose()` closes the server (Nest 11.1.17 `core/nest-application-context.js:126-131`) `[C]`.

**Guard registration and overriding.** When `globalGuard` is true, the registration is `providers: [{ provide: APP_GUARD, useExisting: BetterAuthGuard }, { provide: APP_INTERCEPTOR, useExisting: BetterAuthScopeInterceptor }]`. `overrideProvider(BetterAuthGuard)` replaces what `APP_GUARD` aliases; that does not work with `useClass` (R:nest-di §9). `@UseBetterAuth()`/`@UseGuards(BetterAuthGuard)` sites create separate injectables that only `overrideGuard(BetterAuthGuard)` replaces (`core/injector/module.js:344-356`). The testing helper `overrideAuthGuard` therefore does both, for the guard and the interceptor (§14.8) `[R1:NEST-r1-08]`. B16 recognizes a global enhancer by identity with the instance the class token resolves to, so an overridden `BetterAuthGuard` still covers every `'global'` claim `[R4:NEST-r4-02]`. With `globalGuard: false`, `@UseBetterAuth()` applies both enhancers where needed, and B16 reports every claimed handler that declares something and that nothing guards, and every unclaimed method whose own metadata is on B16's trigger list (§5.4) `[R2:NEST-r2-02]` `[R3:NEST-r3-07]`. An app may also register the enhancers itself, to control where `BetterAuthGuard` runs among its own global guards: `globalGuard: false` plus `{ provide: APP_GUARD, useExisting: BetterAuthGuard }` and `{ provide: APP_INTERCEPTOR, useExisting: BetterAuthScopeInterceptor }` in `AppModule`, listed before the guards that read the principal. Nest runs an `AppModule`'s own `APP_GUARD`s before those of the modules it imports (REV3-NEST:`exp1-app-guard-order.mjs`, both majors and both bootstraps), and B16 counts the enhancers wherever they were registered `[R3:NEST-r3-02]`.

## 6. HTTP integration, per platform

### 6.1 Mount timing in the Nest lifecycle

Core owns the lifecycle and the platform supplies the platform-specific moves (§5.7, `MountCoordinator`). `HttpAdapterHost.init$` is the only signal that works under both `NestFactory` and `@nestjs/testing`. Constructor-time registration alone would break tests, because `httpAdapter` is `undefined` in provider constructors there (R:nest-platform §1.1). Because `init$` can fire before any provider exists, and fires with a `null` adapter for adapter-less bootstraps, preparation waits for the later of "adapter known" and "platforms registered" (§5.7, LEAD-EXP-3) `[R1:NEST-r1-02, NEST-r1-03]`.

| Platform | Step                                                                  | Lifecycle point                                          | `NestFactory` 11 / 12                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `@nestjs/testing` 11 / 12                                               | Why here                                                                                                                                            |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Express  | A: bounded raw capture of auth-route bodies                           | `prepare` (last of `init$` / platform registration)      | inside `create()`, before it resolves: before parsers and `main.ts` middleware                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | inside `createNestApplication()`, before it returns and before `init()` | must precede Nest's `jsonParser`/`urlencodedParser` (R:nest-platform §2.3)                                                                          |
| Express  | B: dispatcher (`app.use`, path-checked)                               | `onModuleInit` (`mount`)                                 | after parsers, `main.ts` middleware/CORS, `configure()` middleware and controller routes; **before** the 404 handler                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | same                                                                    | host CORS, helmet and `app.use` apply to auth routes. Routes registered after `onModuleInit` are hidden by v11's 404 handler (R:nest-platform §2.5) |
| Fastify  | root `onRequest` hook recording `request.raw → reply`                 | `prepare`                                                | before `ready()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | before `init()`                                                         | lets Apollo-on-Fastify find the reply for cookies (LEAD-V8)                                                                                         |
| Fastify  | encapsulated plugin at `prefix: basePath`, with a child error handler | `onModuleInit` (`mount`, `await instance.register(...)`) | loaded immediately; no `ready()` needed (EXP-B:E10). Its routes capture the error handler current at registration, which is Fastify's default because Nest sets its own later (`registerRouterHooks` after `callInitHook`), so the scope installs a child handler that delegates **at request time** to the root's current handler, Nest's (LEAD-V28, LEAD-EXP-2) `[R1:NEST-r1-04]` | same                                                                    | Fastify is order-insensitive until `ready()`; adding routes after `listen()` throws (R:nest-platform §2.4)                                          |

The resulting Express stack was verified on Nest 11.1.17 and 12.0.1 under both bootstraps by EXP-A:`exp-express.mjs`, EXP-B:E1 and EXP-C4/C5:

```
[nest hook] → [A: capture] → cors (enableCors) → user app.use(...) → jsonParser → urlencodedParser
            → consumer middleware → controller routes → [B: dispatch] → 404 → error handler
```

- **Consumer middleware.** `MiddlewareConsumer` middleware, for example a CLS or MikroORM `RequestContext` middleware applied with `forRoutes({ path: '*path', method: ALL })`, wraps the Express dispatcher when there is **no** global prefix (EXP-A:`exp-consumer-mw.mjs`, EXP-C5). With `setGlobalPrefix('v1')` it does not, because Nest mounts consumer middleware under the prefix. `http.around` covers that case (§4.6).
- **Nest 12** does not change any of this. The init order and body-parser timing are the same (R:nest-platform §7.3). The v12 Express 404 prefix-scoping change does not matter, because B runs before the 404 handler on both majors. Raw routes are invisible to v12's `routeConflictPolicy`, which is documented.

### 6.2 Path resolution (S3) `[A][B][C]`

```ts
async function resolveMountPath(auth: AuthLike, allowRoot: boolean): Promise<string> {
  const ctx = (await auth.$context) as AuthContextView;
  const raw = ctx.baseURL
    ? new URL(ctx.baseURL).pathname                 // static baseURL (incl. BETTER_AUTH_URL): its path wins over basePath
    : ctx.options.basePath || '/api/auth';          // unset or dynamic { allowedHosts }: ctx.baseURL === '' (EXP-B:E11)
  const path = raw.length > 1 ? raw.replace(/\/+$/, '') : raw;
  if (!path.startsWith('/') || (path === '/' && !allowRoot)) throw new BetterAuthConfigurationError('INVALID_MOUNT_PATH', …);
  return path;
}
```

- The router uses exactly `new URL(ctx.baseURL).pathname` for a static `baseURL` (`BA/api/index.ts:280`; `BA/utils/url.ts:73-89`).
- For an unset or dynamic `baseURL`, the per-request base path is `options.basePath || '/api/auth'` (`BA/auth/base.ts:51`). EXP-B:E11 verified every configuration style.
- `auth.options.basePath` is **never** read. It is `undefined` by default and wrong when `baseURL` contains a path (R:ba-core §3.7).
- **When it runs** `[R1:NEST-r1-02]`. `MountCoordinator` resolves the path in `onModuleInit`, once per instance, and only when the app has an HTTP adapter and the instance's `http.mount` is not `false`. Adapter-less bootstraps (`createMicroservice`, `createApplicationContext`) never resolve or mount anything (§5.7). B10 then checks the result across instances: no overlapping mounts, and no `Symbol.for(…:mounted)` stamp for the same path on the server.
- **An unset `baseURL` is a development-only configuration** `[R1:SEC-r1-07]`. In the `ctx.baseURL === ''` branch the _path_ is static, but better-auth derives the _origin_ of its base URL from each request, and with it token links and a trusted origin (`BA/auth/base.ts:76-100`). A client-chosen `Host` header then ends up in password-reset links (REV-SEC:`probe-unset-baseurl.mjs`). In production that configuration fails boot (B23 `UNSAFE_BASE_URL`), unless `baseURL` is a dynamic `{ allowedHosts }` config, which better-auth validates per request, or the user sets `http.allowRequestDerivedBaseURL` (§6.3 step 2).
- **Matching** is a raw-string prefix test on the undecoded pathname of the original URL, with the query stripped: `p === base || p.startsWith(base + '/')`. It uses no Express or path-to-regexp wildcard syntax, which broke the reference seven times (R:ref-issues cluster 1). Everything below the prefix goes to better-auth, which owns 404, method checks and trailing-slash rules. An unknown path under the prefix is therefore a bodiless better-auth 404, the largest misconfiguration cluster in the reference's issues. The response stays as it is, and outside production core logs the path once with a "did you mean" (§6.3 step 7) `[R1:SEC-r1-16]`.
- **Precedence.** A Nest controller route that exactly matches a path under the base path is served by Nest on every platform (H11), and B17 warns about it at boot.
- **All methods** are routed, including PUT/PATCH/DELETE (SCIM, oauth-provider), HEAD and OPTIONS. better-auth answers HEAD and OPTIONS with 404 unless host CORS answered the preflight first (R:ba-core §3.1; ADR-32).

### 6.3 Web Request construction (core `AuthExchange`) `[A][B][C]`

`binding.handle(inbound)` does the following, in order:

1. **Body.**
   - GET and HEAD: `null`.
   - A `Uint8Array` is used as-is; the platform has already enforced the limit, and core re-checks `byteLength > bodyLimit` as a guard against a faulty third-party platform.
   - A `ReadableStream` is buffered up to `bodyLimit`. Past the limit the stream is cancelled and the result is `payloadTooLarge()`. This keeps the limit and the 413 in one place for Web-native platforms `[C]`.
2. **URL.** If the instance has a static `baseURL`, the origin is replaced with that origin, so no client-controlled header influences it `[B][C]`. Otherwise the platform's trust-proxy-aware origin is kept, and better-auth applies its own `advanced.trustedProxyHeaders` gate on the untouched `x-forwarded-*` headers (`BA/utils/url.ts:167-190, 270-340`). With an unset `baseURL`, better-auth derives token links and a trusted origin from that origin, so a production boot without a `baseURL` fails (B23) unless the user opts into `http.allowRequestDerivedBaseURL` `[R1:SEC-r1-07]`. An unparsable URL, such as a malformed `Host`, yields `400 { code: 'INVALID_REQUEST_URL' }` `[A]`.
3. **Headers.** Copy `inbound.headers`, then:
   - delete hop-by-hop headers (`connection`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-connection`, `transfer-encoding`, `te`, `trailer`, `upgrade`), because the body is now a fixed buffer;
   - delete any inbound copy of the client-IP header, and any header named `x-nsba-ip-*`, for anti-spoofing;
   - set the client-IP header from `inbound.clientIp` when it is non-null (§6.8).

   `Origin`, `Referer`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, `Cookie`, `Authorization`, `Content-Type` and `X-Forwarded-*` are never touched (R:ba-core §1.2 P8). Pseudo-headers cannot be present, because `Headers` rejects them and `toWebHeaders` drops them.

4. **`around` chain.** `http.around` functions run outermost-first around step 5 (§4.6).
5. **Dispatch.** `auth.handler(new Request(url, { method, headers, body, signal }))` runs **outside** any `RequestScope`. Router calls carry `_flag === 'router'` anyway, so the cookie bridge and refresh suppression stay inactive, and the Response already carries its cookies. better-auth's router applies its own origin check, rate limit, `disabledPaths` and routing.
6. **Errors.** `auth.handler` can throw: on an init failure, on a disallowed dynamic host, or when the user set `onAPIError.throw` (`BA/auth/base.ts:49-109`; LEAD-V25).
   - If the instance sets `onAPIError: { throw: true }` and `isAPIError(e)`, the error is **rethrown unchanged**, with its hidden `better-call:api-error-headers` intact, so it reaches the host error pipeline (Express `next(err)`, a Fastify rejection) and the user's Nest filters, which is what that option asks for `[R1:BA-r1-09]`.
   - Otherwise, if `isAPIError(e)` (never `instanceof`, S6), the result is `Response.json(e.body ?? { message: e.message }, { status: e.statusCode, headers })`. The headers are `e.headers` merged with the hidden `e[Symbol.for('better-call:api-error-headers')]`, which carry cookies set before the throw. This covers the init and dynamic-host cases.
   - Anything else becomes `BetterAuthInfrastructureError(cause)` with a redacted cause (§13.4), which rejects to the platform. The platform routes it to the host error pipeline, so it surfaces as a 5xx logged by Nest's filters.
7. **Diagnostics** (never change the response):
   - **Unknown paths** `[R1:SEC-r1-16]`. When `http.diagnostics` is on (default outside production) and better-auth answers 404 for a matched path, core logs one WARN per distinct method and path, capped at 100 distinct paths. It names the resolved base path and suggests the closest endpoint path by Levenshtein distance over `auth.api[*].path` (the list B12 builds), for example: `better-auth has no route for POST /api/auth/signin/email (mounted at /api/auth). Did you mean /api/auth/sign-in/email?`
   - **Untrusted proxy** `[R1:SEC-r1-06]`. In production, when the platform reports `proxyTrust().mode === 'none'` and an auth-route request carries `x-forwarded-for`, `forwarded` or `x-real-ip`, core logs `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` once per application (the flag lives in `AuthExchange`, §12.5). The message names the socket IP the platform resolved, says that it became the rate-limit key or, when better-auth's `trustedProxies` covers it, that better-auth resolved no IP and every client shares one bucket, and names the platform setting to change `[R2:BA-r2-04]`. While better-auth's rate limiter is off (B30), it says instead that the IP is recorded on sessions only `[R4:BA-r4-02]`.

**Why we do not use `toNodeHandler`, `getRequest` or `setResponse`** `[A][B][C]`:

- they lose the query string under some Express mounts (R:nest-platform §6.1);
- they crash on HTTP/2 pseudo-headers;
- they trust `x-forwarded-proto` unconditionally;
- they re-serialize consumed bodies, which breaks raw-signature endpoints;
- they apply no body limit to chunked requests;
- using them means importing `better-call`, which better-auth pins exactly.

Building the `Request` ourselves also makes body semantics independent of better-call versions: 1.3.2 and 1.4.0 differ (R:ba-core §5.2).

### 6.4 Body strategy (S4)

**Invariant.** Auth routes receive exactly the bytes the client sent, bounded by `bodyLimit` (default 1 MiB). App routes keep Nest-native parsing, including `rawBody: true`, `useBodyParser`, parser limits and Fastify's secure JSON parser. The library never asks for `bodyParser: false` and never replaces the app's parsers (R:ref-issues cluster 2). H3 and H4 (§4.1.2) state this for every platform, third-party ones included. H4 also fixes the over-limit answer: the same `payloadTooLarge()` bytes on every platform, with the host's CORS headers, whatever the platform's own limit mechanism answers internally `[R1:NEST-r1-04]`.

#### 6.4.1 Express: two phases `[A][B][C]`

- **Step A**, at `prepare()`, a path-less `app.use(nsbaCapture)`. It acts only when `ctx.route(rawPath(req.originalUrl))` matches, the method is not GET, HEAD or OPTIONS, and `mayHaveBody(...)` is true. For those requests it calls `readBoundedBody(req, { limit, declaredLength, drainOnOverflow: true })`, stores the result under `req[Symbol.for(…:raw-body)]`, and calls `next()` through `bindAsyncContext`, so any async context that was already active survives the stream callback (EXP-C5). body-parser 2.x skips a finished stream (`body-parser/lib/read.js:40-44`), so Nest's parsers, any `useBodyParser(...)` and any `express.json()` never touch auth bodies. They behave normally for everything else (EXP-B:E1: app routes keep `rawBody`, with and without `useBodyParser`). `prepare()` runs before `NestFactory.create()` resolves even when the options factory awaits an async dependency (LEAD-EXP-3), so the capture is always ahead of `main.ts` middleware and of the parsers registered in `init()`.
- **Overflow.** A declared `content-length` above the limit, or a streamed overflow, sets the flag `'too-large'`. Capture stops buffering and **drains** the rest of the stream so later middleware sees it finished, which is what body-parser itself does before it answers an error (`read.js:132-135, 240-247`). The drain is capped at `drainCap` (default `8 × bodyLimit`, a design choice that has not been measured). Past the cap the socket is destroyed. Step B then answers 413 **after** the host's CORS middleware, so browsers can read it: EXP-B:E1 and EXP-B:E4 showed 413 with ACAO. Answering inside step A returned 413 **without** ACAO (EXP-A:`exp-e2e.mjs`), which is why the flag is deferred `[A][B]`.
- **Step B**, at `onModuleInit`, one `app.use(nsbaDispatch)` per binding. If the path does not match it calls `next()`. Otherwise it builds `InboundAuthRequest` from these parts and writes the Response back (§6.5):
  - `req.method`;
  - `${req.protocol}://${req.host}${req.originalUrl}` (`req.protocol` and `req.host` honor `trust proxy`);
  - `toWebHeaders(req.headers)`;
  - the captured bytes;
  - `options.clientIp?.(req) ?? req.ip`.

  A rejection goes to `next(err)`, which Nest's Express error handler and global filters receive at request time.

- **Residual caveat** `[B]`. Global middleware that reads the raw stream _without_ checking `isFinished`, such as a hand-written `raw-body` logger, would wait on an ended stream for auth routes. This is documented, and case `H-middleware-order` catches it.

#### 6.4.2 Fastify: an encapsulated `parseAs: 'buffer'` parser and a child error handler `[A]` `[R1:NEST-r1-04]`

```ts
const root = adapter.getInstance();
await root.register(
  async (scope) => {
    scope.removeAllContentTypeParsers(); // this context only; root parsers untouched
    scope.addContentTypeParser(
      "*",
      { parseAs: "buffer", bodyLimit: binding.bodyLimit },
      (_req, body, done) => done(null, body),
    ); // exact bytes as a Buffer; FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE above the limit
    scope.setErrorHandler(function (err, request, reply) {
      // routes capture THIS handler at registration
      if ((err as { code?: string }).code === "FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE")
        return sendWebResponse(reply, binding.payloadTooLarge(), false); // canonical 413, reply-level CORS headers kept (H4)
      return root.errorHandler.call(this, err, request, reply); // read at REQUEST time: Nest's handler (H8)
    });
    const handler = async (request: FastifyRequest, reply: FastifyReply) => {
      const response = await binding.handle({
        method: request.method,
        url: `${request.protocol}://${request.host}${request.originalUrl}`, // originalUrl = raw.originalUrl || raw.url
        headers: toWebHeaders(request.raw.headers), // drops HTTP/2 pseudo-headers
        body: request.body instanceof Uint8Array ? request.body : null,
        clientIp: options.clientIp?.(request) ?? request.ip,
        platformRequest: request,
        signal: abortOnClose(request.raw, reply.raw),
      });
      return sendWebResponse(reply, response, request.method === "HEAD"); // §6.6
    };
    scope.route({
      method: scope.supportedMethods,
      url: "/",
      handler,
      exposeHeadRoute: false,
    });
    scope.route({
      method: scope.supportedMethods,
      url: "/*",
      handler,
      exposeHeadRoute: false,
    });
  },
  { prefix: binding.basePath },
);
```

- **Isolation.** Parsers are copied into child contexts when the plugin loads, so `removeAllContentTypeParsers()` affects only auth routes (R:nest-platform §3.2). App routes keep Nest's parsers, Fastify's secure JSON parser and `rawBody`.
- **Coverage.** A body without `content-type` falls through to the `'*'` parser (LEAD-V10, `content-type-parser.js:119-153`).
- **Limit.** `parseAs: 'buffer'` with `bodyLimit` makes Fastify enforce the limit in its own parser path. It rejects a declared `content-length` above the limit before reading and stops a streamed overflow, raising `FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE`. The child error handler turns that into the canonical `payloadTooLarge()` Response through `reply`, so the body is identical to Express's and `@fastify/cors` headers survive (LEAD-EXP-2: 413 `{ code: 'PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE' }` with the CORS header, on Nest 11 and 12 under both bootstraps).
- **Error pipeline.** The plugin loads during the awaited `register()`, so its routes capture the error handler that is current at that moment. In `onModuleInit` that is Fastify's default handler, because Nest calls `setErrorHandler` later, in `registerRouterHooks` (12.0.1 `nest-application.js:103-124`; 11.1.17 `:93-104`). Without a child handler an infrastructure error would get Fastify's own 500 body, skip every `APP_FILTER` and go unlogged, since Nest creates Fastify with its logger off (REV-NEST:`exp2-fastify-error.cjs`). The child handler looks up `root.errorHandler` when a request fails, and by then it is Nest's. `FastifyAdapter.setErrorHandler` always targets the root instance, even with a global prefix (LEAD-V28). LEAD-EXP-2 showed `APP_FILTER` receiving the auth-route error with `setGlobalPrefix('v1')` on 11.1.17 and 12.0.1, under `NestFactory` and `@nestjs/testing`.
- **Exactness.** EXP-A:`exp-e2e.mjs` echoed JSON with odd whitespace, UTF-8 over PATCH and multipart byte-for-byte on Nest 11 and 12. Form sign-in succeeds (EXP-B:E4 with the equivalent pass-through variant).
- **Methods.** `supportedMethods` includes HEAD and OPTIONS. `exposeHeadRoute: false` prevents an auto-generated HEAD sibling, which is what triggers Fastify's `reply.send(Response)` HEAD 500 bug (`head-route.js:29`).
- **Why not the alternatives** (ADR-04, ADR-39):
  - a hand-rolled pass-through reader (EXP-B:E4) works but duplicates Fastify's limit logic;
  - a root route with a route-level `onRequest` answering from the hook (EXP-C6) works but runs handler logic in a hook;
  - registering without `await` (the plugin loads at `ready()`, after Nest's handler exists) also reaches Nest's filters, but makes route availability depend on who calls `ready()` and when; the child handler is explicit and works either way;
  - middie middleware bypasses `@fastify/cors` and `onSend`.

#### 6.4.3 Degraded tier (documented, warned once) `[A][C]`

If a platform finds the stream already consumed before its capture point, it falls back in this order (`recoverConsumedBody`, §2.2.10):

1. `req.rawBody` (a Buffer): exact.
2. `req.body` re-serialized for its content type, with `JSON.stringify` or `URLSearchParams`: lossy.

- **The limit still holds.** Recovered bytes reach `binding.handle()` as a `Uint8Array`, and core re-checks `byteLength > bodyLimit` (§6.3 step 1). An over-limit body therefore still gets the canonical `payloadTooLarge()` Response (H4), even though the host's own parser already read it.
- **A one-time warning** (`W_BODY_ALREADY_CONSUMED`) names the cause and the endpoints that break: raw-signature webhooks such as Stripe's, which read `ctx.request.text()` (R:ba-integrations §4). "One-time" means once per application: the flag lives in the platform provider, because the library keeps no module-level state (§12.5).
- **Trigger.** The only known trigger is an Express instance passed to `new ExpressAdapter(app)` that already had `express.json()` attached before `NestFactory.create`. It never happens in the default setup. Phase A runs inside `NestFactory.create()`, even when the options factory awaits an async dependency (§5.7, LEAD-EXP-3), so it is ahead of everything Nest or `main.ts` registers `[R1:NEST-r1-03]`. Fastify cannot reach this tier, because the auth scope owns its content-type parsers (§6.4.2).

#### 6.4.4 Why buffer instead of streaming to better-auth `[A][B]`

Buffering bounded bytes gives:

- a deterministic 413 before better-auth runs, byte-identical on every platform (H4);
- a correct `content-length`;
- no `duplex: 'half'` stream plumbing;
- no half-consumed stream when a before-hook short-circuits.

With a streaming body and an in-flight limit, better-auth logged `SERVER_ERROR: PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` before the host could answer (EXP-B:E4). better-auth's endpoints take small bodies; the largest legitimate ones are SAML responses and SCIM documents, well under 1 MiB (§17 Q5).

### 6.5 Express write-back `[A][B]`

`writeWebResponse(res, response, { head })`, exported from `./platform` for other Node platforms:

- `res.statusCode = response.status`.
- `res.setHeader(k, v)` for every header except `set-cookie`. For `vary`, merge the union with any value already set (CORS sets `Vary: Origin`). For every other header better-auth's value wins.
- `set-cookie`: append each value from `response.headers.getSetCookie()` to any existing values. Never loop with `setHeader`, which keeps only the last cookie (R:ba-integrations §5 C1).
- HEAD, or a `null` body: `res.end()`.
- Otherwise stream the body with backpressure (`drain`), and cancel the reader on the client's `close`. A client that disconnects mid-exchange also aborts `inbound.signal`; the write is abandoned without an error log (§6.10).
- Redirects (302 + `Location`) pass through untouched with their cookies (EXP-B:E4).
- The library's own Responses, the canonical 413 (`binding.payloadTooLarge()`) and the 400 `INVALID_REQUEST_URL`, are written through this same function in step B, after the host's CORS middleware. They therefore carry the same host headers as better-auth's responses (H4; EXP-B:E1).
- A rejected `binding.handle()` writes nothing. It goes to `next(err)`, so Nest's Express error handler and the global filters answer it at request time (H8, §6.4.1).

### 6.6 Fastify write-back `[A][B][C]`

```ts
function sendWebResponse(
  reply: FastifyReply,
  response: Response,
  head: boolean,
) {
  reply.code(response.status);
  for (const [k, v] of response.headers)
    if (k !== "set-cookie") reply.header(k, v);
  for (const c of response.headers.getSetCookie())
    reply.header("set-cookie", c); // Fastify appends set-cookie
  return reply.send(head ? undefined : (response.body ?? undefined));
}
```

- `reply.send(Response)` is **not** used. It returns 500 for HEAD on routes with an auto-generated HEAD sibling (R:nest-platform §6.3). Unwrapping status, headers and the body stream is the verified workaround, and it keeps `@fastify/cors` headers and `onSend` hooks (EXP-B:E4, EXP-C6).
- `reply.hijack()` and writes to `reply.raw` are never used. They drop `reply.header()` values such as CORS and skip `onSend`.
- The handler is `async`. A rejection takes Fastify's error path: the scope's child error handler delegates to the root's current handler (Nest's), then the global filters, so it never hangs, unlike a rejected middie middleware (R:ref-impl §2.3), and it is never answered by Fastify's default handler (§6.4.2).

### 6.7 Write-back rules common to every platform

| Concern                                                                          | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Evidence                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Multiple `Set-Cookie`                                                            | read via `getSetCookie()`, append each (H7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | EXP-B:E4 `["a","b"]` on both platforms                                                                               |
| Streaming                                                                        | pass `response.body` through with backpressure                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | better-auth returns streamed and HTML bodies (`BA/api/dispatch.ts:421-424`)                                          |
| HEAD                                                                             | status and headers, no body                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | better-auth answers HEAD with 404; the Fastify HEAD bug is avoided                                                   |
| Redirects                                                                        | verbatim 3xx + `Location` + cookies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `ctx.redirect` is an `APIError('FOUND')` with a `location` header (R:ba-core §3.6, better-call `context.ts:309-312`) |
| Arbitrary content types                                                          | never re-serialize                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | oauth-provider, SSO and error pages return raw Responses (R:ba-core §3.6)                                            |
| Host headers                                                                     | merge, don't clobber (`vary` union, `set-cookie` append)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | CORS survives (EXP-B:E4, EXP-A:`exp-e2e`, EXP-C4/C6)                                                                 |
| The library's own Responses (413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, 400 `INVALID_REQUEST_URL`) | built by core as Web `Response`s and written through the same path, so they are byte-identical across platforms and carry host CORS headers (H4) `[R1:NEST-r1-04]`                                                                                                                                                                                 | EXP-B:E1/E4; LEAD-EXP-2                                                                                              |
| Failures                                                                         | never answered with a platform's default error body. A rejected `handle()` reaches the host error pipeline at request time: Express `next(err)`; Fastify's child error handler, which delegates to the root's current handler (H8, §6.4.2). With `onAPIError.throw` the original `APIError` travels the same way (H13) `[R1:NEST-r1-04, BA-r1-09]` | LEAD-EXP-2; LEAD-V25                                                                                                 |
| Nest interceptors, pipes and serializers                                         | never run on auth routes. Exception filters see auth routes only for those failures                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | better-auth principles P1/P2 (§0.2)                                                                                  |

### 6.8 Client IP for rate limiting `[A][B][C]`

better-auth reads the client IP **only from headers**; the default is `x-forwarded-for`. When its rate limiter is on, which better-auth's default makes true only for `NODE_ENV=production` (LEAD-V52; B30 reports it off in a deployment this library treats as production) `[R4:BA-r4-02]`, a request with no usable IP falls back to one shared bucket per path, and sign-in is limited to 3 per 10 s for everyone (`CORE/utils/ip.ts:353-383`; `BA/api/rate-limiter/index.ts:342, 442-451`). The IP is also recorded on every session. A Web `Request` cannot carry the socket address, so the host must supply it. The design splits the job so that proxy trust is configured once, in the platform, for the whole app:

1. **The platform decides trust.** Express `req.ip` honors `app.set('trust proxy', …)`; Fastify `request.ip` honors `trustProxy`. Each platform accepts a `clientIp` override.
2. **The plugin declares the header.** `nestjs()` returns `{ options: { advanced: { ipAddress: { ipAddressHeaders: [header] } } } }` from `init()`. better-auth merges plugin options with `defu(userOptions, pluginOptions)` (LEAD-V4), so this is a construction-time _default_, not a mutation (S1). A user-configured list stays first and ours is appended. The merged options feed both the rate limiter and session IP recording (`db/internal-adapter.ts:501`).

   **Interaction with better-auth's own proxy trust** `[R2:BA-r2-04]`. When the user set no `ipAddressHeaders`, ours becomes the **only** header better-auth reads, so `X-Forwarded-For` is no longer consulted, and better-auth still applies `advanced.ipAddress.trustedProxies` to our header's value (`CORE/utils/ip.ts:311-331, 364-377`). With the platform's trust off behind a load balancer inside `trustedProxies`, the value is the balancer's address, which better-auth discards: every client resolves to no IP and shares one bucket (REV2-BA:`exp4-trustedproxies-header.mjs`: plain better-auth `203.0.113.7`, with the plugin `null`, with the platform's trust on `203.0.113.7`). With the platform's trust set, the value is the client's address and `trustedProxies` is harmless. A deployment configured the better-auth way therefore sets the platform's trust proxy when it adds `nestjs()`, or keeps better-auth's chain parsing with `nestjs({ clientIpHeader: false })`. B18 warns in production about exactly this combination.

3. **The header name is unguessable** `[R1:SEC-r1-18]`. By default `nestjs()` generates `x-nsba-ip-<32 hex chars>` once per `nestjs()` call with `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()` (Web Crypto, so the plugin stays runtime-agnostic): one name per plugin instance, so an app with named instances (§5.5) has several. The name never leaves the process. A code path that forwards raw client headers to better-auth, such as a custom controller calling `auth.handler(new Request(url, { headers: req.headers }))` or `auth.api.signInEmail({ headers: fromNodeHeaders(req.headers) })`, therefore cannot be abused to pick a rate-limit bucket or a recorded IP. A fixed name is used only when `clientIpHeader` is set explicitly (for a trusted sidecar that calls `auth.handler` itself).
4. **Core strips and sets.** `AuthExchange` deletes any client-supplied copy of the header, and any `x-nsba-ip-*` header, then sets it from `inbound.clientIp`. For app routes the kernel does the same on `TransportCall.headers()` using `call.clientIp`, so direct `auth.api.signInEmail({ headers })` calls record the right IP. `BetterAuthService.headersFrom(req)` does it too. The name is read from the plugin's protocol object (`handle.clientIpHeader`), so the plugin is the single source of truth.
5. **Verified end to end** (with the v1 fixed name; the random name changes nothing on this path). EXP-A:`exp-e2e.mjs` covers Nest 11/12 × Express/Fastify; EXP-B:E9 and EXP-C7 ran with `NODE_ENV=production`:
   - better-auth sees the trust-proxy-resolved IP;
   - a spoofed header is ignored;
   - under the sign-in rule (3 per 10 s), the fourth request from one IP gets 429 while another IP gets 200 (EXP-C7 recorded `401, 401, 401, 429`; better-auth denies once the count reaches `max`, `BA/api/rate-limiter/index.ts:78`);
   - a user list is kept first: `["cf-connecting-ip", <our header>]`.
6. **Proxy-trust diagnostics** `[R1:SEC-r1-06]`. The two classic misconfigurations are silent. better-auth's own "shared bucket" warning fires only in the `trustedProxies` case of item 2, where the IP resolves to none; otherwise the platform always supplies a valid, wrong IP `[R2:BA-r2-04]`:
   - _trust off behind a proxy_: every client gets the proxy's IP (or, with better-auth's `trustedProxies` covering it, no IP), so one attacker sending 3 sign-ins every 10 s locks out every user;
   - _trust everything_: `req.ip` is the client-chosen left-most `X-Forwarded-For` value, so rotating it bypasses the limit.

   Platforms therefore report `proxyTrust()` (Express from `app.get('trust proxy')`, Fastify from `initialConfig.trustProxy`). The boot summary prints it. B27 warns when it is `'all'` in production. In production, the first auth-route request that carries `x-forwarded-for`, `forwarded` or `x-real-ip` while trust is `'none'` logs `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` once, naming the socket IP and what better-auth made of it (§6.3 step 7). Migration step 8 (§15.1) walks through the setting.

7. **Opt-out.** `nestjs({ clientIpHeader: false })`. The user then configures `advanced.ipAddress` themselves (better-auth's `trustedProxies` with `X-Forwarded-For`), and B18 warns in production if nothing is configured.

### 6.9 CORS, global prefix and versioning

**CORS stays with the host** `[A][B][C]`. better-auth emits no CORS headers and answers preflight with 404; `trustedOrigins` is its CSRF check, not CORS (R:ba-integrations §0 item 2). The library configures no CORS. Its job is to make sure host CORS reaches auth routes:

- **Express:** the dispatcher is registered after `enableCors()` and `app.use()`.
- **Fastify:** the auth route is a real Fastify route answered through `reply`, so `@fastify/cors` hooks and preflight apply, including on the canonical 413.

Preflight 204 with ACAO, and ACAO on 200, 302 and 413, were verified on both platforms and both majors (EXP-B:E1/E4, EXP-A:`exp-e2e`, EXP-C4/C6, LEAD-EXP-2). We never call `enableCors` ourselves: Fastify throws on double registration (#52) and Express would apply it app-wide (#69, #95).

**`betterAuthCorsOrigin(auth, { allowPatterns? })`** is a `cors` / `@fastify/cors` origin callback for teams that want CORS to follow better-auth's trusted origins `[C]` `[R1:BA-r1-11, SEC-r1-17]`:

- **The trusted set is the post-init one** (`TrustedOrigins`, U17). `(await auth.$context).trustedOrigins` is computed before plugins' `init()` run, and plugin-contributed origins (for example `expo()` adding `exp://` in development) live only in the post-init `ctx.options.trustedOrigins` (LEAD-V17). The helper therefore merges `ctx.trustedOrigins` with the post-init array. It matches through better-auth's own matcher, `ctx.isTrustedOrigin.call({ trustedOrigins: merged }, origin)`, which keeps better-auth's wildcard and custom-scheme semantics. The origin check (§7.10) uses the same resolver.
- **Exact origins only by default.** `trustedOrigins` exists for CSRF and redirect allow-listing. By default the helper allows an origin only if it equals a trusted entry that is an exact `http(s)` origin with no wildcard. Exact `http:` origins are kept because development uses `http://localhost:3000`. Wildcard and custom-scheme matches need `allowPatterns: true`. This default excludes **only** wildcard and custom-scheme entries: without it, every origin a pattern such as `https://*.vercel.app` (preview deployments) matches would gain credentialed read access wherever the helper applies.
- **Every exact trusted origin gains credentialed CORS wherever the helper applies.** The helper cannot tell why an origin is trusted. A partner origin listed exactly in `trustedOrigins` only so that it is accepted as a `callbackURL` is, to the helper, an allowed origin like any other, so it can read the responses of every route the helper covers with the user's cookies. That is why the helper belongs on the auth mount (next bullet) and app routes get their own allow-list.
- **Function-valued `trustedOrigins(request)`** cannot be evaluated without a request, and a CORS origin callback receives none, so the helper throws at first use with a hint to supply your own `origin` function `[C]`. That is safer than silently using init-time values.
- **Scope.** The docs recommend an explicit CORS allow-list for app routes, and show how to scope the helper to the auth mount: on Express `app.use(basePath, cors({ origin: betterAuthCorsOrigin(auth), credentials: true }))` when app routes need no CORS, or one `cors` middleware whose per-request options delegate picks the helper for paths under the mount and the allow-list elsewhere (§15.1 step 4); on Fastify an `@fastify/cors` `delegator` keyed on the request path. An app-wide `app.enableCors({ origin: betterAuthCorsOrigin(auth), credentials: true })` is documented only with the caveat of the previous bullet. Case `LIB-cors-helper` (§14.5) tests the helper.

**Global prefix and versioning** `[A][B][C]`. Auth routes live at better-auth's own path, outside `setGlobalPrefix` and `enableVersioning`, because raw platform routes are subject to neither (R:nest-platform §5).
