  The alternatives each fail somewhere. A plain `GraphQLError` (drafts A and C) is logged at ERROR on every denial, because it is not intrinsic. An `HttpException` (draft B) has its `extensions.code` rewritten by Apollo's `autoTransformHttpErrors`, so 429 becomes `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (LEAD-V8).

- **Infrastructure and configuration errors** `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`. GraphQL drivers put `err.message` into `errors[i].message`, even in production (LEAD-EXP-7), so request-time `BetterAuthConfigurationError` details would reach clients (handler and instance names, better-auth error text). Two layers prevent it. Request-time configuration errors are generic as thrown (`atRequest`, §7.8, §13.3), which covers errors raised where the guard did not run. For errors the guard catches, the GraphQL transports implement `toInternalException`, which returns `BetterAuthGraphqlInternalError`:
  - message `'Internal server error'`;
  - `extensions: { code: 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR', reason: 'AUTH_UNAVAILABLE' | 'AUTH_MISCONFIGURED', statusCode: 500 }`;
  - `cause` = the original error (already redacted for infrastructure errors).

  It is not intrinsic, so Nest logs it, `[cause]` included (LEAD-V31), and the details stay in server logs. Nest's external exception handler logs every non-intrinsic error **per resolver invocation**, so 500 aliased root fields during an outage would write 500 ERROR entries for one request. When the guard reports `repeated: true` (an earlier invocation of the same request key already surfaced this error, §7.1), `toInternalException` returns `BetterAuthGraphqlRepeatedInternalError` instead: the same message and `extensions`, but intrinsic, so the outage costs one ERROR line per request `[R3:SEC-r3-08]`.

- **Field resolvers are nested and inherit** `[R2:NEST-r2-04, SEC-r2-09]` `[R3:NEST-r3-05]` `[R4:NEST-r4-01]`. Outside federation, a field resolver (`RESOLVER_PROPERTY_METADATA`, `'graphql:resolve_property'`) runs only inside an operation whose root field the guard already authorized. In a federation subgraph it may also run under `_entities`, where the enclosing decision comes from the entity type's guarded reference resolver, or, when there is none, its `inherit` plan fails with `NO_ENCLOSING_DECISION` ("Federation entry points" below, §7.1). The GraphQL transports' `defaultAccessFor` answers `'inherit'` for it, which makes it a nested handler: class-level access, acceptance and requirements on its resolver class do not apply to it (§7.6 step 3), and a field resolver **without method-level access, acceptance or requirement metadata** gets an `inherit` plan: when field guards run, the guard returns at once, with no I/O and no decision. v2 gave it `defaultAccess` instead, so the moment an app enabled `fieldResolverEnhancers: ['guards']` (the fix B16 itself suggested), every undecorated field resolver demanded authentication and every public query that traversed one failed for anonymous callers, once per list item (REV2-NEST:`exp2-field-resolver-default-access.mjs`, identical on 11.1.17/13.2.4 and 12.0.1/14.0.0: `data: null`, `UNAUTHENTICATED` at `posts.0.author`). A field resolver that declares its own access (`@RequireAuth()`, `@OptionalAuth()`, `@Public()`), acceptance or requirements **at method level** gets a real plan and is enforced per field; its guard run shares the principal memo, so only its decisions add work (one per field per item, with policy I/O deduped by inputs). `@CurrentSession()` in an inheriting field resolver reads its enclosing field's reading through the lineage (§7.8).

  **Class-level metadata reaches the operations only** `[R3:NEST-r3-05]`. `@Resolver(() => Project) @RequireOrgMember({ organization: fromParam('orgId') })` protects the class's queries, mutations and subscriptions, which carry `orgId`, and not its `tasks` field resolver, which inherits from whichever operation reached it. That is how Nest applications use class-level guards on resolvers in practice (field resolvers get enhancers only with `fieldResolverEnhancers`, whose default is `[]`), and it keeps a class-level requirement from running once per field per list item. v3 applied the class level to field resolvers: boot failed by default for that pattern, following the hint made every item answer 403 (a field resolver has no `orgId` argument), and neither `@Public()` (B15 `PUBLIC_READS_PRINCIPAL`) nor `@OptionalAuth()` (a real plan again) was an escape. A field that exposes data its operations do not authorize, such as `salary` on an `Employee` reachable from several queries, carries its own method-level requirement. The GraphQL units' `advise()` prints `I_CLASS_METADATA_OPERATIONS_ONLY` (info, once per resolver class, capped) for resolver classes that carry class-level access, acceptance or requirements and also field resolvers without method-level metadata, so the scope of each class-level declaration is visible at boot (§17 Q30, RK29).

  An inheriting field resolver is as open as the operation that reaches it. The GraphQL units' `advise()` therefore warns `W_FIELD_RESOLVER_INHERITS` when a schema has `@Public()` or `@OptionalAuth()` root fields and inheriting field resolvers, listing both (capped), with the hint to put `@RequireAuth()` (plus `fieldResolverEnhancers: ['guards']`) on a field resolver that must never be served anonymously; B22 counts inheriting handlers separately.

- **Field-resolver coverage** `[R1:NEST-r1-06, SEC-r1-10]`. `@ResolveField` resolvers get guards only when `fieldResolverEnhancers` includes `'guards'`; the default is `[]` (LEAD-V30). A method-level requirement on a field resolver is otherwise silently not enforced. For example, `@RequirePermission({ salary: ['read'] }) @ResolveField() salary()` would leak salaries to any authenticated caller who reaches an `Employee` through another query.

  The GraphQL transports' `validate()` reads the driver options with `moduleRef.get(GRAPHQL_MODULE_OPTIONS, { strict: false })` (`'GqlModuleOptions'`, exported by `@nestjs/graphql` 13 and 14) and claims handlers (§5.4 B16): root resolver methods (`RESOLVER_TYPE_METADATA`) as `'global'`, field resolvers as `'global'` when `'guards'` is present and `'none'` otherwise, with code `FIELD_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`, the hint `fieldResolverEnhancers: ['guards', 'interceptors']` (or remove the method-level declaration so that the field resolver inherits), and severity `fieldResolverCoverage`, each with its `@Args` names as inputs. Core then fails boot for a field resolver with a real, non-public plan that no guard can reach; inheriting ones are covered by definition, and class-level metadata no longer turns a field resolver into a real plan.

- **Federation entry points** `[R4:NEST-r4-01]` `[R4:NEST decision]`. In a federation subgraph, the router's `_entities` query reaches an entity type's fields without any root resolver the guard runs for: @apollo/subgraph calls the type's `@ResolveReference()` handler once per representation, or, when the type has none, uses the representation itself as the entity, and then runs the type's field resolvers. v4 knew only root and field resolvers. A reference resolver carries neither `RESOLVER_TYPE_METADATA` at method level nor `RESOLVER_PROPERTY_METADATA`, so no unit claimed it, and it gets guards only through `fieldResolverEnhancers` (LEAD-V55): an anonymous `{ _entities(representations: [{ __typename: "User", id: "1" }]) { ... on User { email secretNote } } }` returned the data the `user(id)` query denied, while B16 passed; with field guards every representation shared one `info`, so v4's per-invocation decisions were reused across entities, and `fromParam` found no arguments (REV4-NEST:`exp1-federation-reference.mjs`). The GraphQL units now treat federation as follows, all inside the units:
  - **Reference resolvers are entry points.** A method with `RESOLVER_REFERENCE_METADATA` (imported from `@nestjs/graphql`) is never nested: `defaultAccessFor` does not answer `'inherit'` for it, so class-level access, acceptance and requirements and `defaultAccess` apply. `validate()` claims it with `everyHandler`, as `'global'` when `fieldResolverEnhancers` includes `'guards'` and `'none'` otherwise, code `REFERENCE_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`, hint "`fieldResolverEnhancers: ['guards', 'interceptors']`, or `@Public()` on the reference resolver", severity `federationCoverage`.
  - **Federation subgraphs need field guards.** When the driver's class chain names a federation driver, or any handler carries `@ResolveReference()`, and the schema has field or reference resolvers, `validate()` requires `fieldResolverEnhancers` to include `'guards'` (`FEDERATION_FIELD_GUARDS_REQUIRED`, severity `federationCoverage`): only a guard run can tell, at request time, that a field resolver under `_entities` has no authorized entry point (below). `'warn'` suits a subgraph that only an authenticating router can reach, which the library cannot observe (§17 Q36, RK34).
  - **Each representation is an invocation.** For a reference resolver, `describe()` takes the representation (`gql.getRoot()`; `GqlExecutionContext` normalizes @apollo/subgraph's three-argument call, and the Mercurius federation driver passes four) as `invocation`, so each entity gets its own decisions (T7), and `param(name)` reads the representation's fields. Param factories, which get raw arguments, apply the same normalization.
  - **Positions per entity type.** A reference resolver records its reading at `'<op>:_entities#<__typename>'`, and `enclosing(args)` of a field under `_entities.N` yields that position, taken from the `typename` of the path entry below the list index, before `'<op>:_entities'`. Representations of one type share the position and the plan, so their readings are identical (T6); two types in one `_entities` call never share one.
  - **No entry point, no data.** A field resolver of an entity type that has no reference resolver runs under `_entities` with no enclosing reading. Its `inherit` plan then fails with `NO_ENCLOSING_DECISION` (§7.1) instead of serving `@Parent()` data built from attacker-chosen representations; a field resolver with its own method-level access is judged on its own plan. The error names the type and the hint "add a guarded `@ResolveReference()` for this type, or declare access on the field resolver".
  - **Advice.** `W_FIELD_RESOLVER_INHERITS` counts `@Public()` and `@OptionalAuth()` reference resolvers as public entry points.

  Mercurius federation is **UNVERIFIED at runtime** (RK3); `T-reference-resolver` pins both drivers before 1.0.

- **Versions.** `@nestjs/graphql` 13 serves Nest 11 and 14 serves Nest 12. Version 14 removed `subscriptions-transport-ws`, so only `graphql-ws` is supported.

|                                   | Apollo (`apolloTransport()`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Mercurius (`mercuriusTransport()`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Request over HTTP                 | `gql.req`; the driver guarantees `req` (`apollo-base.driver.js:196-216`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `gql.req` (Nest's default `(req) => ({ req })`), else `gql.reply.request`                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Response over HTTP                | Express `req.res`; Fastify `responseFor(req)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `gql.reply`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Recognizing a WebSocket operation | `context.req` has `connectionParams` and `extra.request` (default context), or `context.req` / `context.extra?.request` carries `upgrade: websocket` (custom context)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `_connectionInit`, or the upgrade request stored by `mercuriusSubscriptionContext()`                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Recognizing an HTTP operation     | `kit.http.isRequest(context.req)` and, where implemented, `isLive` (`GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_STALE_REQUEST`); neither shape → `GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_UNRECOGNIZED` `[R3:SEC-r3-05]` `[R4:SEC-r4-03]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `kit.http.isRequest(context.reply?.request)` and `isLive`; neither shape → `GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_UNRECOGNIZED`                                                                                                                                                                |
| Checks at boot                    | the driver's class chain names no Mercurius driver; `context`, when set, is a function (`GRAPHQL_STATIC_CONTEXT`) `[R4:SEC-r4-03]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | the driver's class chain names no Apollo driver; `context`, when set, is a function                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Federation                        | `ApolloFederationDriver`: reference resolvers called with `(reference, context, info)`, claimed as entry points; field guards required (`FEDERATION_FIELD_GUARDS_REQUIRED`) `[R4:NEST-r4-01]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `MercuriusFederationDriver`: reference resolvers called with `(reference, {}, context, info)`; same rules; **UNVERIFIED at runtime**                                                                                                                                     |
| Credentials over a WebSocket      | graphql-ws context `{ connectionParams, extra: { request } }`. Headers = `toWebHeaders(extra.request.headers)`, then `connectionParams` keys in `connectionParamHeaders` (default `authorization`, `cookie`) **replace** same-named headers, or `subscriptionCredentials(ctx)` plus the upgrade request's `host`/`x-forwarded-*` unless it sets them `[R4:BA-r4-03]`. **UNVERIFIED at runtime** (R:nest-di §4.2) | `gql._connectionInit` payload + the upgrade request exposed by `mercuriusSubscriptionContext()` under a `Symbol.for` key, same replacement rule. **UNVERIFIED at runtime**; Mercurius subscriptions ship as _preview_ until `T-subscription-credentials` passes (§17 Q7) |
| Browser leg over a WebSocket      | `extra.request` (Origin, cookie), its own headers only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | the upgrade request                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Cookies over a WebSocket          | `null`, refresh suppressed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `null`, refresh suppressed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Subscription lifetime             | the guard runs once per subscription start, not per event; revalidation during a long-lived subscription is out of scope for 1.0 (§17 Q11)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | same                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

### 9.3 WebSockets: socket.io and ws (`./websockets`)

**Credentials:**

- **socket.io** `[A][B][C]` takes them from `client.handshake.headers`. The handshake is an HTTP request, so it carries cookies for same-site browsers or with `withCredentials`. Then `credentials(client)` supplies more and **replaces** same-named headers, for example `handshake.auth.token` → `authorization: Bearer <token>` for the `bearer()` plugin. The default mapping copies `handshake.auth.token` when no `authorization` header exists. The mapping feeds the principal sources only; the browser leg of the origin check stays the handshake's own headers (§7.10) `[R2:SEC-r2-01]`.
- **ws** `[B][C]` has a problem: the bare `WebSocket` has no headers, and the upgrade request is passed only to the `connection` event (`@nestjs/platform-ws` `adapters/ws-adapter.js:144`). `withUpgradeRequest(Base)` is a mixin over any `WsAdapter` subclass. It overrides `bindClientConnect(server, cb)` and records `{ headers: toWebHeaders(request.headers), url, remoteAddress, encrypted }` on the client under `UPGRADE_REQUEST` before delegating. A mixin composes with users' own adapters (Redis, custom) and needs no `@nestjs/platform-ws` import. Custom adapters call `recordUpgradeRequest(client, request)` directly.

  ```ts
  app.useWebSocketAdapter(new (withUpgradeRequest(WsAdapter))(app)); // main.ts
  ```

  A guarded message from a client without a recorded request throws `BetterAuthConfigurationError`, which includes this snippet.

**Origin check: Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking** `[R1:BA-r1-03, SEC-r1-01]`. Browsers attach cookies to WebSocket upgrades, and CORS does not apply to them. A malicious page can open `new WebSocket('wss://api.example.com/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket')`, the victim's cookie authenticates the socket, and the page reads every reply. The browser leg is the handshake (socket.io `handshake.headers` and `handshake.url`; ws the recorded upgrade request), and `enforce` is always true. Every message on a socket whose handshake carried a cookie is therefore allowed only if the handshake's `Origin` is trusted by better-auth (§7.10), whatever `handshake.auth` holds: a cross-site page that adds a junk `auth.token` no longer switches the check off while the victim's cookie authenticates (REV2-SEC:`probe-origin-bearer-exempt.mjs`) `[R2:SEC-r2-01]`. Sockets whose handshake carries no cookie (native and server clients with tokens) are unaffected. The verdict is computed once per socket, from an absolute URL built with `upgradeRequestUrl()` (socket.io `handshake.secure` and `handshake.url`; ws the recorded `encrypted` flag and `url`) `[R2:SEC-r2-05]`.

**Memo, revalidation and decorators.**

- `principalTtlMs: 0` is the default `[A][C]`. Each guarded message resolves once, memoized across the guards of that message through the shared `args` array (LEAD-V7). With the session source this adds no writes, because refresh is suppressed. Sources that consume quota or write per resolution (`effects`, for example `apiKeyPrincipal()`, which writes the usage counter) verify on every message. The WS units' `advise()` warns `W_QUOTA_PER_MESSAGE` when such a source is registered and `principalTtlMs` is 0, and recommends connection-time authentication plus a TTL `[R1:SEC-r1-14]`.
- `principalTtlMs > 0` caches **authenticated and absent** results per socket (`call.connection`) for chat-style traffic. Rejections and infrastructure failures are never cached on the socket (§7.2). Handlers with authoritative freshness (`@RequirePermission`, `@RequireAuth({ authoritative: true })`) never use the TTL, so a banned admin loses admin access on the next message `[R2:SEC-r2-07]`. Decisions are always per message, so a socket that joined org A cannot reuse that allow to join org B `[R1:NEST-r1-01]`. The docs state the revocation delay a TTL implies for other handlers.
- Param decorators read the resolution from the scope interceptor. The socket is deliberately **not** used as a carrier, because concurrent messages on one socket would race (§7.8).

**Guard behavior by Nest major** (LEAD-V6, LEAD-V29, R:nest-di §3.4 runtime table):

|                                                            | Nest 11 | Nest 12                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `APP_GUARD` runs for `@SubscribeMessage` handlers          | **no**  | yes                                                     |
| `APP_INTERCEPTOR` wraps them                               | **no**  | yes                                                     |
| An `HttpException` thrown by a guard reaches the client as | n/a     | `{ status: 'error', message: 'Internal server error' }` |
| Global exception filters apply to gateways                 | no      | no                                                      |

**Design consequences** `[C]` `[R1:NEST-r1-13, SEC-r1-12]`:

1. The WS transports always throw `WsException({ status: 'error', statusCode, code, reason, message })` themselves. `BaseWsExceptionFilter` emits an object payload as-is, and filters never reach gateways (R:nest-di §5.2).
2. **Every gateway needs `@UseBetterAuth()` (or `@Public()`), on both majors.** v1 skipped the requirement on Nest 12 through a capability probe (`AbstractHttpAdapter.prototype.mapException`). That API belongs to `@nestjs/core`, while the behavior is decided by `@nestjs/websockets` (`getContextCreator(container)` on 11.1.17 vs `getContextCreator(container, config, …)` on 12.0.1, LEAD-V29). The probe could therefore report "covered" for a skewed install (core 12 with websockets 11), or for an 11.x release that backported the HTTP API, and leave every gateway open. A probe of `@nestjs/websockets` itself would need a deep import of an unexported module whose specifier differs between the two majors' packaging. v2 dropped the probe. The WS transports' `validate()` enumerates gateway classes through Nest's `'websockets:is_gateway'` class metadata (LEAD-V13) and their message handlers through `'websockets:message_mapping'` method metadata (neither re-exported from the package root, LEAD-V42; both checked by a canary at boot and pinned by a CI test on both majors), and **claims** every message handler as `'explicit'` with `everyHandler`, code `GATEWAY_UNGUARDED` and severity `gatewayCoverage` (§5.4 B16) `[R2:NEST-r2-02, NEST-r2-12]`. Core then fails boot for any handler that has neither `@Public()` nor `@UseBetterAuth()` at class or method level, with the hint: "Add @UseBetterAuth() to ChatGateway (or @Public() to opt out). Global guards and interceptors do not reach gateways on NestJS 11, and this check does not depend on the version."
   - **Guard and interceptor.** An `'explicit'` claim is covered only by `@UseBetterAuth()` or by both `@UseGuards(BetterAuthGuard)` and `@UseInterceptors(BetterAuthScopeInterceptor)`. v2 accepted `@UseGuards(BetterAuthGuard)` alone; on Nest 11 no global interceptor reaches a gateway and WS has no carrier, so `@CurrentSession()` threw `NO_AUTH_RESULT` on every message, and direct `auth.api` calls in the handler slid the session without suppression (NEST-r2-11). The literal `'__interceptors__'` is pinned next to `'__guards__'` (§12.4).
   - **A renamed key cannot pass vacuously** `[R2:NEST-r2-12]` `[R3:NEST-r3-08]`. Before they enumerate, the WS units run a canary: they apply `@WebSocketGateway()` and `@SubscribeMessage('probe')` from the installed `@nestjs/websockets` to a private probe class and read `'websockets:is_gateway'` and `'websockets:message_mapping'` back. A mismatch fails boot with `NEST_METADATA_KEY_CHANGED` (B16). A gateway without message handlers is then genuinely one, such as a push-only gateway that only emits through `@WebSocketServer()`, and is not claimed. v3 claimed the class of any gateway with non-lifecycle methods and no discovered handler, so `NotificationsGateway { notifyUser() {} }` failed boot with `GATEWAY_UNGUARDED` and a misleading hint, and the workaround inflated the public count.

   On Nest 12 with a global guard the second guard run is a memo hit, with no extra I/O and no log line.

3. **Connection-time authentication** `[B]` `[R1:NEST-r1-12]`. Guards never run on connect (`handleConnection` is never guarded). The socket.io and ws definitions provide `WsConnectionAuth` and export it under `WS_CONNECTION_AUTH` (`ExtensionDefinition.exports`, re-exported globally by the default `forRoot`). It reuses the transport's credential mapping, applies the origin check to the handshake, resolves with refresh suppressed, and caches authenticated/absent results on the client for `principalTtlMs`. It takes an `instance` option for named instances:

   ```ts
   @WebSocketGateway()
   @UseBetterAuth()
   export class ChatGateway implements OnGatewayInit, OnGatewayConnection {
     constructor(
       @Inject(WS_CONNECTION_AUTH) private readonly wsAuth: WsConnectionAuth,
     ) {}
     afterInit(server: Server) {
       server.use(this.wsAuth.socketIoMiddleware({ required: true }));
     } // socket.io
   }
   // ws: async handleConnection(client) {
   //   const r = await this.wsAuth.authenticate(client);
   //   if (r.outcome !== 'authenticated') client.close(r.outcome === 'rejected' ? wsCloseCodeFor(r.failure) : 4401, 'UNAUTHENTICATED');
   // }
   ```

4. **`param(name)`** reads `switchToWs().getData()?.[name]`.

### 9.4 Microservices / RPC (`./microservices`) `[A][B][C]`

RPC messages have no cookies of their own and no browser leg; credentials travel in transport metadata. `rpcTransport({ carriers })` handles every `'rpc'` context. Its `describe()` uses the first carrier whose `matches(ctx)` is true (default: `defaultCarriers`); when none matches, the message carries no credentials: `headers()` returns empty `Headers`, a required handler answers 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, and a public one runs. v2 made a carrier match part of `handles()`, so a credential-less TCP or Redis message (no `auth` object in the payload) answered 500 `NO_TRANSPORT`, public handlers included (NEST-r2-03) `[R2:NEST-r2-03]`:

| Carrier                             | Matches                                                             | Credential source (headers copied into `Headers`)                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grpcCarrier()`                     | `getArgByIndex(1)` is a gRPC `Metadata` (duck-typed `get`/`getMap`) | metadata entries (`authorization`, `cookie`, `x-api-key`)                                                                                                                                         |
| `natsCarrier()`                     | the context has `getHeaders()`                                      | NATS message headers                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `kafkaCarrier()`                    | the context has `getMessage().headers`                              | Kafka headers (Buffer values decoded as UTF-8)                                                                                                                                                    |
| `rmqCarrier()`                      | the context has `getMessage().properties`                           | `properties.headers`                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `mqttCarrier()`                     | the context has `getPacket()`                                       | MQTT 5 `userProperties` (MQTT 3 has no headers)                                                                                                                                                   |
| `payloadCarrier({ field: 'auth' })` | the payload has an object at `field`                                | `data.auth` (TCP and Redis carry no headers). The docs warn this is weaker: credentials are visible to every hop. A primitive payload or one without the field matches no carrier: no credentials |

- **Credentials** are ordinary better-auth credentials: `authorization: Bearer <session token>` with the `bearer()` plugin, a `cookie` header, or `x-api-key`. `getSession` and `apiKeyPrincipal()` work unchanged (keys still need a route that accepts `'api-key'`, §7.6). Forwarding browser cookies between services is discouraged.
- **Memo key, invocation and carrier:** `switchToRpc().getContext()`, one object per message. **Cookies:** `null`, so refresh is suppressed. **Browser leg:** none, so the origin check never applies: no browser can send an RPC message. **No `Host`:** carriers copy no host, so every `auth.api` call made for an RPC message is host-less; the unit declares `requires.hostlessCalls`, and a dynamic `baseURL` without `fallback` fails boot (B20) instead of answering 500 per message `[R2:BA-r2-05]`.
- **Denial:** `new RpcException({ status: 'error', statusCode, code, reason, message })`. `BaseRpcExceptionFilter` passes an `RpcException` object through as-is and turns anything else into "Internal server error".
- **gRPC:** the carrier's `toException` returns `RpcException({ code: 16 | 7 | 8, message })` (UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED). On Nest 12, if `@nestjs/microservices` exports `GrpcUnauthenticatedException` / `GrpcPermissionDeniedException`, the carrier uses them. That is feature-detected by export presence inside the RPC unit, not in core. **UNVERIFIED at runtime** on Nest 11 (grpc-js reads `code` from the error object).
- **Guard registration and hybrid coverage** `[R1:NEST-r1-05, SEC-r1-09]` `[R2:NEST-r2-02, NEST-r2-11]`. Standalone microservices (`createMicroservice`) apply `APP_GUARD`. A hybrid app's `connectMicroservice(options)` gets a **fresh** `ApplicationConfig` unless `{ inheritAppConfig: true }` is passed (LEAD-V32), so without it `APP_GUARD` never runs for `@MessagePattern`/`@EventPattern` handlers and any publisher can invoke them unauthenticated. The RPC transport's `validate()` claims every message and event handler, found through `'microservices:pattern'` method metadata (not re-exported from the package root, LEAD-V32; checked at boot by a canary that applies `@MessagePattern('probe')` to a private probe class, and pinned by a CI test on both majors), and core's coverage rule makes this fail closed (§5.4 B16):
  - without an HTTP adapter (a standalone microservice), or when the user asserts `rpcTransport({ inheritAppConfig: true })`, handlers are claimed `'global'`;
  - with an HTTP adapter and no assertion, they are claimed `'explicit'` with `everyHandler`, code `RPC_HANDLER_UNGUARDED` and severity `hybridCoverage`: every handler needs `@UseBetterAuth()` (guard and interceptor, so direct calls in the handler get refresh suppression) or `@Public()`;
  - the unit cannot observe `connectMicroservice` itself, so the assertion is the user's. Its `advise()` prints what the assertion means at every boot (RK22);
  - an app that **forgot** `rpcTransport()` in a hybrid app has nobody claiming its message handlers: any of them whose metadata is on B16's trigger list fails boot with core's `UNGUARDED_AUTH_METADATA`, naming the registered transports (NEST-r2-02);
  - duplicate guard runs (global plus `@UseBetterAuth()`) are memo hits. `'warn' | 'off'` relaxes the transport's own check.
- **`param(name)`** reads `switchToRpc().getData()?.[name]`.

### 9.5 Summary: guard reach, cookie capability, origin check, error delivery

| Transport                                                                                            | Guard reaches it                                                                                                                                                     | Cookies | Refresh    | Origin check (cookie on the browser leg)                                         | Denial                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| HTTP controllers (Express, Fastify)                                                                  | 11 ✓ / 12 ✓ (with `globalGuard: false`, `@UseBetterAuth()` where the plan declares something, boot-checked)                                                          | ✓       | normal     | unsafe methods carrying a cookie; handlers that forward auth cookies (form rule) | `HttpException` + payload                                    |
| GraphQL query/mutation over HTTP (Apollo, Mercurius)                                                 | 11 ✓ / 12 ✓ (root fields; field resolvers inherit, or declare their own access and are boot-checked; federation reference resolvers with field guards, boot-checked) | ✓       | normal     | mutations carrying a cookie                                                      | `BetterAuthGraphqlDenial` (`extensions.code`)                |
| GraphQL over a WebSocket (subscriptions; queries and mutations over graphql-ws or `fullWsTransport`) | 11 ✓ / 12 ✓ (per operation)                                                                                                                                          | ✗       | suppressed | every operation, when the upgrade request carries a cookie                       | `BetterAuthGraphqlDenial`                                    |
| WS socket.io / ws                                                                                    | `@UseBetterAuth()` on both majors (boot-checked)                                                                                                                     | ✗       | suppressed | every message, when the handshake carries a cookie                               | `WsException({ status, statusCode, code, reason, message })` |
| RPC standalone                                                                                       | 11 ✓ / 12 ✓                                                                                                                                                          | ✗       | suppressed | never (no browser leg)                                                           | `RpcException` / gRPC status                                 |
| RPC hybrid                                                                                           | `inheritAppConfig` (asserted) or `@UseBetterAuth()` (boot-checked)                                                                                                   | ✗       | suppressed | never                                                                            | same                                                         |

## 10. Hooks

### 10.1 Why a plugin (S1) `[A][B][C]`

The reference library wraps `auth.options.hooks.before/after` and `databaseHooks` _after_ `betterAuth()` has run. That works only because `ctx.options` is a shallow copy that shares the nested objects, which is why users had to pre-declare `hooks: {}` (R:ref-impl §5.2; reference issues #42 and #103; PR #138 broke it with `{ source, hooks }`). The wrappers also drop return values, so `{ context }` rewrites, short-circuits and DB `false`/`{ data }` all stop working.

better-auth's documented alternative is a plugin:

- plugin `hooks.before/after` are **arrays of matcher + handler** (`CORE/types/plugin.ts:89-100`);
- plugins contribute database hooks through `init() → { options: { databaseHooks } }` (LEAD-V4);
- the docs say "if you need to reuse a hook across multiple endpoints, consider creating a plugin" (`docs/concepts/hooks.mdx:326-328`).

`betterAuth()` cannot take plugins after construction (R:ba-core §2.1), so the user adds `nestjs()` in `auth.ts`. Nest-discovered hooks bind to it late, through a registry. Nothing in `auth.options` is ever written.

### 10.2 The plugin (`./plugin`)

```ts
// imports only better-auth/api, better-auth/cookies and defu — never @nestjs/*, never node:* (runtime-agnostic; CI-enforced)
import {
  createAuthMiddleware,
  setShouldSkipSessionRefresh,
} from "better-auth/api";
import { parseCookies } from "better-auth/cookies";

const HANDLE = Symbol.for("nestjs-slightly-better-auth:bridge");

/** Versioned protocol object on the plugin instance; core finds it via (await auth.$context).getPlugin(id)[HANDLE]. [B][C] */
export interface BridgeHandle {
  readonly protocol: 4; // checked by core (B04); v5: binding state and instance, the caller-session check [R4:SEC-r4-01, SEC-r4-02, BA-r4-05]
  readonly clientIpHeader: string | null; // single source of truth for the header name (§6.8)
  /** 'unbound' until the first bind(); 'bound' while an application's hooks are registered; 'closed' after its shutdown, hooks still registered. */
  readonly state: "unbound" | "bound" | "closed";
  /** Endpoint dispatches and database-hook dispatches (writes) seen before the first binding, reset by every bind() (B26). */
  readonly unboundDispatches: number;
  /**
   * Registers the application's hooks and returns close(), which the kernel calls in onApplicationShutdown: a closed binding keeps
   * dispatching until another application binds (§10.6). A second bind() from the same owner for the same instance is a no-op that
   * returns the existing registration (NestMicroservice.init() runs lifecycle hooks twice); from the same owner for another instance it
   * throws PLUGIN_SHARED_BETWEEN_INSTANCES (B03). Throws INSTANCE_ALREADY_BOUND if another bootstrapped application is bound; takes over
   * a never-bootstrapped one (reported, B06) and a closed one (silently). [R2:NEST-r2-05] [R4:SEC-r4-01, BA-r4-05]
   */
  bind(binding: BridgeBinding): { close(): void; tookOverFrom?: string };
  /** true when an endpoint returned `value` (an object) in a non-router dispatch observed while bound; false for before-hook short-circuits (LEAD-V37). */
  producedByEndpoint(value: unknown): boolean;
}
export interface BridgeBinding {
  /** The application: compared by identity for the same-owner no-op; `description` goes into the B06 message. */
  readonly owner: { readonly description: string };
  /** The instance this plugin object serves; one plugin object serves one instance (B03). [R4:BA-r4-05] */
  readonly instance: string;
  /** 'initialized' at bind; the kernel sets 'bootstrapped' in onApplicationBootstrap; close() sets 'closed'. [R4:SEC-r4-01] */
  state: "initialized" | "bootstrapped" | "closed";
  /** View of the kernel's RequestScope; the plugin never owns an AsyncLocalStorage. [C] */
  current(): ScopeView | undefined;
  /** Credential header names declared by the instance's principal sources (credential matching, §7.5). */
  readonly credentialHeaders: readonly string[];
  readonly before: readonly CompiledHook[]; // sorted by order, then discovery order
  readonly after: readonly CompiledHook[];
  readonly database: Readonly<
    Record<
      DatabaseHookTarget,
      {
        readonly before: readonly DbBeforeFn[];
        readonly after: readonly DbAfterFn[];
      }
    >
  >;
  /** Debug log when the bridge drops a direct call's cookies because its credential is foreign. */
  onDropped(path: string): void;
}
export interface ScopeView {
  readonly cookies: CookieSink | null;
  readonly forward: "none" | "same-credential" | "any";
  readonly inbound: (() => Headers) | undefined;
  readonly internal: boolean;
  /**
   * Present in a handler scope whose browser leg enforces the origin check and carries a cookie, unless the plan's origin check is 'off'
   * (§7.5). Returns when this leg has a passing origin verdict for `instance` or better-auth's flags disable the check; otherwise throws the
   * kernel's BetterAuthConfigurationError PUBLIC_HANDLER_USED_CALLER_SESSION. [R4:SEC-r4-02]
   */
  readonly checkCallerSession?: (path: string, instance: string) => void;
}
export interface CompiledHook {
  /**
   * A throwing user predicate makes matches() return TRUE, so that run() rethrows it: as APIError 500 from before-hooks
   * (better-auth logs and converts before-hook matcher throws) and raw from after-hooks (better-auth propagates them),
   * LEAD-V23. v1 returned false and silently skipped the hook. [R1:BA-r1-06]
   */
  matches(ctx: HookEndpointContext, scope: ScopeView | undefined): boolean;
  run(ctx: HookEndpointContext): Promise<unknown>;
}

export function nestjs(options: NestjsPluginOptions = {}) {
  let binding: BridgeBinding | null = null; // never reset to null: a closed binding keeps its hooks [R4:SEC-r4-01]
  let unboundDispatches = 0;
  const endpointResults = new WeakSet<object>(); // objects endpoints returned; after-hooks never run for a short-circuit
  const scope = () => binding?.current();
  const isRouter = (ctx: object) =>
    "_flag" in ctx && (ctx as { _flag?: string })._flag === "router";
  const clientIpHeader =
    options.clientIpHeader === false
      ? null
      : (options.clientIpHeader ??
        `x-nsba-ip-${globalThis.crypto.randomUUID().replaceAll("-", "")}`); // per plugin instance (per nestjs() call), process-local [R1:SEC-r1-18]
  const handle: BridgeHandle = {
    protocol: 4,
    clientIpHeader,
    get state() {
      return binding === null
        ? "unbound"
        : binding.state === "closed"
          ? "closed"
          : "bound";
    },
    get unboundDispatches() {
      return unboundDispatches;
    },
    bind(b) {
      if (binding && binding.owner === b.owner) {
        if (binding.instance !== b.instance)
          throw new Error(
            `PLUGIN_SHARED_BETWEEN_INSTANCES: '${binding.instance}' and '${b.instance}'`,
          );
        const same = binding;
        return {
          close: () => {
            same.state = "closed";
          },
        };
      }
      if (binding?.state === "bootstrapped")
        throw new Error(
          `INSTANCE_ALREADY_BOUND: bound to ${binding.owner.description}`,
        );
      const tookOverFrom =
        binding?.state === "initialized"
          ? binding.owner.description
          : undefined; // a failed init(): kernel warns; a closed app: silent
      binding = b;
      unboundDispatches = 0;
      return {
        tookOverFrom,
        close: () => {
          b.state = "closed";
        },
      };
    },
    producedByEndpoint: (value) =>
      typeof value === "object" && value !== null && endpointResults.has(value),
  };
  return {
    id: "nestjs-slightly-better-auth",
    [HANDLE]: handle,
    init: () => ({
      options: {
        databaseHooks: createDatabaseDispatchers(
          () => binding,
          () => {
            unboundDispatches++;
          },
        ), // 4 models × 3 ops × before/after (§10.6); counts writes before the first binding
        ...(clientIpHeader
          ? { advanced: { ipAddress: { ipAddressHeaders: [clientIpHeader] } } }
          : {}), // default; user wins (§6.8)
      },
    }),
    hooks: {
      before: [
        {
          // 1. refresh suppression: every non-router endpoint dispatched from a cookie-less scope (§7.4); also counts dispatches before the first binding
          matcher: (ctx) => {
            if (!binding) {
              unboundDispatches++;
              return false;
            }
            return !isRouter(ctx) && scope()?.cookies === null;
          },
          handler: createAuthMiddleware(async () => {
            await setShouldSkipSessionRefresh(true);
          }),
        },
        {
          // 2. caller-session check: a direct call that carries the scope's own session-token cookie, in a scope whose unsafe browser leg
          //    carries a cookie; the kernel's check throws unless the guard verified the leg's origin (§7.5) [R4:SEC-r4-02]
          matcher: (ctx) => {
            const s = scope();
            return (
              !isRouter(ctx) &&
              !!s?.checkCallerSession &&
              !s.internal &&
              carriesInboundSession(ctx, s)
            );
          },
          handler: createAuthMiddleware(async (ctx) => {
            scope()!.checkCallerSession!(ctx.path, binding!.instance);
          }),
        },
        {
          // 3. Nest @BeforeAuth dispatcher
          matcher: (ctx) =>
            binding?.before.some((h) => h.matches(ctx, scope())) ?? false,
          handler: createAuthMiddleware((ctx) =>
            runBefore(binding!, ctx, scope()),
          ),
        },
      ],
      after: [
        {
          // 4. Nest @AfterAuth dispatcher
          matcher: (ctx) =>
            binding?.after.some((h) => h.matches(ctx, scope())) ?? false,
          handler: createAuthMiddleware((ctx) =>
            runAfter(binding!, ctx, scope()),
          ),
        },
        {
          // 5. endpoint-result observer: records the final returned object of a non-router dispatch; a before-hook short-circuit skips
          //    every after-hook, so a session a hook supplied is never recorded (LEAD-V37, LEAD-EXP-8) [R2:BA-r2-06]
          matcher: (ctx) => binding !== null && !isRouter(ctx),
          handler: createAuthMiddleware(async (ctx) => {
            const r = ctx.context.returned;
            if (typeof r === "object" && r !== null) endpointResults.add(r);
          }),
        },
        {
          // 6. cookie bridge (nextCookies pattern), only where the scope enables forwarding; last, so it also sees cookies Nest after-hooks set
          matcher: (ctx) => {
            const s = scope();
            return !isRouter(ctx) && !!s?.cookies && s.forward !== "none";
          },
          handler: createAuthMiddleware(async (ctx) => {
            const s = scope()!;
            if (
              s.forward === "same-credential" &&
              !sameCredential(ctx, s, binding!.credentialHeaders)
            ) {
              binding!.onDropped(ctx.path);
              return; // foreign credential: never hand it to this caller [R1:SEC-r1-03]
            }
            const setCookie = ctx.context.responseHeaders?.getSetCookie() ?? [];
            if (setCookie.length) s.cookies!.append(setCookie);
          }),
        },
      ],
    },
  } satisfies BetterAuthPlugin;
}

/** Session-token cookie (better-auth's own name and parser), authorization, and declared credential headers. */
const SEP = "\u0000"; // cannot occur in header values
const NO_CREDENTIAL = (extra: readonly string[]) =>
  SEP.repeat(extra.length + 1);
const sessionTokenOf = (
  headers: Headers | undefined,
  ctx: HookEndpointContext,
) =>
  parseCookies(headers?.get("cookie") ?? "").get(
    ctx.context.authCookies.sessionToken.name,
  ) ?? "";
function credentialOf(
  headers: Headers | undefined,
  ctx: HookEndpointContext,
  extra: readonly string[],
): string {
  if (!headers) return NO_CREDENTIAL(extra);
  return [
    sessionTokenOf(headers, ctx),
    headers.get("authorization") ?? "",
    ...extra.map((h) => headers.get(h) ?? ""),
  ].join(SEP);
}
function sameCredential(
  ctx: HookEndpointContext,
  s: ScopeView,
  extra: readonly string[],
): boolean {
  const call = credentialOf(ctx.headers, ctx, extra);
  return (
    call === NO_CREDENTIAL(extra) ||
    call === credentialOf(s.inbound?.(), ctx, extra)
  ); // login/sign-up, or the caller's own
}
function carriesInboundSession(
  ctx: HookEndpointContext,
  s: ScopeView,
): boolean {
  // the caller's own session cookie [R4:SEC-r4-02]
  const token = sessionTokenOf(ctx.headers, ctx);
  return token !== "" && token === sessionTokenOf(s.inbound?.(), ctx);
}
```

- **Entry order** follows `nextCookies` (`BA/integrations/next-js.ts:47-144`):
  - Suppression runs before any Nest before-hook. Nested `auth.api` calls made inside a hook share the dispatch's request state and inherit the flag.
  - The caller-session check runs before the Nest before-hooks, so no Nest hook acts on a call that is about to be refused. It reads the call's **original** headers, as every before-hook does (LEAD-V23), so the bearer plugin's cookie conversion never makes a bearer call look like a cookie call `[R4:SEC-r4-02]`.
  - The observer runs after the Nest after-hooks, so it records the value a Nest after-hook put in `ctx.context.returned`, which is the value the caller receives. It records only objects, in a `WeakSet` on the plugin instance, and costs one set insertion per non-router call while bound.
  - The cookie bridge runs after the Nest after-hooks, so it also forwards cookies they set with `ctx.setCookie`.
- **Placement** `[R1:BA-r1-07]`. The plugin must be **last** in `plugins`, the `nextCookies` rule: later plugins' after-hooks could set cookies the bridge never sees, because plugin hooks run in plugin order after `options.hooks` (LEAD-V1). B05 warns otherwise. Being last does **not** let Nest before-hooks see other plugins' before-hook effects (v1 wrongly said so). Every before-hook receives the original input, and `{ context }` results such as `bearer()`'s cookie conversion are merged only after all before-hooks ran (LEAD-V23). A before-hook that short-circuits pre-empts every later one and all after-hooks. For example, the api-key plugin answers `/get-session` itself when `enableSessionForAPIKeys` is on, so no Nest hook on `/get-session` runs for API-key callers (LEAD-V21).
- **Construction time only.** The plugin writes nothing into `auth.options` after construction. Its `init()` contributions are merged by better-auth itself during construction.
- **Fixed entries and a late-bound registry, not per-hook entries pushed at bind time** `[A][C]`. Pushing entries into our own `hooks.before` array at bind time would get better-auth's composition for free. It would, however, depend on better-auth re-reading plugin arrays on every dispatch. That is true in 1.7.4 (LEAD-V1: `getHooks` runs per dispatch) but is an implementation detail; if it were ever cached at init, every Nest hook would silently stop, which is the reference's #42 failure mode (ADR-07).
- **Runtime-agnostic** `[C]`. The plugin imports only `better-auth/api`, `better-auth/cookies` and `defu`, and uses Web Crypto for the header name. The `AsyncLocalStorage` lives in the kernel and is reached through `binding.current()`, so `auth.ts` stays loadable in every runtime better-auth supports, and by the better-auth CLI.
- **Inert only before the first binding** `[R4:SEC-r4-01]`. Until an application binds, all matchers return `false` and the DB dispatchers are no-ops, so the same `auth.ts` can be shared with scripts and non-Nest code; the pre-bind counter, which the first before-hook matcher and every DB dispatcher increment then, only feeds B26 `[R2:NEST-r2-10]`. Once bound, the plugin never becomes inert again: `onApplicationShutdown` closes the binding, and a closed binding dispatches the application's Nest hooks until another application binds (§10.6). v4 unbound the handle at shutdown, so background work a global module drained later in the same shutdown skipped every Nest hook, security rules included.
- **One plugin object, one instance** `[R4:BA-r4-05]`. The binding lives in the closure of one `nestjs()` call. Two `betterAuth()` calls that share one plugins array share that object, `getPlugin()` returns it to both, and its `init()` gives both instances database dispatchers over the same binding. B03 therefore fails boot when two instances resolve the same handle, and `bind()` throws for a second instance from the same application. v4 treated that second `bind()` as a repeated lifecycle call, so the second instance's Nest hooks never ran and the first instance's ran for its dispatches and writes (REV4-BA:`exp5-shared-plugin-object.mjs`).
- **Dual-package safety.** Core finds the handle through `getPlugin(id)`, which returns the user's own plugin object (EXP-B:E2, EXP-C1), under a `Symbol.for` key. A plugin imported from the ESM build and a kernel loaded from the CJS build still find each other.

### 10.3 Discovery and validation `[A][B][C]`

`HookBinder` runs in the core module's `onModuleInit`. Among non-global modules this runs first; other global modules imported before `BetterAuthModule` may run their `onModuleInit` earlier (LEAD-V27), which is why seeding belongs in `onApplicationBootstrap` and B26 reports calls made before binding `[R1:NEST-r1-11]`. Steps:

1. `discovery.getProviders()` across all modules. It is a full scan, because the `metadataKey` filter misses `useFactory`/`useValue` providers (R:nest-di §6.2). Wrappers without an instance and `isAlias` wrappers are skipped.
2. `MetadataScanner.getAllMethodNames(prototype)`, then read `Symbol.for(…:hook)` and `Symbol.for(…:db-hook)` metadata per method. No class marker is required `[C]`.
3. Validate:
   - a non-static provider (`wrapper.isDependencyTreeStatic() === false`) fails boot (B11), because discovery would see a prototype-only instance with no dependencies (R:nest-di §6.3);
   - unknown string patterns fail boot with a "did you mean" (B12);
   - an unknown `instance` fails boot;
   - the same class provided in two modules registers twice, and boot warns with both module names.
4. Compile matchers, bind `instance[method]` to the instance, sort by `order` ascending then discovery order, and bind the tables (plus the instance's source `credentialHeaders`) to each instance's plugin handle.

Lazily loaded modules are not discovered, because Nest gives them no lifecycle hooks. This is documented (risk RK7).

### 10.4 Matching `[A][B][C]`

- **Patterns.** `ctx.path` is the endpoint's **route pattern** (`'/callback/:id'`), not the concrete URL (`BA/api/dispatch.ts:348`). A string matches a pattern exactly. An array matches any of its patterns. A predicate `(ctx) => boolean` is the escape hatch for anything else. No argument means every endpoint. Pattern strings autocomplete from `EndpointPath` (§11.4) and are validated at boot against `auth.api[*].path`: 67 of 69 endpoints expose `.path` at runtime (EXP-C8).
- **`calls`.** `'http'` matches requests routed by `auth.handler` (`ctx._flag === 'router'`). `'server'` matches direct `auth.api.*` calls. `'all'` is the default.
- **`skipInternal`.** The library's own calls (the guard's `getSession`, policy checks) run in scopes marked `internal: true`, and `skipInternal: true` ignores them. The **default is `false`**, which is faithful to better-auth, where user hooks also run for server calls (R:ba-core §4.1). The docs warn that a path-less hook therefore runs on every guarded request, the unexplained "hooks run twice" of reference issue #103, and that `skipInternal: true` is the one-flag fix for audit-style hooks. Draft B's opposite default was rejected (ADR-08).
- **Security rules belong where every path passes** `[R1:BA-r1-07]` `[R2:BA-r2-07]`.
  - A `@BeforeAuth('/get-session')` that looks up the user from the request would fail open, because before-hooks see the original request (a bearer-token client presents no session cookie there) and the api-key short-circuit skips it entirely. A path-less `@BeforeAuth` is no alternative, for the same reason.
  - An `@AfterAuth('/get-session')` that inspects or replaces `ctx.context.returned` runs for cookie and bearer callers of **`getSession` dispatches**: the guard's resolution and every other `auth.api.getSession` call. It is therefore a place for rules that apply to **Nest routes only**. It does **not** reach better-auth's own endpoints: they resolve the session with `getSessionFromCtx`, which calls `getSession` as a plain function, and a plain call skips hooks (`BA/api/dispatch.ts:317-318`; LEAD-V36). A "suspended user" rule written this way answers 401 on Nest routes while the same cookie keeps working on `/update-user`, `/change-email`, `/organization/*` and `/api-key/create` through the mount (REV2-BA:`exp7-afterhook-get-session-scope.mjs`). It also misses API-key callers (the short-circuit skips after-hooks).
  - A rule that must hold **everywhere** changes state that better-auth itself consults on every path: better-auth's admin ban (it revokes the user's sessions and blocks new ones through its `session.create` hook), revoking the user's sessions, or a `@BeforeDatabase('session.create')` hook, which sees every sign-in path.

  The repository test `LIB-hook-bearer-client` (§14.5) pins the before-hook visibility rule and the after-hook's scope.

### 10.5 Return-value semantics (a faithful mirror of better-auth)

| Hook                                                    | better-auth semantics (LEAD-V1, LEAD-V22, LEAD-V23)                                                                                                                                                                                       | Dispatcher behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Verified                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| before → `undefined`                                    | continue                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | continue                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | EXP-A:`exp-plugin.mjs`                                                                                                               |
| before → `{ context }`                                  | `headers` are `set` into the accumulated Headers; other keys merged with `defuReplaceArrays(rest, acc)` (later hook wins, arrays replaced); **every hook sees the original input**; the result is applied only after all before-hooks ran | identical, using `createDefu` with the same array-replacing merger (`defu`, better-auth's own dependency). The accumulated `{ context }` is returned to better-auth, which merges it into its own accumulator. Empty accumulation returns `undefined` | EXP-A:`exp-merge.mjs` (SAME as N native plugins for full-spread, partial and array bodies); EXP-C10 (`hooks saw: orig,orig`; merged) |
| before → any other object                               | short-circuit: becomes the response                                                                                                                                                                                                       | returned immediately; remaining Nest hooks skipped                                                                                                                                                                                                    | EXP-A, EXP-B:E2, EXP-C1 (`{"shortCircuited":true}`)                                                                                  |
| before → throws                                         | propagates; with `asResponse` still thrown; cookies set in that hook are lost (R:ba-core §6.5)                                                                                                                                            | propagates unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | by construction                                                                                                                      |
| before matcher throws                                   | logged, `APIError` 500                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | a throwing predicate makes `matches` true and `run` rethrows it inside the before-hook handler: 500                                                                                                                                                   | `LIB-dispatcher-parity` (§14.5)                                                                                                      |
| after → value `!== undefined`                           | replaces `ctx.context.returned`; later hooks see it                                                                                                                                                                                       | sets `ctx.context.returned`, continues, returns the final value                                                                                                                                                                                       | EXP-B:E2 (`{"ok":"replaced"}`); EXP-C10 (after-hook 2 sees after-hook 1's value)                                                     |
| after → throws `APIError`                               | becomes the current `returned` with its headers merged; later hooks still run                                                                                                                                                             | identical: captured as `returned`, headers merged into `ctx.context.responseHeaders`, later Nest hooks run, the final value returned                                                                                                                  | EXP-C10 (403 `NOPE` reaches both the `auth.api` caller and HTTP)                                                                     |
| after → throws non-`APIError`                           | propagates (500)                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | propagates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | by construction                                                                                                                      |
| after matcher throws                                    | propagates raw                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | a throwing predicate makes `matches` true and `run` rethrows it raw                                                                                                                                                                                   | `LIB-dispatcher-parity`                                                                                                              |
| DB `create.before` → `false`                            | abort (`BA/db/with-hooks.ts:56-58`)                                                                                                                                                                                                       | return `false` immediately                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | EXP-A:`exp-plugin.mjs`, EXP-B:E2 (`400 FAILED_TO_CREATE_USER`)                                                                       |
| DB `create.before` → `{ data }`                         | shallow-merged; the _next_ hook sees the merged data                                                                                                                                                                                      | identical: the next Nest hook sees the payload with the accumulated results; returns `{ data: acc }` only if something changed                                                                                                                        | EXP-A (`orig+db`), EXP-B:E2 (`"… +db"`); LEAD-EXP-10                                                                                 |
| DB `update.before` → `{ data }` (update and updateMany) | shallow-merged into the update; **every hook receives the original payload** (`with-hooks.ts:129, 204`)                                                                                                                                   | identical: each Nest hook gets the original `Partial` payload, and only what the hooks **return** accumulates into `{ data: acc }`, so better-auth's merge keeps what earlier plugins changed `[R1:BA-r1-06]` `[R2:BA-r2-02]`                         | `LIB-dispatcher-parity`, with a preceding plugin (§14.5); LEAD-EXP-10                                                                |
| DB `update.before` → `false`                            | abort                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | return `false`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `LIB-dispatcher-parity`                                                                                                              |
| DB `delete.before` → `false`                            | abort; any other return value is ignored (`with-hooks.ts:291, 328`)                                                                                                                                                                       | only `false` is honored; the type allows `void \| false` only                                                                                                                                                                                         | `LIB-dispatcher-parity`                                                                                                              |
| DB after                                                | queued after the transaction completes (`queueAfterTransactionHook`)                                                                                                                                                                      | our dispatcher is itself queued, so Nest after-hooks run after commit; return values ignored                                                                                                                                                          | EXP-A:`exp-plugin.mjs`                                                                                                               |

Hook methods receive better-auth's own context objects: `HookEndpointContext` for endpoint hooks, and `(data, ctx | null)` for DB hooks, where `ctx` is `null` outside an endpoint. Nothing is re-wrapped, so `ctx.setCookie`, `ctx.json` and `ctx.redirect` behave as in native hooks. `ctx.body` is the raw input: better-auth validates the body only when the endpoint itself runs, after the before-hooks (better-call `context.ts:203-219`), so the hook types mark body values `unknown` (§11.3) `[R1:BA-r1-08]`.

**Parity guarantee.** A property test (`LIB-dispatcher-parity`) registers the same randomly generated hook functions two ways: as N native plugins, and as N Nest hooks behind one `nestjs()` dispatcher. It asserts identical responses, headers and DB effects for create, update, updateMany and delete, and for throwing matchers (§14.5). That is how the mirror stays faithful across better-auth releases.

### 10.6 `databaseHooks`, ordering, lifecycle, teardown, multiple apps

- **Coverage.** Models `user`, `session`, `account` and `verification`; operations `create`, `update` and `delete`; phases before and after. `init()` contributes one delegating dispatcher per target, mirroring better-auth per operation (LEAD-V22) `[R1:BA-r1-06]`:

  ```ts
  before: async (data, ctx) => {
    const binding = getBinding();
    if (!binding) { countUnbound(); return undefined; }                       // before the first binding only; B26 also counts writes [R2:NEST-r2-10]
    const fns = binding.database[target].before;
    if (op === 'delete') {                                                    // only false is honored
      for (const fn of fns) if ((await fn(data, ctx)) === false) return false;
      return undefined;
    }
    let acc = {}, changed = false;                                            // ONLY what hooks return [R2:BA-r2-02]
    for (const fn of fns) {
      const r = await fn(op === 'create' ? { ...data, ...acc } : data, ctx);  // create chains; update: every hook sees the ORIGINAL payload
      if (r === false) return false;                                          // abort, like better-auth
      if (r && typeof r === 'object' && 'data' in r) { acc = { ...acc, ...r.data }; changed = true; }
    }
    return changed ? { data: acc } : undefined;                               // better-auth merges it over its own accumulator
  },
  after: async (data, ctx) => {
    const binding = getBinding();
    if (!binding) { countUnbound(); return; }
    for (const fn of binding.database[target].after) await fn(data, ctx);
  },
  ```

  v2 returned `{ ...originalPayload, ...hookData }` for updates. better-auth merges a hook's result over the data earlier plugins already changed (`with-hooks.ts:136-139`), so the original values of every payload key overwrote those changes: a preceding plugin's `name.trim()` was undone whenever a Nest hook returned only `{ image }` (REV2-BA:`exp2-db-update-clobber.mjs`). Returning only the hooks' own data is what N native plugins produce (LEAD-EXP-10).

- **Ordering.** For endpoint hooks, better-auth runs the user's `options.hooks` first, then earlier plugins, then Nest hooks (`order` ascending, then discovery order). For DB hooks, **Nest's run before the user's `databaseHooks`** in `auth.ts`, because better-auth appends user DB hooks last (LEAD-V4). This is documented.
- **Bind and close** `[B][C]` `[R4:SEC-r4-01]`. Binding happens in `onModuleInit`, after discovery and B03/B04, once per application; a second `bind()` from the same application for the same instance is a no-op (§5.7) `[R2:NEST-r2-05]`. The kernel sets `binding.state = 'bootstrapped'` in `onApplicationBootstrap` and calls `close()` in `onApplicationShutdown` (idempotent). A closed binding **keeps dispatching** the application's Nest hooks, including for work another module drains after that point of `app.close()` (a BullMQ worker, a message consumer, an outbox relay: LEAD-V54), until the next application binds the instance. A hook that needs a provider already shut down throws, and the better-auth call fails closed; a hook never silently stops. The same applies in tests: after `app.close()`, a direct call on the instance still runs the closed application's hooks until the next test app binds (RK33). v4 unbound here and made the plugin inert, so a job's `signUpEmail` created an account that a `@BeforeDatabase('user.create')` rule had rejected a moment earlier (REV4-SEC:`probe-shutdown-unbind.mjs`). Nothing on `auth.options` needs reverting, because nothing was changed.
- **Exclusive binding** `[B][C]`. One **live** Nest application per better-auth instance. A second `bind()` while a bootstrapped app is bound throws (B06). That catches forgotten `app.close()` calls in tests and double imports, instead of silently running hooks twice or leaking them across apps; the reference accumulated wrappers on a shared singleton (R:ref-impl §5.3). In practice:
  - sequential lifetimes are fine: close, then boot the next app, which takes over the closed binding. `initTestApp` closes a previous test app still bound to the same instance before initializing the next one, which makes `beforeEach`-built apps work (§14.8) `[R1:SEC-r1-15]`;
  - an app whose `init()` failed never bootstrapped, so the next `bind()` takes over its binding and the kernel logs `W_INSTANCE_TAKEN_OVER`, instead of every later test failing with `INSTANCE_ALREADY_BOUND` and hiding the original error;
  - applications created one after another from one compiled `TestingModule` share a container and its singletons: after the first one's `close()`, the second one binds and mounts again on Fastify, and fails `init()` with `APP_ADAPTER_CHANGED` on Express, never silently unbound (§5.7) `[R3:NEST-r3-03]`;
  - concurrent apps need one instance each (shape 3 in §5.1);
  - vitest isolates test files by default, so per-file module-level instances are already separate;
  - hybrid apps share one container, so there is one binding.
- **Calls outside any scope** (cron jobs, CLI scripts using an application context) still run bound Nest hooks. `current()` is `undefined` there, so there is no cookie capture and no suppression, which is plain better-auth behavior.
- **Named instances** each have their own plugin instance and therefore their own binding. A plugin object shared by two instances fails boot (B03, §10.2) `[R4:BA-r4-05]`.

### 10.7 Reference vs this design

|               | @thallesp/nestjs-better-auth 2.8.0                              | This design                                                                                                               |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mechanism     | mutates `auth.options.hooks`/`databaseHooks` after construction | construction-time plugin with fixed entries and a late-bound registry                                                     |
| Prerequisite  | `hooks: {}` and `databaseHooks: {}` in the user's config        | `plugins: [..., nestjs()]` (boot-checked)                                                                                 |
| Return values | dropped (user hook and Nest hook)                               | better-auth semantics per operation, parity-tested                                                                        |
| Matching      | exact path equality only                                        | route patterns validated at boot, arrays, predicates, `calls`, `skipInternal`, `order`                                    |
| Typing        | `any`                                                           | `AuthHookContext<P>` (paths autocomplete, body values `unknown`), DB payloads from better-auth's own option types (§11.4) |
| Teardown      | none (leaks across apps)                                        | exclusive bind (one plugin object per instance), takeover of failed inits and closed apps, hooks kept through shutdown    |

## 11. Types
