## 13. Error model

### 13.1 Taxonomy `[A][B][C]`

| Class                                                | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Status                                                                                                         | `code` / `reason`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Logged                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Denial: unauthenticated**                          | required route, no principal (including an authoritative route that met a session a hook supplied, §7.3); a policy's better-auth call answered the generic 401 and the principal no longer resolves, or came from a source that is not session-backed (§8.1) `[R3:BA-r3-01]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | 401                                                                                                            | `UNAUTHENTICATED`; `reason` = better-auth's code where one exists                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | no (debug)                                                                                                      |
| **Denial: rejected credential**                      | a source returned `rejected` (for example an `APIError` 401/403 from `getSession` hooks, a bad JWT, an API key reported invalid, disabled or expired)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | 401 or 403 (better-auth's status)                                                                              | `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `FORBIDDEN`; `reason` = better-auth `body.code` (`INVALID_API_KEY`, `KEY_EXPIRED`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, …)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | no (debug)                                                                                                      |
| **Denial: forbidden**                                | a policy, the acceptance gate, a param-kind constraint or the origin check denied; a policy's better-auth call answered a 401 with a specific code for an authenticated principal (§8.1) `[R3:BA-r3-01]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | 403 (401 for `USER_NOT_FOUND` and `USER_BANNED`, or when a policy asks for re-authentication with a challenge) | `FORBIDDEN` / `UNAUTHENTICATED`; `reason` ∈ `MISSING_PERMISSION`, `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, `USER_BANNED` (§8.3), `USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THE_ORGANIZATION`, `YOU_ARE_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THIS_ORGANIZATION`, `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` (better-auth's membership codes, passed through by the org policies, §8.3), `ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, `SESSION_NOT_FRESH`, `PRINCIPAL_NOT_SUPPORTED`, `USER_REQUIRED`, `USER_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_ORIGIN`, `MISSING_OR_NULL_ORIGIN`, `CROSS_SITE_NAVIGATION_LOGIN_BLOCKED` (§7.10), better-auth codes, extension codes | no (debug)                                                                                                      |
| **Denial: rate limited**                             | better-auth 429 during resolution or evaluation, or `verifyApiKey` reporting `RATE_LIMITED`/`USAGE_EXCEEDED`; a request past `limits.maxAuthorizationCallsPerRequest` (§8.1) `[R3:SEC-r3-08]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 429                                                                                                            | `RATE_LIMITED`; `reason` = the better-auth code, or `TOO_MANY_AUTHORIZATION_CHECKS`; `Retry-After` from the error's headers or `details.tryAgainIn`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | no (debug)                                                                                                      |
| **Infrastructure** (`BetterAuthInfrastructureError`) | any throw from a source, policy or better-auth call that is not a 401/403/429 `APIError`: storage or network failure, `APIError` ≥ 500, `BetterAuthError`, an API-key verification that answered `INVALID_API_KEY` slowly or while the probe's read or no-op write fails (§8.3.1) `[R3:SEC-r3-01]`; a generic 401 from a policy's better-auth call while the session-backed principal still resolves authoritatively (§8.1); a failing function-valued `trustedOrigins` (§7.10); `auth.handler` throwing on auth routes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | 500                                                                                                            | HTTP: Nest's default 500 body; GraphQL `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` with `reason: 'AUTH_UNAVAILABLE'` and a generic message; WS/RPC "Internal server error"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | **yes**, once per logical request, by Nest's exception layer (not intrinsic), with a **redacted** cause (§13.4) |
| **Configuration** (`BetterAuthConfigurationError`)   | boot validation (§5.4); at request time: no transport for a context, unresolved policy, `userId` mapper returning `null`, another 4xx `APIError` from our own call, a principal or invocation param decorator with no authentication result or published value (`NO_AUTH_RESULT`, `NO_INVOCATION_VALUE`, §7.8), `BetterAuthService.getPrincipal()` outside any handler scope (`NO_AUTH_SCOPE`), `principalFor()` in a guard that runs before `BetterAuthGuard` (`PRINCIPAL_READ_BEFORE_GUARD`, §7.8), `forwardForeignCookies()` in a handler that does not forward (`FORWARDING_NOT_DECLARED`, §7.5), a GraphQL context the transport cannot classify (`GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_UNRECOGNIZED`, §9.2) or whose request already finished (`GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_STALE_REQUEST`, §9.2), an inheriting handler whose entry point no guard ran for (`NO_ENCLOSING_DECISION`, §7.1), a direct call with the caller's session cookie on an unsafe browser leg whose origin no guard verified (`PUBLIC_HANDLER_USED_CALLER_SESSION`, §7.5) `[R4:NEST-r4-01, SEC-r4-02, SEC-r4-03]`, an HTTP adapter that appeared after the core module initialized (`LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER`) or a second application on a container whose platform cannot prepare again (`APP_ADAPTER_CHANGED`, §5.7) `[R3:NEST-r3-02, SEC-r3-04, SEC-r3-05, NEST-r3-03]`, and any of these raised through `BetterAuthService` in a handler or resolver body | boot: the process fails; request time: 500                                                                     | `code` = the check id (e.g. `NO_TRANSPORT`, `UNRESOLVED_POLICY`, `NO_AUTH_RESULT`). Request-time errors are created with `atRequest`: `message` is `Authentication is misconfigured` and site, detail and hint are own properties, so a client never sees them, whether a transport mapped the error (guard) or not (decorators, services). On GraphQL the client sees only `reason: 'AUTH_MISCONFIGURED'` and a generic message `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`                                                                                                     | yes (Nest's exception layer prints `detail`, `site` and `hint`, LEAD-V31)                                       |
| **Auth routes**                                      | anything better-auth returns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | verbatim                                                                                                       | better-auth's `{ message, code }` bodies; ours only for `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` (413) and `INVALID_REQUEST_URL` (400), in the same shape; with `onAPIError.throw`, the user's filters decide                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | host pipeline for 5xx and rethrown `APIError`s                                                                  |

**The key rule (S6).** Only a _denial value_ produces 401, 403 or 429. Detection uses `isAPIError` from `better-auth/api` (LEAD-V5), the status comes from `e.statusCode`, and the reason from `e.body?.code`. For `verifyApiKey`, which returns failures as values, the mapping is an explicit table with an outage probe (§8.3.1). Nothing in the library catches an arbitrary error and returns 401/403. The reference did that for every plugin error (R:ref-impl §6.1).

### 13.2 Normalization `[B][C]`

Sources and policies return values. The kernel's safety net normalizes anything they throw:

```ts
/** A policy's better-auth call answered the generic 401: the evaluator decides 401 or 5xx from the principal's source (§8.1). */
type SessionLossCandidate = {
  readonly sessionLoss: unknown;
  readonly reason?: string;
};
function normalizeThrown(
  e: unknown,
  where: "source" | "policy",
  site: string,
  secrets: readonly string[],
): AuthFailure | SessionLossCandidate | never {
  if (isAuthFailure(e)) return e; // brand check, dual-package safe
  if (isInfrastructureError(e) || isConfigurationError(e)) throw e; // already classified (e.g. SESSION_USER_ID, the API-key outage probe): never re-wrapped
  if (isAPIError(e)) {
    // better-auth/api; never instanceof (S6)
    const status = e.statusCode,
      reason = (e.body as { code?: string } | undefined)?.code;
    if (status === 429) return AuthFailures.fromAPIError(e)!; // Retry-After from headers or body.details.tryAgainIn
    if (
      status === 401 &&
      where === "policy" &&
      (reason === undefined || reason === "UNAUTHORIZED")
    )
      return { sessionLoss: e, reason }; // §8.1: generic 401, session-backed sources re-read [R2:BA-r2-03] [R3:BA-r3-01]
    if (status === 401 || status === 403)
      return where === "source"
        ? AuthFailures.rejected({ status, reason }) // presented credential rejected
        : AuthFailures.forbidden(reason ?? "FORBIDDEN"); // principal is authenticated → 403 (coded 401s too, §17 Q28)
    if (status >= 500) throw new BetterAuthInfrastructureError(e, { secrets });
    throw BetterAuthConfigurationError.atRequest(
      "BETTER_AUTH_REJECTED_CALL",
      `better-auth rejected the library's call (${status} ${reason})`,
      { site },
    );
  }
  throw new BetterAuthInfrastructureError(e, { secrets });
}
```

A 4xx other than 401, 403 or 429 means our own call was malformed, for example a validation error from `userHasPermission`. That is a bug or a misconfiguration, not a client error `[C]`. Built-in policies convert the better-auth outcomes they expect into decisions themselves before this net sees them:

- `USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THE_ORGANIZATION` (401 → 403);
- `YOU_ARE_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THIS_ORGANIZATION` (403 → 403, as a decision rather than a thrown error);
- `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` and `MEMBER_NOT_FOUND` (400) from `getActiveMember` in the default organization ref → no organization, 403 `NO_ACTIVE_ORGANIZATION` (§8.3);
- the admin endpoint's 400 `user not found` (a user deleted between the guard's read and the policy's call; the error has no body code, so the policy matches status 400 and that message, pinned per better-auth version by `Z-admin-deleted-user`, LEAD-V51), and a missing owner row on the delegated path → 401 `USER_NOT_FOUND`; an owner under an active ban on the delegated path → 401 `USER_BANNED` (§8.3) `[R1:BA-r1-10]` `[R3:BA-r3-02, SEC-r3-06]` `[R4:BA-r4-01]`. v4 read the row itself and passed its role, which made a NULL role a 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` that this net turned into a 500 (BA-r4-01).

A source never gets the re-classification: a source's 401 is a rejected credential. A policy's generic 401 (`UNAUTHORIZED`, or no code) goes through it, because better-auth's session checks cannot tell a lost session from a failed read (LEAD-V36, LEAD-V43); the evaluator re-reads only when the principal's source is `sessionBacked`. A policy's 401 with any other code is better-auth denying an authenticated caller and becomes 403 with that code (§8.1) `[R3:BA-r3-01]`.

### 13.3 Mapping per transport and payload contract

```ts
/** HTTP body of a denial: Nest's default shape plus a stable code. [A][C] */
export interface AuthErrorBody {
  statusCode: 401 | 403 | 429;
  error: string;
  code: AuthErrorCode;
  reason?: string;
  message: string;
}
/** GraphQL extensions of a denial or an internal error (both drivers). [L] */
export interface AuthGraphqlExtensions {
  code: AuthErrorCode | "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR";
  reason?: string;
  statusCode: number;
}
/** WS and RPC error object. [A][B][C] */
export interface AuthTransportErrorPayload {
  status: "error";
  statusCode: number;
  code: AuthErrorCode;
  reason?: string;
  message: string;
}
```

| Transport                   | Denial thrown                                                                                                                                     | Client-visible payload                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Infrastructure / configuration at request time                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| HTTP                        | `UnauthorizedException` / `ForbiddenException` / `HttpException(…, 429)` constructed with `AuthErrorBody` and `{ cause }` (intrinsic: not logged) | `{ "statusCode": 403, "error": "Forbidden", "code": "FORBIDDEN", "reason": "MISSING_PERMISSION", "message": "Forbidden" }` + `WWW-Authenticate` when a challenge exists + `Retry-After` for 429. User filters catching `ForbiddenException` keep working | the error itself: Nest's filters answer a generic 500 and log it (redacted cause)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| GraphQL (Apollo, Mercurius) | `BetterAuthGraphqlDenial` (intrinsic, `extensions`) (LEAD-EXP-1)                                                                                  | `errors[i].extensions = { code, reason, statusCode }`, HTTP 200; identical across drivers; same codes Apollo uses for 401/403                                                                                                                            | from the guard: `BetterAuthGraphqlInternalError` via `toInternalException`: message `Internal server error`, `extensions.code = 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR'`, `reason` `AUTH_UNAVAILABLE` / `AUTH_MISCONFIGURED`; for later invocations of the same request, the same payload as the intrinsic `BetterAuthGraphqlRepeatedInternalError` (logged once) `[R3:SEC-r3-08]`. Thrown where no transport maps it (a param decorator whose guard did not run, `BetterAuthService` in a resolver body): the error as thrown, `Authentication is misconfigured` / `Authentication service unavailable` with the same `extensions` (LEAD-EXP-7). Details only in the server log `[R1:SEC-r1-19]` |
| WebSocket                   | `WsException(AuthTransportErrorPayload)`                                                                                                          | `exception` event with that object (`BaseWsExceptionFilter`)                                                                                                                                                                                             | "Internal server error", logged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| RPC                         | `RpcException(AuthTransportErrorPayload)`                                                                                                         | that object (`BaseRpcExceptionFilter`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | "Internal server error", logged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| gRPC (carrier)              | `RpcException({ code: 16 \| 7 \| 8, message })` or Nest 12's `Grpc*Exception`                                                                     | gRPC status + message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | status 13                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Auth routes                 | better-auth's own responses, untouched                                                                                                            | better-auth's `{ message, code }`                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 500 via the host pipeline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

**Errors thrown outside the guard** `[R1:SEC-r1-19]`. Param decorators (§7.8) and `BetterAuthService` run where the guard's transport mapping does not, so their errors reach each runtime unmapped: Nest's default 500 on HTTP, `Internal server error` on WS and RPC, and the error's own `message` and `extensions` on GraphQL. Both library error classes are therefore generic as thrown: a request-time `BetterAuthConfigurationError` (`atRequest`) and `BetterAuthInfrastructureError` carry a fixed message and `extensions` with the reason, and keep the specifics in own properties (`detail`, `site`, `hint`, the redacted `cause`) that neither GraphQL driver serializes (LEAD-EXP-7).

`AuthFailure` is transport-neutral, and only a transport's `toException` knows the transport's format. A new transport therefore gets the whole taxonomy by implementing one method, plus `toInternalException` if its runtime would expose error messages `[B]`.

### 13.4 Logging and redaction `[R1:SEC-r1-08]`

- **Denials are not errors.** HTTP and GraphQL mappings are `IntrinsicException`s, which Nest's filters do not log (LEAD-V9). Denials are logged at `debug` by the guard. Origin-check denials are also logged at WARN for the first occurrence of each distinct `(reason, origin)` pair within an hourly window per application, sanitized, capped at 100 pairs per window with a summary line when the window closes, and with a `Referer` reduced to its origin (§7.10) `[R3:SEC-r3-03]` `[R4:SEC-r4-05]`.
- **Infrastructure failures are logged once per logical request, by Nest's exception layer, with a redacted cause.** `RequestScope` remembers which errors a request key has surfaced; a later invocation of the same request that meets the same memoized error (a failed principal resolution, or since v5 a failed re-classification read, §8.1 `[R4:SEC-r4-04]`) passes `repeated: true` to `toInternalException`, and the GraphQL transports then throw the intrinsic `BetterAuthGraphqlRepeatedInternalError`, so 500 aliased root fields during an outage write one ERROR entry, not 500 (`T-internal-error-logged-once`) `[R3:SEC-r3-08]`. Nest's `ConsoleLogger.error(err)` prints `util.inspect(err)`, which includes the `[cause]` chain and enumerable properties (LEAD-V31); pino/nestjs-pino serializers and Sentry's linked-errors integration read `error.cause` too. Driver errors commonly embed query parameters: drizzle-orm 0.45.2 builds `DrizzleQueryError` with the message `` `Failed query: ${query}\nparams: ${params}` `` (`errors.js:10-16`), and `findSession(token)` puts the session token in those params. v1 attached the raw cause, so a database timeout would have shipped live session and bearer tokens to log aggregators for every guarded request during the outage.

  v2's `ErrorRedactor` (U18) builds the cause instead:
  - **Secrets** are the request's credential values:
    - every cookie value in the `Cookie` header, and its URL-decoded form;
    - for signed values (`token.signature`), the part before the last `.` when at least 16 characters long, which is the form stored in the database;
    - the `authorization` value and its credential part after the scheme;
    - the values of every declared credential header (source `credentialHeaders`, e.g. `x-api-key`).
  - **The redacted cause** is a new `Error` with the original's `name` and its `code`, `errno` and `syscall` when present. Its message is the **first line** of the original message, truncated to 300 characters, with every secret replaced by `[REDACTED]`. Its `stack` is that header plus the original stack frames (frames are file positions only). Nested causes are redacted the same way, to a depth of 3.
  - **The raw cause** is kept under a non-enumerable `Symbol.for('nestjs-slightly-better-auth:raw-cause')` slot, which `util.inspect` does not print. It is reachable through `getRawCause(error)` only when `errors.exposeRawCause: true` (local debugging).
  - The same redaction applies on auth routes (`AuthExchange` knows the inbound credentials) and on the `WsConnectionAuth` path.

- **Never logged:** request headers, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie`, bearer tokens and API keys. One alternative library logs full headers (R:ba-integrations §6.6). A hygiene conformance case (`S-log-redaction`) makes an adapter throw with the session token in its message and asserts the token never appears in captured logs.
- **better-auth's own logger** is outside this library's control. It logs `Failed to validate API key:` with the underlying error at ERROR for every failed key verification (LEAD-V20), and it logs origin failures at ERROR on auth routes. The docs recommend configuring better-auth's `logger` (level, or a redacting `log` function) in production (RK19).
- The docs warn that with `apiKey({ enableSessionForAPIKeys })`, the mocked session carries the raw key in `session.token`. Serializing `@CurrentSession()` into responses or logs leaks it (R:ba-authz §1.2). `apiKeyPrincipal()` never exposes the raw key.

### 13.5 Customization

```ts
export interface ErrorMappingOptions {
  /** Replace what a transport throws for a denial; return undefined to keep the transport's default. [C] */
  map?: (
    failure: AuthFailure,
    context: ExecutionContext,
    transport: string,
  ) => unknown;
  /** Keep the unredacted cause reachable through getRawCause() (local debugging only). Default false. [R1:SEC-r1-08] */
  exposeRawCause?: boolean;
}
```

- `errors.map` is a per-instance override: a runtime option (§5.2) of the instance whose plan produced the denial (§5.5). It is applied before the transport's `toException`, and receives the transport's id (§9.0).
- A deeper change is made by subclassing a transport (for example the HTTP transport) and listing it in `transports`, where it is selected before the built-in one `[A]`.
- Neither mechanism depends on exception filters, which do not reach WebSocket gateways in any Nest version (R:nest-di §5.2).

## 14. Testing strategy

### 14.1 Conformance kits (the LSP proof, reusable by third parties) `[A][B][C]`

The kits live in `nestjs-slightly-better-auth/testing/conformance`. They are **runner-agnostic**: each returns `ConformanceCase[]`, and `runConformance(cases, { describe, it })` registers them with vitest, jest or `node:test`. Assertions use `node:assert/strict`. The same kits run in our CI for every built-in unit, which makes "Express and Fastify behave the same" a tested property rather than a claim. Every kit builds its better-auth instances with `advanced.disableOriginCheck: false` set explicitly, so the origin cases test what they claim under any runner and environment: better-auth's `isTest()` is true under vitest whatever `NODE_ENV` says (vitest sets `TEST=true`, LEAD-V48), and would otherwise switch off the origin rules the kits test, for the kits' own runs and for third parties running them `[R3:SEC-r3-07]`.

Each HTTP case boots a real Nest app, under both `NestFactory.create` and `Test.createTestingModule().createNestApplication()`. It uses a real better-auth instance (memory adapter) that includes `conformanceProbePlugin()` (and the explicit `disableOriginCheck: false` above). The probe plugin provides these endpoints:

- `/probe/echo-raw`: `disableBody` + `ctx.request.text()`, echoing the received bytes and headers;
- `/probe/multi-cookie`: three cookies;
- `/probe/redirect`: 302 with a cookie;
- `/probe/stream`: three chunks with delays;
- `/probe/html`;
- `/probe/put`, `/probe/patch`, `/probe/delete`;
- `/probe/url`: echoes `request.url`;
- `/probe/ip`: echoes `getIP(request)`;
- `/probe/throw-api-error`, `/probe/throw-error`.

The probe plugin also contributes a trusted origin through `init()` (`https://probe-plugin.example`), so trusted-origin cases exercise the post-init set (LEAD-V17). The kit also adds a throwing `around` interceptor, an app controller `/app/echo` that returns `{ body, rawBody }`, and a global `APP_FILTER` that records what it sees.

```ts
export interface HttpConformanceOptions {
  platform: ExtensionRef<HttpPlatform>;
  /** Fresh Nest HTTP adapter per app, e.g. () => new ExpressAdapter(). */
  createHttpAdapter(): AbstractHttpAdapter;
  /** Bootstraps to exercise. Default both. */
  bootstrap?: readonly ("factory" | "testing")[];
  /** Enable host CORS the platform's usual way. Default: app.enableCors({ origin, credentials: true }). */
  enableHostCors?(app: INestApplication, origin: string): void | Promise<void>;
  /** Configure trust in one forwarding hop the platform's usual way (for H-proxy-trust / H-url-trust-proxy). */
  trustOneProxy?(app: INestApplication): void | Promise<void>;
  /** HTTP/2 variant, required when the platform declares capabilities.http2. */
  http2?: { createHttpAdapter(): AbstractHttpAdapter };
  /** How to obtain a base URL. Default: app.listen(0) + getUrl(). */
  listen?(app: INestApplication): Promise<string>;
}
export interface TransportConformanceOptions {
  transport: ExtensionRef<AuthTransport>;
  /**
   * Boots an app exposing the kit's fixture handlers (TransportFixtures: 'required', 'optional', 'public', 'forbidden', 'triple',
   * 'tripleMixed', 'readsSession', 'unsafe', 'loginProxy', 'loginProxyService', 'publicService', 'acceptsApiKey', 'org', 'inherited',
   * 'unguarded', and 'graph' for GraphQL shapes) in the transport's shape, with BetterAuthModule's globalGuard set as given. Handlers receive the default
   * instance's BetterAuthService (FixtureContext), injected with @Inject(BETTER_AUTH_SERVICE). With globalGuard: true the harness adds
   * what its shape needs for coverage (a gateway class carries @UseBetterAuth()); with false it adds nothing, and the kit adds
   * @UseBetterAuth() or @UseGuards(BetterAuthGuard) to a fixture's decorators where a case asks for it. When `override` is given, the harness
   * boots through Test.createTestingModule() and passes the builder through it before compile(). The kit boots [R2:NEST-r2-02]:
   *   1. with globalGuard: true, for every case that serves requests;
   *   2. with globalGuard: true and override = (b) => overrideAuthGuard(b, passThrough), a stand-in guard that returns true and
   *      stamps nothing (§14.8), for the 'unguarded' part of T-internal-error-generic: B16 sees every handler covered, yet the
   *      param decorators find no result, a path no coverage check can see (§7.8 item 5);
   *   3. with globalGuard: false, only for T-coverage-claims: boots that serve no request, where the bare fixtures are expected to fail
   *      and the variants that add @UseBetterAuth() or register BetterAuthGuard and BetterAuthScopeInterceptor as APP_GUARD and
   *      APP_INTERCEPTOR are expected to boot;
   *   4. with globalGuard: true and override = (b) => b.overrideProvider(BetterAuthGuard).useValue(standIn) (and .useClass), only
   *      for T-coverage-claims: expected to boot, because B16 recognizes the replaced global guard by identity, and serving no
   *      request. [R4:NEST-r4-02]
   */
  createApp(
    fixtures: TransportFixtures,
    auth: AuthLike,
    options: {
      globalGuard: boolean;
      override?: (builder: TestingModuleBuilder) => TestingModuleBuilder;
      /** Passed to BetterAuthModule (T-reads-session, T-unsatisfiable-kinds). [R3:NEST-r3-06] */
      defaultRequirements?: readonly RequirementExpr[];
      /** GraphQL shapes: the fieldResolverEnhancers to serve 'graph' with. The kit boots every GraphQL case with [] and with ['guards', 'interceptors']. [R3:NEST-r3-01] */
      fieldResolverEnhancers?: readonly ("guards" | "interceptors")[];
      /** GraphQL shapes: serve 'graph' from a federation subgraph (FixtureNode an entity keyed by id, with GraphFixtures.reference when given). [R4:NEST-r4-01] */
      federation?: boolean;
    },
  ): Promise<INestApplication>;
  /** Invokes a fixture handler with given credentials and browser headers; returns the transport-native outcome. */
  invoke(
    app: INestApplication,
    handler: Exclude<keyof TransportFixtures, "graph">,
    headers: HeadersInit,
    input?: Record<string, unknown>,
  ): Promise<{
    ok: boolean;
    body?: unknown;
    error?: {
      code?: string;
      statusCode?: number;
      reason?: string;
      message?: string;
    };
    setCookies: string[];
  }>;
  /**
   * Two invocations of the 'org' fixture in ONE logical request or connection, with different inputs, in the given shape:
   * 'aliases': two aliased GraphQL root fields in one operation; 'batched': two operations in one batched GraphQL HTTP request;
   * 'messages': two messages on one WS socket (principalTtlMs > 0); 'subscriptions': two GraphQL subscriptions on one connection
   * (subscriptionPrincipalTtlMs > 0 and 0). The kit calls it once per entry of invocationShapes. [R1:NEST-r1-01]
   */
  invokeTwice?(
    app: INestApplication,
    shape: InvocationShape,
    inputs: [Record<string, unknown>, Record<string, unknown>],
    headers: HeadersInit,
  ): Promise<
    [
      { ok: boolean; error?: { reason?: string } },
      { ok: boolean; error?: { reason?: string } },
    ]
  >;
  /** Shapes invokeTwice can produce; required with it. Apollo and Mercurius: ['aliases', 'batched', 'subscriptions']; socket.io and ws: ['messages']. */
  invocationShapes?: readonly InvocationShape[];
  /**
   * GraphQL shapes: one operation over HTTP selecting the given root fields of fixtures.graph, in order, each with the given
   * FixtureNode fields, against an app createApp served with the given fieldResolverEnhancers. `delays` makes the kit's session

   * with a reason, unless the transport defines defaultAccessFor, in which case they fail. [R2:NEST-r2-04, NEST-r2-06] [R3:NEST-r3-01]
   */
  invokeGraph?(
    app: INestApplication,
    selection: readonly GraphSelection[],
    headers: HeadersInit,
    options?: {
      delays?: { readonly session: number; readonly apiKey: number };
    },
  ): Promise<{
    data: unknown;
    errors: readonly {
      path: readonly (string | number)[];
      code?: string;
      reason?: string;
      message?: string;
    }[];
  }>;
  /**
   * Federation shapes only: one `_entities` query over HTTP for the given representations of FixtureNode (each `{ __typename, id, orgId }`),
   * selecting the given field resolvers, against an app served with a federation driver. Runs T-reference-resolver; without it the case is
   * skipped with a reason, unless the transport claims reference resolvers, in which case it fails. [R4:NEST-r4-01]
   */
  invokeEntities?(
    app: INestApplication,
    representations: readonly Record<string, unknown>[],
    fields: readonly (keyof GraphFixtures["fields"])[],
    headers: HeadersInit,
  ): Promise<{
    data: unknown;
    errors: readonly {
      path: readonly (string | number)[];
      code?: string;
      reason?: string;
      message?: string;
    }[];
  }>;
  expectCookieCapable: boolean;
  /** Whether the transport has a browser leg (false for RPC): enables the T-csrf-* cases. */
  expectBrowserLeg: boolean;
}
export type InvocationShape =
  "aliases" | "batched" | "messages" | "subscriptions";
/** One fixture handler the kit supplies; the harness exposes it as a controller route, resolver field, gateway message or message pattern. */
export interface FixtureHandler {
  /** Method decorators to apply, in order (access, acceptance, requirements). */
  readonly decorators: readonly MethodDecorator[];
  /** Parameter decorators by parameter index, e.g. [CurrentSession()]. */
  readonly params: readonly ParameterDecorator[];
  /** 'read': HTTP GET, GraphQL query, RPC request. 'unsafe': HTTP POST, GraphQL mutation. WS messages are always enforced (§7.10). */
  readonly operation: "read" | "unsafe";
  /** Handler body: receives the decorated parameter values, the invocation input and the harness context; its result is the response. */
  handle(
    params: readonly unknown[],
    input: Record<string, unknown>,
    context: FixtureContext,
  ): unknown;
}
/** What the harness hands every fixture handler. [R2:SEC-r2-04] */
export interface FixtureContext {
  /** The default instance's service (BETTER_AUTH_SERVICE): loginProxy calls service.api.signInEmail, publicService calls getSession(). */
  readonly service: BetterAuthService;
}
/**
 * GraphQL shapes only: one object type FixtureNode, returned by three root fields and carrying the field resolvers below, served with
 * both fieldResolverEnhancers settings (T-stamp-per-plan, T-inherit-no-lookup). The resolver class of the root fields also carries a
 * class-level @AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key') variant in one boot, which must not reach the field resolvers. `guarded` and
 * `nestedReader` are passed only for the ['guards', 'interceptors'] boot: with [], a field resolver with its own requirement fails boot
 * with FIELD_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED at the default fieldResolverCoverage (§9.2), which the GraphQL job asserts (§14.2), so the kit's []
 * boots leave both out. [R2:NEST-r2-04, NEST-r2-06, SEC-r2-09] [R3:NEST-r3-01, NEST-r3-05]
 */
export interface GraphFixtures {
  readonly roots: {
    readonly public: FixtureHandler; // @Public(); no params
    readonly sessionOnly: FixtureHandler; // default kinds; @CurrentPrincipal()
    readonly mixed: FixtureHandler; // @AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key'); @CurrentPrincipal()
  };
  readonly fields: {
    readonly plain: FixtureHandler; // no metadata, no params: an 'inherit' plan
    readonly publicNested: FixtureHandler; // @Public() field resolver returning a FixtureNode; `reader` selected under it reads the enclosing operation's reading under both enhancer settings [R4:NEST-r4-03]
    readonly reader: FixtureHandler; // no access, acceptance or requirement metadata; @CurrentPrincipal(): an 'inherit' plan
    readonly guarded?: FixtureHandler; // @RequireAuth(): a real plan, enforced per field; ['guards', 'interceptors'] boot only
    readonly nestedReader?: FixtureHandler; // like reader, selected under guarded: reads guarded's own result; with guarded only [R3:NEST-r3-01]
  };
  /** Federation shapes only: @ResolveReference() of FixtureNode, with the kit's per-representation requirement on `orgId` (T-reference-resolver). [R4:NEST-r4-01] */
  readonly reference?: FixtureHandler;
}
export interface GraphSelection {
  readonly root: keyof GraphFixtures["roots"];
  readonly fields: readonly (keyof GraphFixtures["fields"])[];
}
/** The fixture handlers of transportConformance, by name (the `handler` argument of invoke()). */
export interface TransportFixtures {
  readonly required: FixtureHandler; // default access; returns the principal's kind (T-no-credentials, T-credentials, T-acceptance, T-infra-5xx)
  readonly optional: FixtureHandler; // @OptionalAuth()
  readonly public: FixtureHandler; // @Public() (T-public-no-lookup)
  readonly forbidden: FixtureHandler; // a requirement whose kit policy always denies (T-error-shape, T-no-error-log)
  /** Three DISTINCT handler methods with equal accepted kinds, invoked in one logical request, e.g. 3 root fields in 3 resolver methods: 1 resolution (T-memo-once, S7). [R2:NEST-r2-16] */
  readonly triple: readonly [FixtureHandler, FixtureHandler, FixtureHandler];
  /** Like triple, but the second method adds @AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key'): exactly 2 resolutions. */
  readonly tripleMixed: readonly [
    FixtureHandler,
    FixtureHandler,
    FixtureHandler,
  ];
  readonly readsSession: FixtureHandler; // @CurrentSession() (T-reads-session, T-carrier / T-scope)
  readonly unsafe: FixtureHandler; // operation 'unsafe' (T-csrf-*)
  readonly loginProxy: FixtureHandler; // @Public() @ForwardAuthCookies(), operation 'unsafe', calls service.api.signInEmail (T-csrf-login-proxy, T-coverage-claims) [R2:SEC-r2-08]
  /** @Public(), operation 'unsafe', no @ForwardAuthCookies(); calls service.forwardForeignCookies(() => service.api.signInEmail(…)) (T-csrf-login-proxy). [R3:SEC-r3-04] */
  readonly loginProxyService: FixtureHandler;
  readonly publicService: FixtureHandler; // @Public(), operation 'unsafe', returns service.getSession() (T-public-service-null) [R2:SEC-r2-04]
  readonly acceptsApiKey: FixtureHandler; // @AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key') (T-credentials)
  readonly org: FixtureHandler; // orgPermission(p, { organization: fromParam('orgId') }) + @ActiveOrganizationId() (T-invocation-decisions, Z-org-ref-types)
  /** One method of an abstract base class, exposed through two subclasses: one @Public(), one with the kit's always-deny requirement (T-inherited-handler). [R2:NEST-r2-01] */
  readonly inherited: FixtureHandler;
  /** @CurrentSession() + @ActiveOrganizationId(), no access metadata; served in boot 2, where a stand-in guard stamps nothing (T-internal-error-generic). [R2:NEST-r2-02] */
  readonly unguarded: FixtureHandler;
  /** GraphQL shapes only; other harnesses ignore it. [R2:NEST-r2-04, NEST-r2-06] */
  readonly graph: GraphFixtures;
}
export interface PrincipalSourceConformanceOptions {
  source: ExtensionRef<PrincipalSource>;
  credentials: {
    valid(): Promise<Headers>;
    invalid(): Headers;
    rateLimited?(): Promise<Headers>;
  };
}
export interface PolicyConformanceOptions {
  requirement: RequirementExpr;
  allowingPrincipal(): Promise<AuthPrincipal>;
  denyingPrincipal(): Promise<AuthPrincipal>;
  delegatedPrincipal?(): Promise<AuthPrincipal>;
}
```

**HTTP platform cases** (invariants H1–H14, §4.1.2):

Each clause names its case id; §4.1.2 maps the ids to invariants, except the cases listed after the table. Every case runs under both bootstraps and on Nest 11 and 12, which is how H9 is checked for the whole suite.

| Group       | Cases (id)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mount       | every method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, QUERY if supported) reaches better-auth under the base path (`H-mount-methods`); the bare base path reaches it, `/api/authx` falls through, and a controller outside the path still works (`H-mount-boundary`); custom path via a `baseURL` path, via `basePath`, and via dynamic `allowedHosts` + `basePath`, and a Nest global prefix + URI versioning leave the mount unchanged (`H-mount-custom-path`); a controller route under the path wins (`H-app-route-precedence`, H11)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Body        | byte-exact echo, one case per content shape (the `H-body-*` family): JSON with odd whitespace and key order (`H-body-json`), UTF-8 (`H-body-utf8`), urlencoded `b=%20x&c=1` (`H-body-urlencoded`), `text/plain` (`H-body-text`), `application/scim+json` (`H-body-scim`), multipart (`H-body-multipart`), binary (`H-body-binary`), chunked transfer (`H-body-chunked`), empty body (`H-body-empty`), no content-type (`H-body-no-content-type`), and a urlencoded sign-in that succeeds (`H-body-form-sign-in`). Over-limit → 413 **with host CORS headers** for a declared `content-length` (`H-limit-declared`) and a chunked body (`H-limit-chunked`), with the canonical body, byte-identical across platforms and exact at the boundary (`H-limit-canonical-body`). App routes are still parsed, with `useBodyParser` limits (`H-app-parsing`), and keep `rawBody` (`H-app-rawbody`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Facts       | URL protocol and host honor the platform's trust-proxy setting (`H-url-trust-proxy`); the query string is preserved, OAuth `?code=&state=` (`H-url-query`); percent-encoding is kept (`H-url-encoded`); `Origin`, `Referer`, `Sec-Fetch-*`, `Cookie`, `Authorization` and `Content-Type` arrive unmodified (`H-headers-passthrough`); better-auth's `getIP` sees the platform IP, with per-IP rate-limit buckets in production mode, and a variant with better-auth's `advanced.ipAddress.trustedProxies` covering the proxy: trust off gives no IP plus the B18 warning, trust on gives the client IP (`H-ip-platform`) `[R2:BA-r2-04]`; a client-sent client-IP header (fixed name or any `x-nsba-ip-*`) is ignored (`H-ip-spoof`); `proxyTrust()` reports the effective setting before and after `trustOneProxy` (`H-proxy-trust`); HTTP/2 pseudo-headers do not crash, h2c with capability `http2` (`H-h2-pseudo`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Write-back  | three `Set-Cookie` preserved on separate lines (`H-resp-multicookie`); 302 + `Location` + cookie, not followed (`H-resp-redirect`); a 3-chunk stream arrives in order and a client abort cancels the reader (`H-resp-stream`); HEAD has no body and never 500s (`H-resp-head`); status and headers are written verbatim, `text/html` passes through, `vary` is merged, and a before-hook `APIError` becomes its Response (`H-resp-status`); host CORS answers the preflight (`H-cors-preflight`) and adds its headers to real responses (`H-cors-actual`); `requests.key()` is the same object for guards, interceptors and GraphQL of one request (`H-accessor-key`); `requests.isRequest()` accepts the request guards and GraphQL contexts receive and rejects an upgrade request and a plain object with `headers`, and `requests.isLive()`, when implemented, is true inside the handler and false for the same request object once its response was sent (`H-accessor-is-request`) `[R3:SEC-r3-05]` `[R4:SEC-r4-03]`; cookies written through `cookieSink()` arrive alongside the handler's own, and `cache-control`/`pragma` from `getSession` never leak onto app routes (`H-accessor-cookie-merge`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Errors      | a non-`APIError` from `auth.handler` reaches the host pipeline as a 5xx (`H-errors-infra`), and the kit's global filter sees it and Nest logs it, with a global prefix set (`H-errors-filter-sees`, the Fastify awaited-registration case of LEAD-EXP-2); with `onAPIError.throw`, the filter receives the original `APIError` (`H-errors-apierror-throw`); no hang, every request completes within a timeout (`H-errors-no-hang`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Lifecycle   | `MiddlewareConsumer` middleware runs before the auth handler, no global prefix (`H-middleware-order`); a `forRootAsync` factory awaiting an async dependency still captures bytes under `NestFactory` (`H-async-options-factory`); `createMicroservice` and `createApplicationContext` through `NestFactory`, `Test…compile()` + `moduleRef.init()`, and `Test…createNestMicroservice()` boot without platform calls, each microservice once with `listen()` and once with `init()` then `listen()` (lifecycle work runs once, no `INSTANCE_ALREADY_BOUND`) (`H-no-adapter`) `[R2:NEST-r2-05, NEST-r2-09]`; `moduleRef.init()` followed by `createNestApplication().init()` fails with `LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER` (`H-late-adapter`); two applications created one after the other from one compiled `TestingModule`, the first closed before the second: with `capabilities.prepareAtInit` the second serves auth routes (200), runs Nest hooks and allows an authoritative route, and without it the second `init()` fails with `APP_ADAPTER_CHANGED`; neither boots unmounted (`H-reused-testing-module`, H14) `[R3:NEST-r3-03]`; a second `forRoot` for the same instance → boot error (`H-double-forroot`); on `app.close()` the binding is closed, not unbound: a better-auth call made after `close()` started (from another module's shutdown hook) still runs the app's Nest hooks, and the next app takes the binding over without a warning (`H-close-keeps-hooks`) `[R4:SEC-r4-01]` |
| Diagnostics | a 404 under the mount logs one WARN with a "did you mean" outside production and never changes the response (`H-diagnostics-404`); `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` once in production with forwarding headers and trust off (`H-proxy-untrusted-warning`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Hygiene     | probe cookies never appear in captured logs (`H-log-hygiene`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

`H-no-adapter`, `H-late-adapter`, `H-double-forroot`, `H-close-keeps-hooks`, `H-diagnostics-404`, `H-proxy-untrusted-warning` and `H-log-hygiene` map to no platform invariant (§4.1.2). They check behavior that core provides around every platform: the mount coordinator's and instance registry's lifecycle (§5.7, B06, B07), 404 diagnostics (ADR-52), the proxy-trust warning built on `proxyTrust()` (§6.8) and log redaction (§13.4). They run in the platform kit so that each platform's bootstraps and error paths exercise them.

| `T-metadata-canary`                            | the transport's boot canaries pass on the installed Nest; with a Nest-owned literal the unit reads patched to a wrong value in a test build, boot fails `NEST_METADATA_KEY_CHANGED`, and a class with no handlers (a push-only gateway) is not claimed `[R3:NEST-r3-08]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `T-unsatisfiable-kinds`                        | its own boots: with `defaultRequirements` holding a kit requirement that admits only `'session'`, the `acceptsApiKey` fixture decorated with a kit requirement that admits only `'api-key'` fails boot with B15 `UNSATISFIABLE_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`, naming both requirements and their origins; with `@SkipDefaultRequirements()` added it boots, an API key is allowed and the boot summary counts one skip `[R3:NEST-r3-06]`; with `defaultRequirements` holding a kit policy that names **no** kinds, the same fixture (admitting only `'api-key'`, whose source declares `delegates`) fails the same way `[R4:NEST-r4-04]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `T-public-service-null`                        | the `publicService` fixture (public, unsafe, returns `service.getSession()`) with a valid cookie and an untrusted `Origin` gets `null`, and the adapter's session read counter stays 0 `[R2:SEC-r2-04]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `T-dynamic-base-url`                           | with `baseURL: { allowedHosts }` and no `fallback`: a transport that declares `requires.hostlessCalls` fails boot (B20); any other resolves every kit credential shape it supports, on every carrier it offers (HTTP, a WebSocket upgrade, a GraphQL operation over a WebSocket), without a 500, and so does the API-key source through it `[R4:BA-r4-03]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `T-reference-resolver`                         | federation shapes (`invokeEntities`): with `fieldResolverEnhancers` unset, a subgraph with the `reference` fixture fails boot (`REFERENCE_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`, `FEDERATION_FIELD_GUARDS_REQUIRED`); with `['guards', 'interceptors']`: an anonymous `_entities` call answers `UNAUTHENTICATED` for each entity; two representations with different `orgId`s in one call are decided independently (the second denied when only the first org allows it); `reader` under `_entities.N` reads the reference resolver's reading; with the `reference` fixture left out, `plain` and `reader` under `_entities` answer `NO_ENCLOSING_DECISION` (generic 500), never data `[R4:NEST-r4-01]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

`T-credentials`, `T-acceptance`, `T-infra-5xx`, `T-public-no-lookup`, `T-public-unclaimed-context`, `T-public-service-null`, `T-reads-session`, `T-unsatisfiable-kinds`, `T-inherited-handler` and `T-scope` map to no transport invariant (§4.2.2): they check behavior that core provides on top of T1–T10 (S6, per-route acceptance of principal kinds (ADR-35), `@Public()` doing no I/O, B15, the plan cache, the decorators' scope) through each transport, and `T-subscription-credentials` gates a preview feature.

**Principal-source cases** (P1–P7: `S-*`) and **policy cases** (Z1–Z6: `Z-*`) are smaller harnesses around a real instance, using the memory adapter plus better-auth's `testUtils()` (LEAD-V15). The instance runs with `session.updateAge: 0`, so any session-reading endpoint a unit calls produces a refresh `Set-Cookie`. The generic cases run against any source or policy:

| Id                      | Invariant | Asserts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

### 14.2 Matrix `[A][B][C]`

| Axis                       | Values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
