**ADR-66. Class-level access, acceptance and requirement metadata apply to the handlers a transport does not nest; nested handlers (GraphQL field resolvers) inherit unless they carry method-level metadata.**

- _Forced by:_ `[R3:NEST-r3-05]`. v3 gave every field resolver of a resolver class with class-level metadata a real plan. `@Resolver(() => Project) @RequireOrgMember({ organization: fromParam('orgId') })` then failed boot by default (`FIELD_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`); following the hint ran the guard once per field per list item, and `fromParam('orgId')` found no argument on `tasks`, so every item answered 403; `@Public()` on the field was rejected by B15 when it read the principal, and `@OptionalAuth()` was a real plan again. Class-level `@AcceptPrincipals('session', 'api-key')`, the usual way to open a resolver to keys, forced app-wide field guards.
- _Decision:_ §7.6 step 3; §9.2. `defaultAccessFor` answering `'inherit'` marks a nested handler; class-level `@UseAuthInstance`, `@SkipOriginCheck` and `@ForwardAuthCookies` still apply to it. The GraphQL units print `I_CLASS_METADATA_OPERATIONS_ONLY` for classes whose class-level declarations do not reach some of their field resolvers.
- _Rejected:_ keeping class propagation and adding `@InheritAuth()` plus a boot check for class-level refs that read `param()` on field resolvers (NEST's option B): every class-level requirement on a resolver becomes either a boot error or a per-item cost, and the check needs to know which refs read which inputs; applying class-level metadata to field resolvers only when `fieldResolverEnhancers` includes `'guards'`: the same source would mean different things depending on a GraphQL module option.
- _Rationale:_ it matches how Nest applications use class-level guards on resolvers (field resolvers get enhancers only on request), and a field that exposes data its operations do not authorize carries its own method-level requirement, which B16 then enforces or fails. The residual, a field resolver relying on a class-level requirement that no longer reaches it, is visible at boot (the info advice) and recorded as RK29 (§17 Q30).
- _Evidence:_ `@nestjs/graphql` 13.2.4 `services/resolvers-explorer.service.js:95-102`; REV2-NEST:`exp2-field-resolver-default-access.mjs`; cases `T-inherit-no-lookup`, the GraphQL job (§14.2), planner unit tests.
- _Revised in v5_ `[R4:NEST-r4-01]`: "a transport does not nest" now excludes federation reference resolvers explicitly. A `@ResolveReference()` handler is an entry point of `_entities`, so its class's access, acceptance and requirements and the instance's `defaultAccess` apply to it like to a query; v4's GraphQL units neither nested nor claimed it, and it ran unguarded (ADR-69). Field resolvers of the same class still inherit, now from the reference resolver's reading.

**ADR-67. Production is assumed unless `NODE_ENV` names development, dev or test; the environment-dependent flags are reported as their effective values; better-auth's public default secret fails a production boot, and its rate limiter being off in production is reported.**

- _Forced by:_ `[R3:SEC-r3-07]`. v3 keyed B23, B18, B19 and B27 on `NODE_ENV === 'production'`. A container that never set `NODE_ENV` and had no `baseURL` booted silently, although B23 exists for exactly that misconfiguration, and if `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` was missing too better-auth signed sessions with its public default secret, which it rejects only when `NODE_ENV === 'production'` (LEAD-V48). Separately, better-auth's `isTest()` is also true for a truthy `TEST`, which vitest sets in every worker, so both better-auth's and the kernel's origin checks were off in every vitest run that did not set `disableOriginCheck: false`, while v3's docs and B19 named `NODE_ENV=test` only.
- _Decision:_ §5.4 ("in production"), B19, B23, B29; the boot summary prints the assumed environment; §12.8, §14.1 and §14.4 set `disableOriginCheck: false` explicitly and document `TEST`.
- _Rejected:_ keeping `NODE_ENV=production` as the only trigger and printing "environment: unset (production checks skipped)" (SEC's second option): the checks fail closed only when someone reads the summary; reading `TEST` as "not production": a stray `TEST` in a deployed image would silence every production check, whereas B19 already reports what it does to the origin checks; our own secret-strength rules: better-auth validates secrets, and only its default is a known public value.
- _Rationale:_ development needs one variable, which better-auth's own documentation already asks for, and every unsafe deployment default now fails closed wherever `NODE_ENV` was forgotten (§17 Q33).
- _Revised in v5_ `[R4:BA-r4-02]`: the library's production is wider than better-auth's, and better-auth keys more than its secret check on `NODE_ENV === 'production'`: its rate limiter too (LEAD-V52). A deployment treated as production without `NODE_ENV=production` therefore ran with the limiter off, unlimited password and code guessing answered 401 and never 429, and B18, B27 and `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` described rate-limit buckets that did not exist (REV4-BA:`exp2-ratelimit-node-env.mjs`). B30 warns `W_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED` when `$context.rateLimit.enabled` is false and the option was not set explicitly, the boot summary prints `rate limit: on | off (why)`, and the IP-related warnings name session IPs while the limiter is off (§17 Q35).
  - _Rejected in v5:_ failing boot like B29 unless `rateLimit.enabled` is set (BA's option (b)): a disabled limiter is a legitimate setup behind an edge limiter, and better-auth makes it a default rather than an error; enabling the limiter ourselves: that means writing `auth.options` (S1).
- _Evidence:_ LEAD-V48; vitest 5.0.1 `dist/chunks/cli-api.DcLieX4F.js:414-416`, `dist/chunks/index.DzobfTyw.js:11750-11753` (cited in `reviews/round-3-SEC.md`); cases `LIB-environment`, the security e2e environment rows (§14.4).

**ADR-68. One logical request has bounded authorization side effects: an infrastructure or configuration error is logged once per request key, and distinct authorization calls per request are budgeted (`limits.maxAuthorizationCallsPerRequest`, default 100, then 429).**

- _Forced by:_ `[R3:SEC-r3-08]`. GraphQL runs the guard once per root field (and per guarded field per item). During an outage the memoized rejection made every alias throw a new, non-intrinsic internal error, and Nest's external exception handler logs each one: 500 aliases wrote 500 ERROR entries with cause stacks for one request. In normal operation 500 aliases naming 500 organizations made 500 parallel `hasPermission` calls, about 1,000 to 1,500 storage reads, for fields that were all denied.
- _Decision:_ §7.1 (the `repeated` flag), §9.2 (`BetterAuthGraphqlRepeatedInternalError`), §8.1 (the budget), §13.4.
- _Rejected:_ making every internal error intrinsic (nothing would be logged, ADR-43); a budget on decisions rather than on distinct better-auth calls (identical checks cost nothing after the first and should not count); bounding concurrency inside the library (a per-request semaphore would serialize legitimate list pages; query complexity limits belong to the GraphQL server); a default of 50 (SEC's example): a page of 100 items with a distinct check per item is an ordinary schema.
- _Revised in v5_ `[R4:SEC-r4-04]`: the bounds cover the re-classification read of a generic 401 as well: it is one budgeted, request-scoped memo entry shared by every invocation, so its failure is one error object that `repeated` logs once (ADR-59). v4's read escaped both bounds.
- _Evidence:_ `@nestjs/core` 11.1.17 `helpers/external-context-creator.js:71-79`, `exceptions/external-exceptions-handler.js:13-18` (cited in `reviews/round-3-SEC.md`); cases `T-internal-error-logged-once`, the security e2e budget row (§14.4), evaluator unit tests.

**ADR-69. Federation entry points are guarded like root fields: reference resolvers are never nested, federation subgraphs require field guards, each representation is its own invocation, and an inheriting handler whose lineage holds no enclosing reading fails instead of serving data.**

- _Forced by:_ `[R4:NEST-r4-01]`. The GraphQL units knew root resolvers and field resolvers. A federation subgraph's `_entities` query reaches an entity type's fields through its `@ResolveReference()` handler, which writes only `RESOLVER_REFERENCE_METADATA` and gets guards only with `fieldResolverEnhancers`, or through no Nest handler at all when the type has none. With default settings an anonymous `_entities` query returned the entity data that the `user(id)` query denied, and B16 passed; with field guards every representation shared one `info`, so a per-entity decision was reused for the next entity and `fromParam` found no arguments (REV4-NEST:`exp1-federation-reference.mjs`, both majors).
- _Decision:_ §9.2 "Federation entry points" and §7.1. In the GraphQL units: reference resolvers are entry points (class-level metadata and `defaultAccess` apply), claimed with `everyHandler` (`REFERENCE_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`); a federation subgraph with field or reference resolvers requires `fieldResolverEnhancers: ['guards']` (`FEDERATION_FIELD_GUARDS_REQUIRED`), both at `federationCoverage` (default `'error'`); a reference resolver's invocation is its representation, and its readings sit at `'<op>:_entities#<__typename>'`. In core, one transport-neutral rule over lineage data: an `inherit` plan whose transport supplies a lineage without an enclosing reading throws `NO_ENCLOSING_DECISION`, which closes `_entities` for entity types without a reference resolver.
- _Rejected:_
  - warning by default (NEST's option B, for subgraphs behind an authenticating router): whether a subgraph is reachable directly is a deployment fact the library cannot see, and §17 Q19 fails closed for every other surface the guard cannot reach; `'warn'` is one option away (§17 Q36);
  - detecting `@key` types at boot and reporting only those without a guarded reference resolver (NEST's `FEDERATION_ENTITY_UNGUARDED`): code-first keys are `@Directive('@key(…)')` entries that `@nestjs/graphql` stores lazily and loads only while `GraphQLModule` builds the schema, after the boot checks run (`decorators/directive.decorator.js`, `LazyMetadataStorage`), and schema-first keys are SDL the units would have to parse; reporting every type with field resolvers instead would fail boot for non-entity types. The runtime rule covers both schema styles exactly, and the boot requirement for field guards makes sure the rule can run;
  - keying the reference resolver's position by the representation's index: neither the guard's arguments nor a nested field's `info` carries the object identity of the representation, while the type name is on the path;
  - treating `_entities` as a root field of the library's own: it is @apollo/subgraph's resolver, not a Nest handler, so no plan exists for it.
- _Rationale:_ a subgraph's entities are reachable by any client that reaches the subgraph, so each entry point needs the same decision a root field gets, and a nested handler must not assume an authorization that never happened. Everything that names GraphQL stays in the GraphQL units; core only compares lineage data it already records.
- _Evidence:_ LEAD-V55; REV4-NEST:`exp1-federation-reference.mjs`; `@nestjs/graphql` 13.2.4 `services/resolvers-explorer.service.js:88-104`; @apollo/subgraph `dist/types.js:101-102` (cited in `reviews/round-4-NEST.md`); cases `T-reference-resolver`, the GraphQL job (§14.2), the security e2e federation row (§14.4); §17 Q36.

**ADR-70. A direct `auth.api` call that carries the caller's session cookie, in a handler scope whose unsafe browser leg carries a cookie, needs a passing origin verdict for that leg: otherwise it fails with `PUBLIC_HANDLER_USED_CALLER_SESSION`.**

- _Forced by:_ `[R4:SEC-r4-02]`. "Public means no identity" (ADR-57) stopped `BetterAuthService` from resolving the caller in a `@Public()` handler, but the design itself equips handlers with `headersFrom(req)`, and better-auth's origin check is router-only. A migrated `@AllowAnonymous()` endpoint that "does its own auth" through `auth.api.changeEmail({ headers: headersFrom(req), body })` acted as the victim of a cross-site form post: `updateUser` and `revokeSessions` succeeded cross-site while the router answered 403 `INVALID_ORIGIN` (REV4-SEC:`probe-public-direct-call-csrf.mjs`). The migration table mapped exactly such endpoints to `@Public()`.
- _Decision:_ §7.5 and §10.2. The scope interceptor gives such scopes (plans whose origin check is not `'off'`) a caller-session check; plugin before-hook entry 2 runs it for non-router, non-internal calls that carry the scope's own session-token cookie; the check reads the memoized verdicts of the leg (ADR-34) and better-auth's skip flags, and throws the generic configuration error where no verdict passed. The migration guide maps such endpoints to `@OptionalAuth()`.
- _Rejected:_
  - running the origin check at that call and throwing its 403 (SEC's option (b)): public handlers that deliberately act on the session would keep working, but the origin rule would gain a second entry point after the handler started, which Q27 and ADR-48 avoided; `@OptionalAuth()` already gives those handlers the check at one cookie-cache hit or one read;
  - leaving it to documentation: the unsafe pattern is a one-line mapping in the migration table, and only a security review would find it;
  - refusing every direct call with the caller's credential in public scopes, bearer and API-key headers included: those are not ambient, so no CSRF applies, and legitimate public handlers verify tokens that way;
  - checking in the guard for public plans: the guard cannot know whether the handler will make such a call, and checking every public unsafe request would reject cookie-carrying anonymous traffic that never touches the session.
- _Rationale:_ one rule, fail closed and loud during development, and no new origin-check path: the check only reads the verdict the guard computed for the same leg (§17 Q37).
- _Evidence:_ REV4-SEC:`probe-public-direct-call-csrf.mjs`; LEAD-V16; `BA/api/routes/update-user.ts:744-830`; cases `LIB-public-direct-call`, the security e2e row (§14.4).

## 17. Open questions and residual risks

### 17.1 Questions for the owner (genuine product trade-offs, each with a recommendation)

The owner answered **Q13 to Q34 on 2026-09-17, each with the recommended option**. They are decisions now, treated like D1 to D4: §17.1.2 keeps each with its options and its recommendation, and a finding can reopen one only by showing a concrete defect, whose fix must keep the decision or become a new question. **Q35 to Q37 are open** (§17.1.1): the round-4 reviewers proposed them, and the design applies the recommended answer to each until the owner decides, so answering "as recommended" changes nothing. Q1 to Q12 come from the v1 merge (§17.1.3). They predate the reviews and were not part of the question list the owner answered, which starts at Q13; the design applies each as recorded, and the owner can reopen any of them.

#### 17.1.1 Open questions `[R4]`

Q35 to Q37 are the user decisions the round-4 reviewers proposed. Each applies the proposing reviewer's recommendation.

| #   | Question                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Options                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Recommendation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Q35 | _(BA; open, proposed in review round 4)_ When better-auth's rate limiter is off in a deployment the library treats as production (`NODE_ENV` unset or `staging`), should boot warn or fail (BA-r4-02)?                                                                                             | (a) warn with `W_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED` and show an explicit `rateLimit.enabled: false` in the summary only. (b) fail boot like B29 (`DEFAULT_SECRET`) unless `rateLimit.enabled` is set explicitly                                                                                    | **(a), applied** (B30, ADR-67), as BA recommended. Unlike the default secret, a disabled limiter is a legitimate setup when an edge proxy or a WAF limits sign-in traffic, and better-auth makes it a default rather than an error; the warning and the summary line close the visibility gap without breaking boots. Choose (b) if brute-force protection must never depend on someone reading a warning; every deployment without `NODE_ENV=production` then adds one line.                                      |
| Q36 | _(NEST; open, proposed in review round 4)_ How strict should boot be about GraphQL federation entry points: reference resolvers no guard reaches, and subgraphs whose field resolvers run without field guards (NEST-r4-01)?                                                                       | (a) fail boot by default (`federationCoverage: 'error'`), like the other surfaces the guard cannot reach (§17 Q19), with `'warn' \| 'off'`. (b) warn by default, because most subgraphs sit behind an authenticating router and are not reachable directly; teams opt into `'error'` | **(a), applied** (ADR-69, ADR-40), as NEST recommended. Whether a subgraph is reachable directly is a deployment fact the library cannot see, and a reachable one served entity data to anonymous callers. Teams with private subgraphs set `'warn'` once, visibly. Choose (b) if most users run subgraphs only behind a router that authenticates, and the boot error would mainly cost migrations.                                                                                                               |
| Q37 | _(SEC; open, proposed in review round 4)_ What should happen when a `@Public()` handler's direct `auth.api.*` call carries the caller's own session cookie on an unsafe operation whose origin no guard verified (SEC-r4-02; not Q27, which covers the service's `getPrincipal()`/`getSession()`)? | (a) fail closed: throw `PUBLIC_HANDLER_USED_CALLER_SESSION` (a generic 500, logged) with the hint `@OptionalAuth()` or `@ForwardAuthCookies()`. (b) check lazily: run the memoized origin check at that call and throw its 403 on failure                                            | **(a), applied** (ADR-70), as SEC recommended. "Public means no identity" is already the model, `@OptionalAuth()` is the supported path, and the check only reads verdicts the guard computed, so the origin rule keeps one entry point. The cost: a public handler that deliberately acts on the session breaks loudly until it switches to `@OptionalAuth()` (one cookie-cache hit or one read per request). Choose (b) if such handlers are common enough to justify a second place where the origin rule runs. |

#### 17.1.2 Decided by the owner on 2026-09-17

Each row keeps the options and the recommendation as they stood when the owner answered. Where they came from:

- **Q13–Q17** are the product trade-offs the round-1 reviewers proposed and the lead did not settle alone, each naming the reviewer who raised it. **Q15's decided option differs from that reviewer's recommendation.** Q16 was reworded in v3, because v3 removed the cheaper admin modes its first option offered (ADR-36).
- **Q18–Q20** were decided by the lead in v2 (D3 delegates naming, ADR-40 sets the fail-closed stance, and an app has one HTTP adapter) and listed so that the owner could overrule them.
- **Q21–Q27** were decided by the lead in v3 `[R2]`, each with the reviewer's recommendation next to the lead's. **Q21 and Q27 differ from the proposing reviewer's recommendation**; the others apply it.
- **Q28–Q34** were decided by the lead in v4 `[R3]`, the same way. **Q29 extends the proposing reviewer's recommendation** (the stored role for every app, not only `customSession` apps; its mechanism was corrected in v5, BA-r4-01), and Q32 prints the global guard order at boot where the reviewer proposed a warning; the others apply the recommendation as proposed.

| Q13 | _(BA)_ Should `Set-Cookie` from **application-level** direct `auth.api.*` calls (in handlers and services, under the scope interceptor) be forwarded to the caller's response by default? (c) on by default, with a module switch and a boot warning that lists handlers calling credential endpoints                                                    | **Decided by the owner on 2026-09-17: the recommended option.** **(b), the v2 default** (ADR-48). Even when forwarding is on, only calls with the caller's credential or none are forwarded.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

(b) on by default, using better-auth's trusted origins, matcher and disable flags; opt out per route (`@SkipOriginCheck()`) or per instance (`originCheck.mode: 'off'`). (c) opt-in only: a decorator or module flag, off by default                                                                                                                                                                                              | **Decided by the owner on 2026-09-17: the recommended option.** **(b), the v2 default** (ADR-34). The library creates these cookie-authenticated surfaces, and better-auth's own check is router-only (LEAD-V16). CORS never covers form posts or WebSocket upgrades. Callers that send no cookie (bearer, API-key and RPC clients) are untouched. Cost: non-browser clients that send cookies on unsafe requests must send a trusted `Origin` or be exempted (RK21). Both reviewers recommended enforcing it on WebSocket and subscription handshakes whatever is chosen for HTTP, so (a) and (c) are choices about HTTP methods and GraphQL mutations only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

(b) allow when no browser signal is present, and reject when an `Origin` or `Referer` is present and untrusted, or `Sec-Fetch-Site` says cross-site                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | **Decided by the owner on 2026-09-17: the recommended option.** **(a), the v2 default; (b) ships as `originCheck.missingOrigin: 'allow-non-browser'`.** SEC recommended (b) as the default with a `strict` switch, so this is a real choice. For (a): it is what better-auth does, so an SSR server that calls better-auth's own `/sign-out` with forwarded cookies already has to send `Origin`, and one rule is easier to reason about than two. For (b): browsers always send `Origin` on cross-site unsafe requests and on WebSocket upgrades, so browser CSRF stays blocked, and SSR/BFF backends keep working after migration without a change. Note that SEC's literal rule ("no `Sec-Fetch-*` at all") would not exempt Node's `fetch`, which sends `sec-fetch-mode: cors` (LEAD-EXP-4); the shipped lenient mode keys on `Origin`, `Referer` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` only. It restores the parity §8.4 claims: a banned admin is locked out on the next request, not five minutes later (REV-SEC:`probe-stale-admin.mjs`). The extra read applies only to routes with an admin requirement; since v4 such a route also reads the stored user row for the role (Q29), so it costs two reads. (b) and (c) also judge an API key's mocked session (`enableSessionForAPIKeys`) with the owner's admin role, which better-auth's admin endpoints never do (BA-r2-06); choosing them needs a credential check the design does not have.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

(b) make `organization` a required option of `orgPermission()`/`orgMember()`                                                                                                                           | **Decided by the owner on 2026-09-17: the recommended option.** **(a), the v2 default** (§8.3). The default is faithful to better-auth and right for apps built around the active organization. The dangerous pattern, acting on an `orgId` input while authorizing against the active org (an IDOR), is detectable from the inputs transports claim (HTTP route params and GraphQL `@Args` names since v4, §8.3 `[R3:NEST-r3-10]`), and the warning names the fix (`fromParam('orgId')`). | #   | Question                                                                                                             | Options                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Recommendation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Q1  | Ship a role-name decorator (`@RequireRole`)?                                                                         | (a) none; permissions only plus the §15.3 recipe ([B][C]). (b) ship a `RolePolicy` in `./admin` that mirrors better-auth's parsing exactly, including `adminUserIds`/`defaultRole` ([A]). (c) the reference's trimming semantics | **(a) in 1.0.** (b) reimplements admin-plugin internals that can drift from better-auth (R1). (c) creates privilege differences. Revisit if better-auth adds a role-check API or users ask repeatedly.                                                                                                                                       |
| Q2  | Default WebSocket principal reuse                                                                                    | per message (`principalTtlMs: 0`, [A][C]) vs per connection for 300 s ([B])                                                                                                                                                      | **Per message.** It is secure by default. With the session source it costs one read per message and no writes (refresh is suppressed). A source that consumes quota or writes per resolution (API keys) does so per message, and boot warns about it (`W_QUOTA_PER_MESSAGE`) `[R1:SEC-r1-14]`. Document `principalTtlMs` for chat workloads. |
| Q3  | Should a method-level `@Public()`/`@OptionalAuth()` opt out of class-level requirements?                             | allow as a visible exception ([C]) vs boot error, fail-closed ([A])                                                                                                                                                              | **Allow.** It fits the common "one public endpoint in a protected controller" case and is Nest-idiomatic. Same-level contradictions still fail boot, and the boot summary counts public handlers.                                                                                                                                            |
| Q4  | Two live Nest apps sharing one better-auth instance                                                                  | exclusive: boot error ([B][C]) vs shared with per-app routing ([A])                                                                                                                                                              | **Exclusive.** It surfaces double side effects and forgotten `app.close()` early. Concurrent apps create one instance each. ### 17.2 Residual risks

Ratings are likelihood / impact. Where round 1 changed a rating, the v1 value is given; where round 2 did, the v2 value; where round 3 did, the v3 value; where round 4 did, the v4 value. RK32 to RK36 are new in v5 `[R4]`.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| RK1  | Reliance on better-auth surfaces its own integrations use but does not formally document: `ctx._flag`, `ctx.context.responseHeaders`/`returned` in after-hooks, `setShouldSkipSessionRefresh` semantics, `getPlugin()` returning the user's plugin object, `init().options` defu merge, `auth.api[*].path`. Added by v2: `$context.authCookies`, `$context.isTrustedOrigin` reading `this.trustedOrigins`, `$context.skipCSRFCheck`/`skipOriginCheck`, `$context.adapter.findOne` with the logical model name `apikey` (the outage probe), and the shape of `verifyApiKey` results. Added by v3: after-hooks being skipped for a before-hook short-circuit and `ctx.context.returned` being the object the caller receives (ADR-54), `$context.adapter.updateMany` returning a count for zero matches, `getActiveMember` returning `organizationId`. Added by v4: `$context.internalAdapter.findUserById` returning `role`, `banned` and `banExpires` (the admin policy), `$context.secret` and the default-secret literal (B29), the `key` column of the `apikey` model (the probe), and Nest's `ApplicationConfig.getGlobalGuards()`/`getGlobalInterceptors()` at `onModuleInit` (B16) `[R3]`. Added by v5: `$context.rateLimit.enabled` and `$context.options.rateLimit` (B30, LEAD-V52), `userHasPermission` reading the stored user for a `userId`-only body and answering a missing one with 400 `user not found` (LEAD-V51, RK35), `getPlugin()` returning one object to every instance that shares a plugins array (B03), the JWT plugin's `getJwks` endpoint (§4.3.4, LEAD-V53), and Nest's `RESOLVER_REFERENCE_METADATA` and `ModuleRef.get` resolving an overridden class token (B16) `[R4]` | low / high                                                                                                        | CI against 1.7.0, latest and a nightly job against the newest version inside the peer range, pre-releases included, plus `main` from source (§14.2, BA-r2-09); `LIB-dispatcher-parity` and `LIB-origin-differential` (§14.5); a dedicated test per surface; a protocol-versioned handle (B04); LEAD-V33 checked the v2 additions at the floor; `LIB-environment` derives the default-secret literal from better-auth on every matrix version                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| RK35 | The admin policy recognizes a user deleted between the guard's read and its `userHasPermission` call by status 400 and the message `user not found`, because better-auth gives that error no body code (LEAD-V51). A reworded message would turn that rare 401 into a logged 500 (Z2's "another 4xx") `[R4:BA-r4-01]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | low / low                                                                                                         | `Z-admin-deleted-user` pins the message on every better-auth version of the matrix, floor, latest and pre-release, so a change fails CI before release; the window is a user deletion during one request; upstream proposal: give the error a code                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| RK36 | A GraphQL context **function** that returns one cached object shares the first request across callers. Boot cannot see it, and `isLive` catches it only once that first request has been answered: while it is still running, a concurrent operation from another caller is indistinguishable from its own `[R4:SEC-r4-03]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | low / high                                                                                                        | a context **object**, the common form of the mistake, fails boot (`GRAPHQL_STATIC_CONTEXT`); after the first response every stale use fails with `GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_STALE_REQUEST`, so the defect surfaces on the second request in any test; the docs show the per-request factory; `T-stale-context`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## 18. Changelog

- **v5.0** (2026-09-17), lead architect. Revision after review round 4. All three reviewers rejected v4, with 15 new findings (0 blockers, 6 majors, 9 minors); every round-3 finding, and the three round-2 findings round 3 had marked unresolved, were marked resolved. All 15 were accepted. The three user decisions the reviewers proposed are applied as each reviewer recommended and recorded as open questions (Q35 to Q37). `ledger.md` has the resolution of each, §16 the decisions (ADR-69 and ADR-70 are new, 22 older ones were revised), and §17 the questions and five new risks. Two mechanisms were replaced rather than patched: the plugin no longer becomes inert at shutdown (a closed binding keeps its hooks), and the admin policy no longer copies the stored role (better-auth's endpoint reads it).
  - **Owner decisions.** The owner answered §17 Q13 to Q34 on 2026-09-17, each with the recommended option. §17.1 now separates the open questions (Q35 to Q37, §17.1.1) from the decided ones (§17.1.2, each marked "Decided by the owner on 2026-09-17: the recommended option", with its options and recommendation kept) and from the v1-merge questions (Q1 to Q12, §17.1.3). The header, §0.4 and §1 say so. The design already applied every recommendation, so no mechanism changed because of the answers.
  - **Shutdown and the plugin** (§5.7, §10.2, §10.6, ADR-31, ADR-25, ADR-53).
    - `onApplicationShutdown` closes a binding instead of unbinding it; a closed binding keeps dispatching the application's Nest hooks until another application binds, so work that a global module drains later in the same shutdown (a BullMQ worker) cannot skip a `@BeforeDatabase` rule. Inert remains the state of a plugin that was never bound. `BridgeHandle.bound`/`unbind()` became `state`/`close()`, and the protocol is version 4 `[SEC-r4-01]`.
    - One plugin object serves one instance: B03 fails boot with `PLUGIN_SHARED_BETWEEN_INSTANCES` when two instances resolve the same handle, and `bind()` throws for a second instance of the same owner `[BA-r4-05]`.
  - **Security.**
    - A direct `auth.api` call that carries the caller's session cookie, in a handler scope whose unsafe browser leg carries a cookie and has no passing origin verdict (a `@Public()` handler), fails with `PUBLIC_HANDLER_USED_CALLER_SESSION`: the scope interceptor supplies `ScopeView.checkCallerSession`, and plugin before-hook entry 2 runs it. The check only reads the guard's verdicts. Migration maps such `@AllowAnonymous()` handlers to `@OptionalAuth()` (§7.5, §15, ADR-70, §17 Q37) `[SEC-r4-02]`.
    - The GraphQL units fail boot for a context object (`GRAPHQL_STATIC_CONTEXT`), and the HTTP branch requires `HttpRequestAccessor.isLive` where implemented (`GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_STALE_REQUEST`), so a context shared across requests can no longer authenticate every caller as the first one (§9.2, ADR-61) `[SEC-r4-03]`.
    - The re-classification read of a generic 401 is shared per logical request in the policy I/O memo and counted against the authorization budget, so an outage costs one read and one ERROR line per request, not one per alias (§8.1, ADR-59, ADR-68) `[SEC-r4-04]`.
    - Origin-denial WARN lines use an hourly window with a summary line instead of a lifetime cap, and a `Referer` is logged as its origin (§7.10, ADR-34, ADR-52) `[SEC-r4-05]`.
  - **GraphQL.**
    - Federation: `@ResolveReference()` handlers are entry points, never nested, claimed with `everyHandler` (`REFERENCE_RESOLVER_UNGUARDED`); federation subgraphs with field or reference resolvers require field guards (`FEDERATION_FIELD_GUARDS_REQUIRED`), both at `federationCoverage` (default `'error'`, §17 Q36); each representation is its own invocation, with positions per entity type; an inheriting handler whose lineage holds no enclosing reading fails with `NO_ENCLOSING_DECISION` instead of serving data (§9.2, §7.1, ADR-69, ADR-40, ADR-56, ADR-66) `[NEST-r4-01]`.
    - Inherit plans take the nearest enclosing reading whatever its instance, and a nested public plan records nothing, so what a nested reader sees no longer depends on the instance of the shared field resolver or on `fieldResolverEnhancers` (`RoutePlan.nested`, §7.8, ADR-64) `[NEST-r4-03]`.
    - A `subscriptionCredentials` override keeps the upgrade request's `host`, `x-forwarded-host` and `x-forwarded-proto` unless it sets them, and invariant T5 requires them for every credential mapping of a transport that makes no host-less calls (§9.2, ADR-60) `[BA-r4-03]`.
  - **better-auth fidelity.**
    - The admin policy calls `userHasPermission({ body: { userId, permissions } })` without a role, so better-auth reads the stored user and applies `defaultRole` and `adminUserIds` itself; a NULL role (every user that predates `admin()`) no longer answers 500. The delegated path passes the row's role only when it is a non-empty string; the endpoint's 400 `user not found` maps to 401 `USER_NOT_FOUND` (§8.3, ADR-36, ADR-13, §17 Q29's mechanism) `[BA-r4-01]`.
    - B30 `W_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED` warns when better-auth's rate limiter is off in a deployment the library treats as production without `NODE_ENV=production`; the boot summary prints the limiter's state, and B18, B27 and `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` stop describing rate-limit buckets while it is off (§5.4, §6.8, ADR-67, §17 Q35) `[BA-r4-02]`.
    - The JWT-source sketch verifies with jose over the instance's JWKS and lets key-fetch and storage errors throw, because `verifyJWT` reports them as invalid tokens (§4.3.4, ADR-13, RK18) `[BA-r4-04]`.
  - **Coverage and planning.**

    - `PrincipalSource.delegates` makes delegation static data, and B15 counts a policy without kinds as admitting exactly the non-delegating sources' kinds, so a kind-less company policy in `defaultRequirements` next to API-key routes fails boot (§4.3.1, §5.4, ADR-35, ADR-58) `[NEST-r4-04]`.

Invariants H10, T5, T6, T7, T8, T10, P5 and Z2 were rewritten; units U1, U2, U7 to U11, U13 and U16 (§3.1) were updated.

- **v4.0** (2026-09-17), lead architect. Revision after review round 3. All three reviewers rejected v3, with 23 new findings (0 blockers, 12 majors, 11 minors), and marked three round-2 findings unresolved (NEST-r2-06, NEST-r2-07, SEC-r2-02). All were accepted; SEC-r3-04 with the reviewer's second option (the per-call-site forwarding switch is removed rather than given its own origin check). `ledger.md` has the resolution of each, §16 the decisions (ADR-64 to ADR-68 are new, 28 older ones were revised), and §17 seven more lead-decided questions (Q28 to Q34) and two new risks. Three mechanisms were simplified rather than patched: v3's six ways to read a principal became one lookup, the gateway heuristic became a canary, and the per-call-site forwarding switch was removed.
  - **Reading the principal** (§7.8, ADR-64, ADR-57) `[NEST-r3-01, NEST-r2-06, NEST-r3-02, NEST-r2-07]`.
    - The carrier map by memo key, its exactly-one rule and the readers' `peek()` are gone. The guard records each reading on the invocation and at its lineage position (the GraphQL response path), and every reader uses one lookup: public plans read no identity, inheriting field resolvers the nearest enclosing invocation's reading, other plans their own. A nested field can no longer read a sibling root field's principal or fail depending on scheduling.
    - `principalFor(ctx)` is total: `'no-identity'` on public plans, and `PRINCIPAL_READ_BEFORE_GUARD` instead of `undefined` in a guard that runs before `BetterAuthGuard`, such as an `APP_GUARD` declared in `AppModule`. B16 counts a `BetterAuthGuard` the app registers itself, and the boot summary prints the global guard order.
  - **Planning** (§7.6).
    - A single `PolicyResolver` resolves policy references before plans compile, so a DI policy's instance-level `requires` (kinds, `freshIdentity`) reaches its plans (ADR-65) `[NEST-r3-04]`.
    - Class-level access, acceptance and requirements apply to operation handlers; GraphQL field resolvers inherit unless they carry method-level metadata (ADR-66) `[NEST-r3-05]`.
    - `@SkipDefaultRequirements()` and B15 `UNSATISFIABLE_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` make `defaultRequirements` composable with machine routes (ADR-58) `[NEST-r3-06]`.
  - **better-auth fidelity.**
    - Only the generic 401 (no code, or `UNAUTHORIZED`) is re-classified, and only for principals from a session-backed source; coded 401s deny 403; `customSession` apps answer 401 for a policy-path outage, as documented (§8.1, ADR-59) `[BA-r3-01, BA-r3-05]`.
    - The admin policy passes the stored user row's role, never a `customSession` shape's (§8.3, ADR-36) `[BA-r3-02]`.
    - The API-key probe is keyed on the `key` column, type-safe under every `generateId` mode, and `verifyApiKey` receives the forwarding headers better-auth reads for a dynamic base URL (§8.3.1, ADR-42, ADR-60) `[BA-r3-03, BA-r3-04]`.
    - The `orgSlug` hint maps slugs through `listOrganizations` (§8.3, ADR-63) `[BA observation on BA-r2-08]`.
  - **Security.**
    - The origin check trusts a leg's own origin only for an unset `baseURL`, and `upgradeRequestUrl()` reads no forwarding headers, which closes a socket hijack through `X-Forwarded-Host` on socket.io's polling handshake (§7.10, ADR-34) `[SEC-r3-02]`.
    - Origin denials are logged at WARN once per reason and origin, and the session unit advises about native clients when the `expo()` plugin meets the strict default (§7.10) `[SEC-r3-03]`.
    - A slow `INVALID_API_KEY` counts as infrastructure, so a lock on the key's own row no longer answers 401; the probe's coverage claim is corrected (§8.3.1, RK18, RK31) `[SEC-r3-01, SEC-r2-02]`.
    - `service.forwardCookies(fn)` is removed; forwarding is declared where the guard applies the form-CSRF rule, and `forwardForeignCookies(fn)` serves account switching inside such handlers (§7.5, ADR-48) `[SEC-r3-04]`.
    - GraphQL contexts take the HTTP branch only when their request is positively the platform's (`HttpRequestAccessor.isRequest`); unrecognized contexts fail with `GRAPHQL_CONTEXT_UNRECOGNIZED` (§9.2, ADR-61) `[SEC-r3-05]`.
    - The delegated admin path denies keys of banned owners (§8.3, ADR-36) `[SEC-r3-06]`.
    - Production is assumed unless `NODE_ENV` names development, dev or test; B19 reports effective skip flags, including vitest's `TEST=true`; B29 rejects better-auth's default secret in production (§5.4, ADR-67) `[SEC-r3-07]`.
    - An infrastructure error is logged once per logical request, and distinct authorization calls per request are budgeted (§8.1, §13.4, ADR-68) `[SEC-r3-08]`.
  - **Lifecycle and coverage.**
    - The lifecycle state belongs to the application that owns the container and is reset at shutdown; a second application from one compiled `TestingModule` is prepared again on Fastify and fails with `APP_ADAPTER_CHANGED` on Express (§5.7, ADR-62) `[NEST-r3-03]`.
    - `UNGUARDED_AUTH_METADATA` has a closed trigger list that leaves hook providers alone (B16) `[NEST-r3-07]`.
    - Boot canaries check every Nest-owned metadata literal on the installed Nest and replace the gateway class-claim heuristic (B16, §12.4) `[NEST-r3-08]`.
    - Both GraphQL units handle every `'graphql'` context and check the driver at boot (§9.2) `[NEST-r3-09]`.
    - `RoutePlan.routeParams` is replaced by transport-supplied inputs in claims (§4.2.1, ADR-41) `[NEST-r3-10]`.
  - **Contracts.** `TransportCall.carrier` became `lineage` (`InvocationLineage`); `AuthTransport` gained `lineage()` and `toInternalException`'s `repeated` flag; `ClaimOptions` gained `inputs`; `BootAdviceContext.plans` became `handlers` (`AdvisedHandler`), and `BootAdviceContext` gained `originCheck`; `HttpRequestAccessor` gained `isRequest`; `HttpPlatform.capabilities` gained `prepareAtInit`; `PrincipalSource` gained `sessionBacked`; `PrincipalResolver` lost `peek`, and `ResolutionRequest.bypassMemo` became `reclassify`; `BetterAuthService.principalFor` returns `PrincipalReading`, and `forwardCookies` became `forwardForeignCookies`; `RoutePlan` lost `routeParams` and gained `declares` and `skipsDefaultRequirements`; `AuthContextView` gained `secret` and `internalAdapter.findUserById`; `ApiKeyPrincipalOptions.outageProbe` takes `{ slowMs }`; new runtime option `limits.maxAuthorizationCallsPerRequest`, decorator `@SkipDefaultRequirements()` and class `BetterAuthGraphqlRepeatedInternalError`. The plugin protocol is unchanged (3).

- **v3.0** (2026-09-17), lead architect. Revision after review round 2. All three reviewers rejected v2, with 34 new findings (3 blockers, 13 majors, 18 minors) and one round-1 finding still unresolved (SEC-r1-01, for WebSockets and subscriptions). All were accepted; four in a modified form (BA-r2-08: no slug ref, because the only slug lookup writes; NEST-r2-06: an invocation stamp plus a single-entry carrier rule instead of decorators computing memo keys they cannot know without DI; SEC-r2-04: public handlers get no identity instead of a lazily origin-checked one; SEC-r2-09: resolved through inheritance plus a warning). `ledger.md` has the resolution of each, §16 the decisions (ADR-54 to ADR-63 are new, 25 older ones were revised), and §17 seven more lead-decided questions (Q21 to Q27) and three new risks.
  - **Blockers.**
    - An authoritative identity read accepts only a session the get-session endpoint produced, observed by a new plugin after-hook, so an API key's mocked session (`enableSessionForAPIKeys`) no longer passes `@RequirePermission` with its owner's role; the session source tolerates the missing `Headers` of a short-circuited dispatch (§7.3, ADR-54) `[BA-r2-06, BA-r2-01]`.
    - Route plans are cached per (controller class, handler), because Nest shares inherited handler functions between subclasses (§7.6, ADR-55) `[NEST-r2-01]`.
    - The origin check has no explicit-credential exemption: any cookie on an unsafe or WebSocket browser leg needs a trusted origin, whatever `handshake.auth` or `connectionParams` hold, as on better-auth's routes; core keeps no scheme list (§7.10, ADR-34) `[SEC-r2-01, NEST-r2-13, SEC-r1-01]`.
  - **Coverage and planning.**
    - Coverage is one core rule over handler claims that transports supply; a forgotten transport or `globalGuard: false` can no longer leave written requirements unenforced; explicit coverage needs guard and interceptor; `'websockets:message_mapping'` is pinned and cannot pass vacuously (B16, ADR-40) `[NEST-r2-02, NEST-r2-11, NEST-r2-12]`.
    - The guard reads the plan before choosing a transport, so public handlers (other than form-checked login proxies) work in any context and credential-less RPC messages get 401, not 500 (§7.1, §9.4, ADR-55) `[NEST-r2-03]`.
    - GraphQL field resolvers without their own metadata inherit their root field's decision (`defaultAccessFor`), and `W_FIELD_RESOLVER_INHERITS` points at field resolvers reachable from public root fields (§9.2, ADR-56) `[NEST-r2-04, SEC-r2-09]`.
    - `defaultRequirements` replaces the `planFor` subclass seam, and the guard's runtime param-kind check is gone (§7.6, ADR-58) `[NEST-r2-08]`.
    - The principal memo key uses a content key for the source set; the stamps hold each invocation's own result plus an operation-wide map by memo key with a single-entry rule (§7.2, §7.8) `[NEST-r2-16, NEST-r2-06]`.
  - **Reading the principal.** `BetterAuthService.principalFor(ctx)` serves guards and interceptors; `getPrincipal()`/`getSession()` never resolve, return `null` on public plans and throw `NO_AUTH_SCOPE` outside a handler scope; principal param decorators lost `instance` (§7.8, ADR-57) `[NEST-r2-07, SEC-r2-04, NEST-r2-14]`.
  - **better-auth fidelity.**
    - A 401 that escapes a policy is re-classified by one authoritative re-resolution, so storage failures swallowed by better-auth's session middleware answer 5xx, not 403 (§8.1, ADR-59) `[BA-r2-03]`.
    - Units declare host-less server calls, and a dynamic `baseURL` without `fallback` fails boot when one does (B20, ADR-60) `[BA-r2-05]`.
    - The DB update dispatcher returns only what hooks returned (§10.6) `[BA-r2-02]`; `@AfterAuth('/get-session')` rules are scoped to Nest routes (§10.4) `[BA-r2-07]`; the client-IP header's interaction with better-auth's `trustedProxies` is documented and warned (§6.8, B18) `[BA-r2-04]`.
    - Organization refs resolve to validated IDs, the default ref included, with tuple memo keys; no slug ref ships (§8.3, ADR-63) `[BA-r2-08, SEC-r2-06]`.
    - The admin policy lost its `'role'` and `'cached'` modes (ADR-36).
  - **Security.**
    - GraphQL operations are classified by carrier: queries and mutations over graphql-ws or Mercurius `fullWsTransport` are cookie-less and origin-checked like subscriptions (§9.2, ADR-61) `[SEC-r2-03]`.
    - The API-key outage probe adds a no-op write (§8.3.1) `[SEC-r2-02]`.
    - WebSocket browser legs have absolute URLs, and the origin verdict is computed once per leg (§7.10) `[SEC-r2-05]`.
    - Authoritative plans never reuse a connection's principal (§7.2) `[SEC-r2-07]`.
    - Handlers with `@ForwardAuthCookies()` get better-auth's form-CSRF rule, public ones included, and B16 requires a guard to reach them (§7.10, §5.4) `[SEC-r2-08]`.
  - **Lifecycle and tests.** The core module's lifecycle work runs once per application and a same-owner `bind()` is a no-op (`NestMicroservice.init()`); an adapter that never emitted counts as none, and a late one fails with `LATE_HTTP_ADAPTER` (§5.7, ADR-62) `[NEST-r2-05, NEST-r2-09]`. B26 counts database writes (§10.2) `[NEST-r2-10]`. `POLICY_INVOKER` (a core-module provider) and `overrideDecisions` let tests stub policies, and `overridePrincipal` answers the 401 re-classification read `absent`, so an unstubbed organization requirement denies 401 (§14.8) `[NEST-r2-15]`. The better-auth pre-release job targets the newest version inside the peer range (§14.2) `[BA-r2-09]`.
  - **Contracts.** `AuthTransport` gained `defaultAccessFor` and `requires`; `TransportValidationContext` gained `claim` and lost `globalGuard`, `isGuardApplied` and `isPublic`; `BrowserExposure` lost `ambientCookie` and gained `key`; `AuthHandle.checkOrigin` takes a mode, and `producedByEndpoint` is new; `OriginCheckOptions.explicitCredentialHeaders` and `BetterAuthGuard.planFor` are removed; the bridge protocol is version 3; `RoutePlan` gained `'inherit'`, `sourceSet` and an origin-check mode.
  - **Conformance and tests.** New cases: `T-public-unclaimed-context`, `T-csrf-http-cookie-plus-token`, `T-csrf-login-proxy`, `T-ws-origin-junk-token`, `T-ws-origin-dynamic-baseurl`, `T-ws-origin-function-trusted-origins`, `T-subscription-origin-junk-connection-params`, `T-stamp-per-plan`, `T-inherited-handler`, `T-inherit-no-lookup`, `T-coverage-claims`, `T-public-service-null`, `S-dynamic-base-url`, `S-apikey-write-outage`, `S-short-circuit-session`, `Z-policy-session-lost`, `Z-admin-rejects-api-key-session`, `Z-admin-dynamic-base-url`, `Z-org-ref-types`, `H-late-adapter`, and the repository tests `LIB-coverage-rule`, `LIB-authoritative-session`, `LIB-principal-for`, `LIB-testing-override-decisions`. Extended: `T-selection` (with and without credentials), `T-no-credentials` (RPC messages without a carrier), `T-memo-once`, `T-csrf-http-unsafe` (no session read before the check), `T-ws-origin-untrusted` (a function-valued `trustedOrigins` once per socket), `T-subscription-origin`, `T-reads-session` (a third boot with `defaultRequirements`), `T-internal-error-generic` (its unguarded part runs under a replaced guard, because `globalGuard: false` now fails boot there), `Z-apierror-mapping` (401 re-classified), `Z-infra-throws`, `Z-admin-banned`, `Z-admin-deleted-user`, `Z-apikey-quota-per-request`, `H-ip-platform` and `H-no-adapter`. Invariant T10 added; T1, T6, T8, Z2 and Z5 rewritten. The transport kit's fixtures gained `tripleMixed` (and `triple` became three methods), `loginProxy`, `publicService`, `inherited` and the GraphQL `graph` fixtures with `invokeGraph`; fixture handlers receive the service (`FixtureContext`); `createApp` takes an `override` for the replaced-guard boot, and `supportsUnguardedHandler` is gone. The dispatcher parity and origin differential tests are named `LIB-dispatcher-parity` and `LIB-origin-differential`; the first got a preceding plugin, the second the cookie-plus-token and form rows.
  - **Boot checks.** B16 changed most: coverage is one core rule over transport claims, "declares something" is defined once, and a form-checked `@Public()` handler is not covered by its access. B04 (protocol 3), B06 (a same-owner `bind()` is a no-op), B15 (kinds that `defaultRequirements` name), B18 (`trustedProxies` with the plugin's header), B20 (an error for units that make host-less calls), B21 (`W_FIELD_RESOLVER_INHERITS`), B22 (the inherit count) and B26 (database writes) changed too (§5.4).
  - **Decision log and questions.** ADR-54 to ADR-63 added, and 25 ADRs revised with the round-2 findings that forced each change (§16). Q21 to Q27 record the reviewers' proposed user decisions, decided by the lead; Q14 and Q16 were reworded. RK27 to RK29 added; RK1, RK2, RK3, RK4, RK9, RK11, RK16, RK18, RK20, RK21 and RK24 revised.
  - **Verification.** LEAD-V36 to LEAD-V42 (source re-checks) and LEAD-EXP-8 to LEAD-EXP-10 (`tmp-r2-revise/`: the endpoint-result observation against better-auth's admin verdict, the no-op write probe, the corrected DB dispatcher), each run on better-auth 1.7.0 and 1.7.4. The reviewers' experiments decided BA-r2-01 to 07, NEST-r2-01, 03, 04, 05, 09 and SEC-r2-01, 02, 06. The lead's own runs reproduce the observations the new mechanisms rest on: the short-circuit's missing headers and better-auth's admin 401 for a key session (LEAD-EXP-8, BA-r2-01, BA-r2-06), the read-only store's `INVALID_API_KEY` (LEAD-EXP-9, SEC-r2-02) and the reverted update (LEAD-EXP-10, BA-r2-02).
- **v2.0** (2026-09-11 to 2026-09-17), lead architect. Revision after review round 1. The three reviewers (BA: better-auth fidelity; NEST: NestJS correctness, packaging, SOLID; SEC: security and operations) all rejected v1, with 43 findings: 4 blockers, 19 majors and 20 minors. All 43 were accepted; one in a modified form (SEC-r1-17), and three are duplicates of others (SEC-r1-09, SEC-r1-10, SEC-r1-12). `ledger.md` has the resolution of each, §16 the decisions (ADR-34 to ADR-53 are new, 30 older ones were revised), and §17 the questions and risks that came out of it.
  - **Who may call what (blockers).**
    - better-auth's origin rule now covers every operation that an ambient cookie authenticated: unsafe HTTP methods, GraphQL mutations, every WebSocket message and subscription. It uses better-auth's own trusted origins, matcher and disable flags (§7.10, ADR-34) `[SEC-r1-01, BA-r1-03]`.
    - Principal kinds are admitted per route (`kinds`, `acceptance`, `@AcceptPrincipals`, kinds named by requirements). Delegated principals (API keys, OAuth tokens) are never widened beyond their own grant: invariant Z5 and `PrincipalDelegation` (§7.6, §8.1, ADR-35) `[BA-r1-01, SEC-r1-02]`.
    - Authorization decisions are memoized per handler invocation (`TransportCall.invocation`), never per request or connection. Policy I/O is deduped by concrete inputs, and `@ActiveOrganizationId()` is per invocation (§7.2, ADR-37) `[NEST-r1-01]`.
  - **Authorization details.**
    - The admin `permission()` reads identity authoritatively by default (`requires.freshIdentity`), so a banned admin is locked out at once, as on better-auth's own admin endpoints (§8.4, ADR-36) `[SEC-r1-04]`.
    - better-auth's 400 `user not found` is a 401 `USER_NOT_FOUND`, no longer a 500 `[BA-r1-10]`.
    - Connection-level principal entries hold only `authenticated` and `absent` `[SEC-r1-13]`.
  - **Cookies and the plugin.**
    - `Set-Cookie` of application direct `auth.api` calls is no longer forwarded by default. Forwarding is opt-in (`@ForwardAuthCookies()`, `cookies.forwardDirectCalls`, `service.forwardCookies`) and limited to calls that carry the caller's own credential or none (§7.5, ADR-48) `[BA-r1-02, SEC-r1-03]`.
    - The client-IP header name is random per plugin instance (ADR-44) `[SEC-r1-18]`. The plugin counts dispatches made before binding (B26, ADR-53) `[NEST-r1-11]`. The bridge protocol is version 2.
  - **API keys** (§8.3.1, ADR-42).
    - A result-mapping table for `verifyApiKey`: 429 with `Retry-After`, 401, or 5xx. A throttled outage probe, the `references` option for organization-owned keys, and declared `effects` `[BA-r1-04, SEC-r1-05, SEC-r1-14]`.
    - The `enableSessionForAPIKeys` quota multiplier is documented, tested and announced as boot advice by the session unit, triggered by the api-key plugin's presence (`session.apiKeySessions` states the unreadable option) `[BA-r1-05]`.
  - **Lifecycle and HTTP platforms.**
    - A last-arrival mount coordinator replaces platform selection inside the `init$` replay, and a `null` adapter means "no HTTP" (§5.7, ADR-38) `[NEST-r1-02, NEST-r1-03]`.
    - The Fastify auth scope has a child error handler: failures reach Nest's filters, and the 413 body is the canonical one (§6.4.2, ADR-39; H4 and H8 tightened) `[NEST-r1-04]`.
    - `onAPIError.throw` is honored (ADR-50; H13 added) `[BA-r1-09]`.
    - Platforms report proxy trust; B27 and `W_PROXY_UNTRUSTED` make the two silent misconfigurations visible (§6.8; H12 added) `[SEC-r1-06]`.
    - A production boot without a `baseURL` fails: B23 (ADR-46) `[SEC-r1-07]`.
    - Unknown paths under the mount get a "did you mean" log line outside production (ADR-52) `[SEC-r1-16]`.
    - `betterAuthCorsOrigin` uses the post-init trusted set and exact origins by default (§6.9, ADR-33) `[BA-r1-11, SEC-r1-17]`.
  - **Surfaces the guard cannot reach fail boot** (ADR-40): every gateway on every Nest major, with the version probe removed `[NEST-r1-13, SEC-r1-12]`; hybrid-RPC handlers without `inheritAppConfig` `[NEST-r1-05, SEC-r1-09]`; GraphQL field resolvers that carry requirements `[NEST-r1-06, SEC-r1-10]`.
  - **Open-closed.**
    - Core names no extension: `definePrincipalParam`, `defineInvocationParam`, a generic `NO_TRANSPORT`, and `advise()` on every contract (B21). The session unit and `httpTransport()` moved to `src/extensions/**` (ADR-41) `[NEST-r1-07]`.
    - Platforms and transports are declared once, on the default instance (B25), and `ExtensionDefinition.exports` provides `WsConnectionAuth` under `WS_CONNECTION_AUTH` (ADR-45) `[NEST-r1-09, NEST-r1-12]`.
    - Named instances must not share cookie names: B24 (ADR-47) `[SEC-r1-11]`.
  - **Hooks and types** (§10, §11, ADR-49). Database hooks are mirrored per operation, with types derived from `BetterAuthOptions['databaseHooks']`; throwing matchers propagate `[BA-r1-06]`. The claim about what before-hooks can see was corrected and the banned-user example replaced `[BA-r1-07]`. Hook bodies are `UnvalidatedBody` `[BA-r1-08]`.
  - **Errors and logging** (§13, ADR-43). Infrastructure errors carry a redacted cause, with the raw one behind `errors.exposeRawCause` `[SEC-r1-08]`. Request-time internal errors are generic on GraphQL (`toInternalException`, `BetterAuthGraphqlInternalError`), and request-time configuration errors are generic as thrown (`BetterAuthConfigurationError.atRequest`), which covers the param decorators that throw where the guard did not run (§7.8, LEAD-EXP-7) `[SEC-r1-19]`.
  - **Testing** (§14, ADR-51). `overrideAuthGuard` covers both guard registrations and `stampPrincipal()` is public; both publish through a test stamp that the scope interceptors copy into the scope, so replaced guards work on WebSocket gateways too (§7.8, LEAD-V34) `[NEST-r1-08]`. `initTestApp` closes the previous test app, and a binding whose app never bootstrapped is taken over: B06, ADR-25 `[SEC-r1-15]`. New conformance cases: `T-invocation-decisions`, `T-acceptance`, `T-csrf-*`, `T-ws-origin-untrusted`, `T-subscription-origin`, `T-internal-error-generic`, `S-apikey-*`, `S-bridge-*`, `S-log-redaction`, `S-delegation`, `Z-delegation-*`, `Z-admin-*`, `Z-per-invocation`, `Z-apikey-quota-per-request`, `H-async-options-factory`, `H-no-adapter`, `H-errors-apierror-throw`, `H-limit-canonical-body`, `H-proxy-trust`, `H-diagnostics-404`, and the repository tests `LIB-hook-bearer-client`, `LIB-cors-helper`, `LIB-testing-override-principal` and `LIB-testing-stamp-mock-guard` (§14.5, §14.8). The matrix gained the 11.2.x line, the adapter-less bootstraps, and the hybrid-RPC and GraphQL coverage jobs.
  - **Naming.** `@Session()` became `@CurrentSession()` (ADR-24) `[NEST-r1-10]`.
  - **Boot checks.** B04, B06, B08, B14, B15, B16, B19, B21 and B22 changed; B23 to B28 are new (§5.4).
  - **Migration guide** (§15). Five new checklist steps (proxy trust, `baseURL`, API-key routes, direct-call cookies, server-side callers that forward cookies), and the behavior changes that follow from the items above.
  - **Packaging** (§12). The plugin's allowed imports are `better-auth/api`, `better-auth/cookies` and `defu`, with Web Crypto and no `node:*`. §12.4 lists the better-auth specifiers the package imports, checked at the 1.7.0 floor, and the Nest-owned identifiers, with no deep imports and no version probing. §12.5 states where every piece of per-application state lives and adds `Symbol.for` brands for the library's own error classes. §12.9 lines up with §14 (identifier pins per Nest major, the adapter-less tarball fixture, consumer types across better-auth versions and with or without `./api-key`).
  - **Decision log and questions.** ADR-34 to ADR-53 added, and 30 ADRs revised with the findings that forced each change. Q13 to Q17 record the reviewers' proposed user decisions; Q18 to Q20 record three more that the lead decided. RK18 to RK26 added; RK13, RK14 and RK15 re-rated; RK9 and RK11 rewritten; RK1, RK3, RK5 and RK10 extended with the v2 surfaces. Q2, Q4, Q6, Q8 and Q12 updated for the v2 defaults. Q1, Q8, Q9, Q11 and RK4 write the first release as `1.0`, so `v1` only ever names design v1.
  - **Verification.** LEAD-V16 to LEAD-V35 (source re-checks) and LEAD-EXP-2 to LEAD-EXP-7 (LEAD-V34, LEAD-V35 and LEAD-EXP-7 come from closing the gaps a post-revision audit found). The reviewers' experiments were re-run where they decided an action. Two facts surfaced while finishing the revision:
    - better-auth's own origin rule gained the `Origin: null` + `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` inference only in 1.7.2, so the mirrored rule already differs from the router at the D4 floor (LEAD-V33, RK20; the origin test became a differential one, §14.5);
    - scrubbing an error's message in place is not enough, because Drizzle keeps the query parameters in an enumerable property (LEAD-EXP-6).
  - **Consistency fixes of the finishing pass.** `normalizeThrown` passes the library's own, already classified errors through (§13.2), which §7.3 and §8.3.1 relied on. Once-per-process wording became once-per-application, because the library keeps no module-level state (§12.5). Draft-internal ids in §16 are written `B-Qn`, so they cannot be mistaken for this document's ids.
- **v1.0** (2026-09-11), lead architect. First merged design, built from drafts A ("better-auth-native"), B ("ports and adapters") and C ("DX and types first").
  - **Adopted from A:**
    - Fastify encapsulated `parseAs: 'buffer'` parser with native 413;
    - the `ExtensionDefinition` registration helper;
    - scope interceptor plus explicit internal scopes;
    - the carrier stamp;
    - `defu`-based dispatcher parity;
    - `getActiveMemberRole` membership proof;
    - the separate plugin build;
    - named instances via `AuthOf<N>`;
    - the Hono two-phase sketch.
  - **Adopted from B:**
    - ports-and-adapters layering with the architecture fitness tests;
    - the `PrincipalResult` union ("denials are values");
    - invariant tables mapped to conformance ids;
    - policies resolved by reference through `ModuleRef`;
    - deferred-413 Express drain;
    - exclusive binding;
    - the `withUpgradeRequest`-style mixin;
    - `WsConnectionAuth`;
    - the experiment log E1–E11.
  - **Adopted from C:**
    - the type layer (`DefaultInstanceCheck`, the required `customSession` mapper, `BetterAuthFactoryResult`, `EndpointPath`, typed hook contexts, permission types becoming `never` without the plugin);
    - aggregated boot diagnostics with "did you mean";
    - no hook class marker, and `'model.op'` DB hook targets;
    - `defaultAccess`;
    - the plan compilation rules and `readsSession`;
    - a two-level `code`/`reason` error payload;
    - authoritative reads as a plan attribute;
    - unbinding in `onApplicationShutdown`;
    - the Nest-major capability probe for gateway coverage.
  - **Lead changes [L]:**
    - GraphQL denials as an `IntrinsicException` subclass (LEAD-EXP-1 showed B's approach loses the 429 code under Apollo and A/C's approach logs every denial);
    - param decorators read the interceptor scope first, because WS param factories cannot see the per-message key and the socket races (LEAD-V7);
    - the platform-scope rationale was corrected, since body-parser preserves ALS (LEAD-V11);
    - the Express/Fastify accessor gained `responseFor` for Apollo on Fastify (LEAD-V8);
    - `orgMember()` corrected to `getActiveMemberRole` semantics (403 `YOU_ARE_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THIS_ORGANIZATION`);
    - LEAD-V1–V15 source verifications.
  - **Resolved contradictions:**
    - plugin mandatory (A, C) vs optional (B) → mandatory;
    - module name `AuthModule` (C) vs `BetterAuthModule` (A, B) → `BetterAuthModule`;
    - platform auto-detection (C) vs explicit (A, B) → explicit;
    - hooks including internal calls (A, C) vs excluding them (B) → including;
    - WS default revalidation per message (A, C) vs 300 s (B) → per message;
    - policy registry by kind (A) vs by reference (B, C) → by reference;
    - multi-app hook routing (A) vs exclusive binding (B, C) → exclusive;
    - one instance (B) vs named instances (A, C) → named;
    - method-level `@Public` fail-closed (A) vs opt-out (C) → opt-out, with Q3;
    - GraphQL error type (A/B/C) → `IntrinsicException` subclass.
